Finally, he went to Fenglong Mountain to seek out the chamber of Guyan, who deeply esteemed him. Upon his arrival...
In the second year of the Taizhi era, he opened the hall at Tianqing. Subsequently, he moved to Tongxiang on Mount Xiong’er, Lingyan on Mount Tai, and Songshao in Luoyang.
A monk asked, "Does the 'merit of no-merit' have its own deviations and correctness? The Master replied, "Deviations and correctness are clearly evident."
[The student] asked: "What is the fundamental deviation and correctness of the groundless? The Master said: "The stone ox spits forth the mist of the three springs;
the numinous bird does not perch in the shadowless forest. [The student] asked: "What is the direct pointing to the human mind? The Master said: "The tongue is inside the mouth. [The student] asked:
"What is seeing one's nature and attaining Buddhahood? The Master said: "Though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a speck of dust. [The student] asked: "How is this so?"
"Do not take the standard from these words. The Master said, "The fire of the Way has never once burned my mouth.
[A monk] asked, "What is the principle of clarifying the source beyond the phrase? The Master struck him. [The monk] asked, "Why did you strike me?
The Master said, "Do you want me to clarify the source within the phrase? In the summer of the Gengchen year, he fell ill. He then addressed his disciples, saying, "This illness cannot be cured."

"I shall certainly depart. On the eleventh day of the fifth month, he attended to his final affairs and wrote this verse: "When coming, it was originally still; when departing, it is perfectly complete.
The void performs a dance, wandering freely as it pleases. He then passed away lying on his right side.

Chan Master Songting Ziyuan of Wan’an Temple in Nanyang Prefecture, a dharma successor of Chan Master Shaoshi Cai of the twenty-seventh generation under Qingyuan; he was from Gu Goushi County in Henan. Fan...
As for his surname: he suffered from many illnesses in his youth. Out of pity for him, his parents permitted him to follow the Śākya teachings.

He paid his respects at Shaolin to Qiyun. At eighteen, he received full ordination. The Master was exceptionally intelligent and surpassed others; he was extensively versed in both Buddhist and secular classics.

Regarding poetry and prose, he was capable without formal study, composing works instantly upon taking up the brush. Great masters and eminent scholars all expected him to become a vessel of the Dharma. Initially, he visited Jiang...
Yuezhao next visited Xixian Rang, from whom he received instructions on the essentials of Chan that awakened him. Later, he visited Chan Master Chunzhuo.
Zhuo examined and debated with him using the *Treasure Mirror Samādhi* (*Baoming Sanmei*), which completely cleared away his doubts and obstructions.

Zhuo said, "The responsibility for carrying the Great Dharma rests entirely upon your shoulders," and subsequently transmitted to him the robe and the Dharma. He was one of those known as "the lion cubs at the peak of Wuyufeng," who outshone their predecessors.
These lines, "Shining afterward, he naturally transcends the multitude," were written at a time when the Wan'an Monastery in Nanyang was vacant; the Master was invited to preside over it.
In the second year of the Hongwu era, the Jihyou year (1369), he took charge of Shaolin. To provide for the community through farming, he composed this verse:

"Returning after the chaos, I cultivate my own field; My life's toil and hardship, with whom can I discuss it? By day, I pick up clods of earth to drive away mountain birds; By night, I sit within my nest-like hut."
Chasing wild boars through the fields; my bowels are severed by the autumn winds as I frequently strike the wooden clappers. My eyes gaze upon the night moon as my soul fades away in darkness.
Only recently have I come to recognize the bitterness of the farmer’s toil; for even a single meal, I still think of the benefactor’s kindness.

A monk asked, "Dizang said, 'Planting rice to earn one's meal. Is this the same as, or different from, the Master? The Master said, "Though we lean against the same railing, we view the mountain colors differently. The monk said, "A hundred..."
Zhang Kai-tian said, "To explain the meaning, one simply extends both hands. [The questioner asked,] "What is the underlying intent?

The Master said, "Although there are no words, their sound is like thunder. [The questioner asked,] "And what about you, Master? The Master said, "By day I pick up clods of earth to drive away mountain birds; by night I sit in my hut to chase off wild pigs.
[The questioner] asked, "Yantou went to study under Dongshan but was not accepted. Dongshan, however, was a successor of Deshan—[how is this so?]"
“‘Ken’ (Yes). What excellence do Deshan and Yantou possess? The Master said, “If you acknowledge those two masters, then you betray them.
[The monk] asked, “He said that Dongshan, an ancient Buddha, was simply ‘without light. What does this mean? The Master said, “He indeed has light;
he is not an ancient Buddha. [The monk] asked, “When the Master ascends the seat, why does the Qin-feng locust tree not come to listen to the Dharma?”
The Master said, "Doubts have long since been severed; what need is there to see another?

In the winter of the thirteenth year, His Highness Prince Zhou respectfully commissioned the Master to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma for the sake of the posthumous merit of Empress Dowager Cixiao, the Mother of the State.
The Emperor bestowed upon him a *saṃghāṭī* robe to mark his extraordinary merit. Later, he retired to live in seclusion; the details of his passing are unknown.

He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Linggu Quan. (In the Ancestral Lineage Chart, the entry identifying this master as a successor of Qingyuan Wei is incorrect; it appears to have mistakenly conflated Baoguo Quan with Linggu Quan.)
Chan Master Zhengying of Jie’an at Linggu Monastery in Nanjing was the son of the Hong family of Jinxī in Fuzhou. In his youth, he entered Sanfeng Monastery in Anren as a śrāmaṇera.
In the nineteenth year of the Hongwu era, he passed the scriptural examinations and received full ordination. He visited Chan Master Xunzhong Qian of Linggu Monastery;
as soon as he stepped through the gate, the incense in his breast pocket suddenly fell to the ground, whereupon he attained realization. Qian appointed him to serve as the *karmadāna* (rector).
Upon the passing of Jian, he went to the celestial realm to visit Xue Xuan. Xuan appointed him as the Keeper of the Archives.

There was subsequently an imperial decree stating, "A monk from Kaiyuan Temple in Quanzhou shall be selected by lot to serve as the abbot. Accordingly, he was chosen by drawing lots. When he was brought for an audience, he was presented before the Emperor.
The Emperor said: "I appoint you to serve as abbot. It is difficult to be an abbot nowadays; if you are good, they will treat you with contempt, and if you are not, they will slander you.
Simply keep your mind pure and yourself clean, and you shall long enjoy the imperial favor. The Master received the decree and came to the monastery.

On the sixth month of the thirty-first year of the Hongwu era, he opened the Dharma hall. A monk asked: "The Dharma assembly has now commenced, and the fourfold assembly looks up to it with full respect. [What of] the Imperial Grace?"

"How can the Buddha's grace be universally repaid? The Master said, "The spring of ambrosia opens and flows across the great earth. [The student] said, "I have received your instruction on the single phrase for repaying grace;
how then shall the meaning of the Patriarchs' coming from the West be proclaimed? The Master said, "The stone pagoda before the courtyard towers into the cold void.
[The student] said, "Throughout the entire realm, it has never been hidden. The Master said, "What do you see? [The student] said, "I truly dare not deceive myself."
The Master said, "Do not let your eyes grow dim. Again, a monk asked, "What is the one phrase by which you, the Master, benefit others?
The Master said, "A rabbit-horn staff picks up the moon in the heavens; a tortoise-hair whisk scatters the clouds on the seashore.

The monk said, "If that is so, then dragons and devas shall all rejoice, and both monastics and laypeople shall turn toward benevolence. The Master said, "Now, shut your mouth! The monk bowed, and the Master then said:

This mountain monk has been graced by imperial favor to reside at this monastery. I personally received the Emperor’s earnest instructions, entrusting me with the four characters “Clear Mind and Pure Self.
These are the seal of the Buddha’s mind transmitted to me; they are also a bright pearl that anchors the sea.

Having already received them upon my head and traveled southward, I shall now bestow them universally upon the great assembly. You, members of the assembly, must understand: as for worldly dharmas and Buddhist dharmas, they are like the setting clouds and—
"Solitary wild ducks fly together; ancient Buddhas and present Buddhas. The autumn waters share the same hue as the vast sky; the mind of Heaven is unfathomable.

The mountains grow ever higher and the seas ever deeper; the words of the Sages are inexhaustible. Heaven covers all and Earth supports all. Great Assembly, how do you understand this intention of the Sages?
Is it that they are unstained by worldly dust? Is it that they do not crave the flavor of the Dharma?"
"Is it not that you do not drink the wine of non-action and do not sit upon the bed of Nirvana?
If you understand it in this way, it is not that it is not so, but it is not yet correct. Today, I dare not keep this secret any longer; I cannot help but point it out from the high seat.
A wooden man dances out before the Dharma Hall, freely letting white snow fly in the blazing heat of summer. The Master resided there for several years.

He abandoned the practice of cultivating both [meditation and study]. In the first year of the Yongle era, upon his return from the imperial court in the capital, the monastic communities of the various mountains in Fuzhou nominated him to reside at Xuefeng.

The buildings at Xuefeng were so dilapidated and decrepit that they were no longer fit for use; the Master renovated them all at once. Everyone considered this to be a fulfillment of the prophecy regarding the "return of the former Xuefeng.
In the first year of the Hongxi era, he received an imperial decree to serve as abbot of Linggu Monastery. In the first year of the Xuande era...

In his later years, he was promoted to the post of Left Lecturer at the Sengluosi (Bureau of Monastic Records). He passed away at Linggu Temple. His recorded sayings, entitled *The Samādhi of the Ancient Mirror*, circulate in the world.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Tianqing Rang.
Chan Master Ding of Songxi at Xiongeri Mountain in Shan Prefecture was the son of the Ma family of Yan County. At the age of seven, he paid his respects to Guruan and received the tonsure.

When Guruan passed away, he went to study under Xianan, who appointed him as the librarian. While discussing matters with him, he attained a sudden and great enlightenment upon hearing the master’s words.
He subsequently emerged from seclusion at Xiongeri Mountain. In a small-scale assembly (xiaochan), he said: "The matter within the Gate of the School is known as the Single Transmission."

Apart from the single mind, there are no other dharmas. It is simply because the sentient beings of this land delight in clinging to words and phrases, and are content to be buried alive within intellectual principles, that they become increasingly bewildered and confused regarding the dharma of the single mind.
Therefore, the First Patriarch came from the West to shatter the old nests and open up a different kind of world; it was not for the sake of seeking novelty.
It is different. It is merely seeing the illness and the medicine, not yet having attained it.

For example, when the First Patriarch first arrived at Shaolin, he kept his mouth sealed for nine years and sat facing the wall, cutting off all branches and leaves, holding up alone the "uppermost nostril.
No matter how you spy upon it, there is no door; no matter how you probe and study it, you cannot enter. Here, one cannot understand through words, nor can one understand through silence.
Regarding "meeting" (hui): it cannot be communicated within the realm of conceptual opposition, nor can it be communicated beyond the realm of conceptual opposition.

One must directly forget emotions and obliterate views before one can attain its heart-essence. Once the heart-essence is attained, the Dharma-seals of all Buddhas and the life-lineage of the successive patriarchs do not transcend this.
By pressing a single finger, earth turns and heaven revolves; by issuing a single command, mountains crumble.
The ocean has dried up. Furthermore, what use is it to carve out space from the void to skillfully establish a school, following the waves and chasing the currents to produce further complications?
Today, many Zen practitioners do not know how to attend to the root; they merely seek branches and pluck leaves to pass their days.
One does not know what use such things are. Dongshan’s "jade thread and golden needle" is much like playing with shadows before the flowers. Linji—
"The Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials are nothing other than adding wine to one's cup after a meal. Can you all see through this? After a long silence, he said:
'The night is still and the water is cold; the fish do not eat. The boat returns empty, carrying only the bright moon. One day, manifesting illness, he said to his disciples:
"My worldly ties have come to an end, and the time for my peaceful passing has arrived. Listen as I deliver the final phrase."
[Postscript]. He then entered nirvana in silence.
This is the lineage of Chan Master Wanan Yan, the twenty-eighth generation descendant of Qingyuan.
Chan Master Liaogui of Shaoshi on Mount Song was born into a flourishing clan in Jindian, Yangqiu, Mount Song.

From his childhood, he fixed his mind upon the school of emptiness and realized there was a matter pertaining to his own person. He subsequently took refuge at Shaolin, receiving the monastic robes at the age of twenty.
Initially, he visited Yueyin at Xiangshan; though he passed through many seasons of cold and heat, he was unable to achieve realization.

Chan Master Huìsōng was residing at Tiānqìng, and the Master went there to rely upon him. He consulted with the master on his own spiritual matter every day. One day, as Huìsōng ascended the hall for a formal discourse, he said:
"A single word that transcends all bounds stands alone, surpassing its time. At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved and at ease. He recounted this realization to Huìsōng.
Tingyin [received the seal] and retired to the Second Patriarch’s Hermitage. In the twenty-third year of the Hongwu era, he was invited to preside over Shaoshi.
He ascended the hall and said: "The Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs is neither speech nor silence; it is neither knowledge nor ignorance."
How could one possibly investigate this beneath words and phrases, or speculate within the consciousness?
When the Patriarch first arrived in the past, he brought with him ancient, stagnant wares that no one would accept; thus, he had no choice but to face the wall for nine years.

Later, the Second Patriarch was like a foolish monkey trying to catch the moon as he came to ask for peace of mind. This old fellow was simply moved by parental affection and failed to notice his own awkwardness.
He said to him, "Bring forth your mind, and I will settle it for you. The Second Patriarch then accepted this empty echo and called it "attaining the marrow.
Looking at it, he too deserves thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because as soon as the lips move, ten thousand mountains intervene. Do you all understand?
*Pah!* If I, this mountain monk, speak thus today, I too deserve thirty blows of the staff. — Yongle.
He remained free from ailment for nineteen years. Suddenly, he summoned his assembly to bid them farewell, spoke a verse, and passed away.
He was the Dharma successor of Chan Master Shaoshi Gaizhi, the twenty-ninth generation descendant of Qingyuan.
Chan Master Qike Bin of Shaoshi on Mount Song was a native of Tanqu in Pingyang. He visited Nengran to seek instruction on the essentials of the mind, consulting him morning and evening.
One day, upon seeing a *qinfeng* (Qin-seal) locust tree, he attained sudden and profound enlightenment. He immediately returned to attend upon his master.
When Rannan saw him for the first time, he said, "Qibin has attained Zen. The Master then gave a shout. Rannan asked, "What was that shout for?
The Master replied, "How can you, Reverend, frame someone with false evidence? Rannan asked, "When Zhaozhou exposed the old woman, where exactly did her failure lie?
The Master said, "A pair of iron hammers without holes. Rannan asked, "What is Zhaozhou?"
Yuanran said, "In a forest of thorns, you have further added a pitfall. Dongshan said, "The letter from Shitou neither reached him nor was it delivered;
what is the meaning of this? Dongshan said, "A thousand miles away, the same wind blows. Yuanran said, "What about Qingyuan’s hanging down his feet?
Dongshan said, "A calamity! A calamity! Yuanran said, "The secret lineage of the Dongshan school rests upon your person."
In the fourth year of the Jingtai era, he presided over the Small Room (Shao-shi). A monk asked, "What is the matter prior to the empty kalpa? The Master said, "A tortoise warming itself by the fire.
The monk asked, "What is 'the biased within the central' (zheng-zhong-pian)? The Master said, "At midnight, a black hen sleeps amidst the snow.
The monk asked, "What is 'the central within the biased' (pian-zhong-zheng)? The Master said, "An old man cradling a stone tortoise. The monk asked, "What is 'the central' (zheng)?"... [text ends]

[The monk] came forward. The Master said, “A blade drawn from its scabbard—its coldness presses upon the heavens. [The monk] asked, “What is ‘reaching within the intermediate’? The Master said, “Gongsun’s sword dance is inconceivable.
[The monk] asked, “What is ‘arriving within the intermediate’? The Master said, “A black dog with silver hooves—nowhere to be found.
[The monk] asked, “Since you have already granted me the instruction on the five ranks, what is the matter of the Direct Pointing of Shaolin? The Master said:
There is no oil in sand; there is flour in wheat.
*Jìdēnglù*, Scroll One; *Jìdēnglù*, Scroll Two.
Compiled by the Drum Mountain lineage-holding śramaṇa Yuánxián,
of the Eighteenth Generation under Nanyuè in the Linjì School.

Chan Master Wuming Haoweng of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Yong of Gushan; he was a native of Fuzhou. Once, while presiding over an assembly, he raised this case:

A monk from under the guidance of Chan Master Jia Shan went to Gaoting. As soon as the monk prostrated himself, Gaoting struck him. The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects; why do you strike me?"

Gao Ting struck him. The monk bowed again, and Ting struck him once more and drove him away. The monk returned and related this to Jia Shan. Jia Shan asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
Jia Shan said, "It is fortunate that you do not understand. Had you understood, Jia Shan’s mouth would have been closed.
Ying’an commented: "For a time, Gao Ting could not restrain his impatience; yet, alas, he let go with his staff far too quickly. As for this monk..."
At that time, had he been a true man, let alone Gao Ting and Jia Shan—even if Master Bodhidharma himself had come forth, he would have cut him into three pieces.
Why? Because "when the family prospers, filial sons arise; when the state is hegemonic, there are strategic ministers. The Master said:
"The pedagogical arrangements of Gao Ting and Jia Shan each attained their proper measure, yet one of them was slightly inferior. Ying...

Anan said, "To speak in such a way is like a tea pitcher from Gongxian. This master compiled the *Lian Deng Hui Yao* (Essentials of the Linked Lamps) for transmission within the monastic community. He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Lingyin Shan;

[his name] appears in the *Huiyuan* (though it does not appear in the *Zongmen Tongyao Ji*, it is now included here to supplement the Lamp Records). He was a successor of Yuyang Guang. (The *Huiyuan* contains no record of his origin; he is now included here to supplement the Lamp Records.)
Chan Master Cángsǒu Shànzhēn of Xùfēng in Fúzhōu was the son of the Lǚ family from Nán’ān, Quánzhōu.
He visited Miàofēng at Língyǐn, where he entered the inner chamber and realized the essential meaning. He emerged from seclusion at Guāngxìáo in his hometown, then ascended to Chéngtiān and Xùfēng.
Subsequently, by imperial decree, he was appointed as the abbot of Yùwáng and later Jìngshān. He ascended the hall and said: "The entire great earth is the purple-golden body. All...
All day long people open their eyes and gaze upon the very heart and liver of Śākyamuni; every step they take strikes against the nostrils of Śākyamuni.
To speak of existence or non-existence is deception; to speak of arising or ceasing is slander; to speak of "mind itself" or "not mind" is delusion.
Without deception, without slander, and without delusion—when the spring breeze blows down the peach and plum blossoms, and the thin mist and sparse rain envelop them...
Qingzhang once inscribed his own portrait, saying: "In the practice of Chan there is no awakening; my literacy is limited.

My eyes are triangular like those of a sorrowful foreigner from Mount Yan; my face is wrinkled like Zhao Po drinking vinegar. Standing out far above all others, I dare say that rice is made from grain.
At the New Year’s Eve small *can*, he cited a monk asking an ancient worthy: "When the year is exhausted and the age has ended, what then?"
De said, "As usual, it is still cold in the first month of spring. The Master said, "When ancient worthies answered in this way, they were only afraid that people would forget.
If someone were to ask me today, 'What is it like when the year ends and the age is exhausted? I would take up my staff and strike them immediately. When they asked, 'Why did you strike me?
I would simply tell them, 'I want you to say for yourself: it is still cold in the first month of spring.'"
That night, he ascended the hall and said: "Spring snow is cold; spring nights are short. The heart of the ancient Buddha is a broken oil lamp; the eye of the True Dharma is a wick made of dry paper.

Summon all your spirit and simply look! Look until the Big Dipper shifts west and the Southern Dipper turns east, and you will see that the Yuanxiao Festival remains the fifteenth day of the first month.
He passed away in the Dingchou year of the Jiading era.
Chan Master Youyun Zongjiao of Longji Monastery in Jixian Prefecture was a native of the Wang family of Luling. Initially, he relied upon Miaofeng.
One day, as Miaofeng ascended the hall, he held up his staff and said, "The Old Man Śākyamuni has arrived; do you all see him?
He then lowered the staff and said, "The subtle, wondrous, pure Dharma-body is endowed with the thirty-two marks. [Now] put down your staff! [He continued,] "You people..."

"I understand. I shall enter nirvana. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. Later, he ascended Mount Foding on Jishui and took up residence in an ancient temple belonging to the master Xiu.
There he lived on wild fruits and drank from mountain streams, sitting upright day and night.

Even when snow and cold left him without a fire for the night, he would pass the days eating only a few inches of sweet flag root. He once composed a verse in his own hand to console himself, which began: "The mountain monk has..."
Dwelling apart amidst mist and vines—no rice, no money, so let him be. The water is like lapis lazuli, the mountains like jade; before one’s eyes there is more than enough.
Miaofeng entrusted his Dharma robe, bamboo staff, and his own portrait to the Master. Miaofeng himself inscribed his portrait, saying:
"On the solitary peak of Miaofeng, the grass grows lush and wild; across my chest I rest a bamboo staff, three feet of iron. Only...
Xǔ Fǒngtǐng Lóngjì knows this: the true secret instructions were not transmitted from father to son.
The Master once wrote on his gate to show those who came to seek instruction, saying: "Setting aside the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind—what is that which is your own self?
If you can speak of it, I will allow you to personally see Lóngjì; if you cannot, then stay outside the gate. When Heshang Xuěyán saw this, he said: [He understood.]
He asked, "How many people have you ever guided? The Master replied, "I have never, from the beginning, been one to force an ox to eat grass.
A monk asked, "What will it be like when the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives? The Master replied, "There will be no debt-collectors at the gate.
Suddenly, manifesting illness, he gathered the assembly to entrust them with his final affairs. Then, snapping his fingers once, he said, "This alone is my parting from the assembly."
These were his words. An attendant monk requested that he leave behind a verse, but he did not answer. When midnight arrived, he suddenly asked for a brush and wrote:
"A single lamp is in sight; there is no further speech. The great earth sinks level, and empty space shatters. He then sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Dongsou Zhongying of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "Above all, do not seek by following others; there is no need to look for it within yourself.
Transcendent and lively, there is letting go and there is gathering in. What is this? A single leaf falls, and autumn comes to all under heaven.
He once composed a verse on Changqing’s words, "Everything is like today, yet Old Hu has expectations," which says: "The sky is high, and wild geese invade the clouds."

Verse: The earth is hushed as crickets and grasshoppers enter the weeds to sing; It is entirely within the landscape of autumn. How many times does the traveler’s sorrow follow the sentiments of a foreign land?

Chan Master Jian of Jingci, Successor of Chan Master Guanghui of Yuyang (Master Guanghui was the successor of Yuyang; his records were originally not extant. He is now included here to supplement the Lamp Records).
Chan Master Wuchu Daoguan of Yuyang in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Lu family of Ning County in Mingzhou. Initially, he relied upon Beijian at Nanping;
one day, during a session in the inner quarters, their words and meaning reached a point of perfect accord, whereupon he attained great enlightenment.

Later, he appeared in the world and successively presided over famous monasteries. In his later years, he took charge of Yuyang. He ascended the hall and said: "One winter, two winters—'you' and 'I,' 'you' and 'I. Dark..."
He chuckled inwardly. To his face, he spoke empty words. Though these are but ordinary fare, who knows there are worms within the rice?

Last night a fine wind blew, snapping a pine branch before the gate. Entering the hall, he said: "Using the 'black bean' method to change people's eyes has occurred as many times as the sands of the Ganges;
yet how many can truly understand the story of the hearth? Nine times nine is eighty-one. The Buddhas of the three periods..."
Ignorant of its existence, he turns his body and kicks over the five Sumeru mountains. Why employ the Dharma-body to hide the Northern Dipper?
To hide the Northern Dipper is to clearly flaunt one's family disgrace to the outside world. Entering the hall, [the Master] said: "The events of kalpas of dust are but this very moment.
If you hesitate when it must be severed, the constellations will shift. He took up his staff, struck once, and said: "The flowers must bloom through the night; do not wait for the dawn."
The wind blew. He ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case where Layman Pang asked Great Master Ma, 'What kind of person is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion?
The Master replied, 'Wait until you can suck up all the water of the West River in a single mouth, and then I will tell you. The Master [Baizhang] said:"
The great and small patriarchs knew only that it was easy to open one's mouth; they did not realize their tongues were so long. Had he been asked by Yuyang at that time, he would have simply said:
"If you want me to speak for you, wait until empty space falls to the ground; then naturally you will be surpassed. Why?
Because a carriage cannot be pushed sideways, and there is no such thing as a crooked judgment. [Ascending the hall: "The orthodox lineage of Bodhidharma is the very nose of the monk. Filled with...

It fills all of empty space, leaving no place to turn or avoid. How laughable are those who wander in delusion! Under the bright sun and clear sky, they keep their eyes wide open yet remain nothing but dozing.
Furthermore, there is that "Old Man with the Yellow Face" who fails to distinguish good from evil;

he plunges into the mud and the water, yet says, "At the place of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I did not obtain a single dharma for which I was granted a prediction. How is this any different from gouging a sore into healthy flesh?
Seeking the calyx of a flower in the sky—how can this ultimately be? *Siri siri*. Since he conformed to worldly ways, his stupa was enshrined in a western hermitage of the monastery.

(This master was a successor of Chan Master Yan of Jingshan; [his name] appears in the *Yuanwu* [of the *Jingde chuandeng lu*], though no record of his lineage has emerged. He is now included here to supplement the Lamp Records.)
Chan Master Yankxi Guangwen of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an was a native of the Lin family of Houguan in Fuzhou.

Initially, he visited Zhe’ung, but his affinity was as difficult to find as a needle meeting its eye. He subsequently traveled extensively to consult various masters. Later, when he visited Zhe’ung again at Mount Jing, the Master greeted him with a smile, saying, “Have you come?
One night, while sitting under the eaves, he heard the watchman strike the gong three times; he entered the room dragging his sandals.

He was startled as if waking from a dream. The following morning, he went to the abbot’s quarters. When the elder raised the story of Zhaozhou washing his alms bowl, the Master was about to open his mouth when the elder suddenly stopped him;
all the doubts and obstructions of his life were instantly dissolved like melting ice. In the Wuzi year of the Shaoding era, he took up the abbacy at Xiao Jingci.
Having resided successively at Xiangshan, Wanshou, Xuedou, Yuyang, Jingci, Lingyin, and Jingshan, he ascended the hall and raised the following case:
Zhaozhou addressed the assembly, saying, "Thirty years ago, when I was in the south, by the hearth, there was a 'no host-guest' koan.
To this very day, no one has brought it up. The Master commented: "The myriad phenomena of the forest and the mountains, brightness and darkness, form and color..."
"Emptiness! Emptiness! he proclaimed day and night. The ancient Buddha Zhaozhou was not unaware; it was simply that his progress was too hurried. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said:
"Yunmen giving Dongshan three blows of the staff—feeding a baby with chewed food. Huangbo giving Linji three blows of the staff—forcing an ox's head down as it eats grass.
Right now, without violating even a single hair’s breadth, there is a skillful means. After a long silence, he said:
The great matter cannot be obtained for you; the small matters you must take up yourself. Entering the hall: At the stone pillar in the crossroads, there is no place for you to shield yourself;
when the cry sounds that the Minister is coming upon the river, there is no place for you to evade.

For you who are practitioners of the patched robe, going out in the morning and returning in the evening, with one foot before and the other behind, you must also be careful. Suddenly, if you strike it or bump into it, [it is] pure.
The staff of compassion has a separate entrustment. [He] ascends the hall, circumambulates the meditation seat once, and strikes the incense table once.
Once the turning of the canon is finished, and once the preaching of the sutra is finished, only those who possess the eye of reading the scriptures will know where it lands.

If this is not yet the case, interpreting the meaning according to the scriptures is an enemy to the Buddhas of the three periods; deviating from the scripture by even a single word is the same as the teaching of a demon. [He] ascends the hall. Zhao—
"The provincial governor drinks tea and goes; the Ox Head eats his meal and comes. The Dragon Gate has many honored guests.

If there is anyone who can provide the final phrase, I shall permit you to enter the Dharma-gate of the letter 'A'. On the fourteenth day of the sixth month in the fourth year of the Jingding era, he passed away.
He was seventy-five years of age and fifty-eight years since his ordination.
Chan Master Dali Putong Zongji of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Fenghua, Mingzhou. He inscribed the following on a portrait of the World-Honored One leaving the palace:
"Dragon-marked and phoenix-tempered, he departs the royal palace; Sleeves bared and robes tattered, he emerges from the Snowy Peak.

His wisdom-vow must surely empty all realms of existence; One knows not when these realms of existence will be emptied. The Master compiled and edited the *Wudeng Huiyuan* (Compendium of the Five Lamps) in twenty fascicles.
This scroll circulated in the world.
Chan Master Yuanzhao of Huaihai from Jing Mountain in Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Pan family of Tongzhou, Yang. He attended upon Zhe’ung.
Zhe’ung asked, “Where are you from? The Master replied, “A person of Huai. Zhe’ung said, “Why is the Great Sage of Sizhou in Yang?”
The Master said, "Today you have encountered me again here in Hangzhou. The old man replied, "For now, there is no connection between us.

The Master said, "I have come from afar to seek your teaching wind. Desiring to greatly stimulate the Master’s alertness and quick wit, the old man did not allow him to enter the hall for formal study;
as soon as he saw him, he said, "Give me a turning phrase. As the Master prepared to open his mouth, the old man immediately shouted. The Master then presented a verse, at the end of which—
There was a verse that said: "The teaching of emptiness turns one’s head to gaze back at Chang’an. The Old Master asked, "What place is this?

The Master replied, "I thank the Abbot for granting me lodging. Only then did he join the ranks of those who enter the inner chamber. Subsequently, he was appointed to oversee the records. After the Old Master passed away...
The Master entered the world at Tongguang Temple in Xiaoxiao. Subsequently, he successively presided over Shuangta, Qingliang, Wanshou, Wannian, and Jiangxin.
By imperial decree, he was transferred to Jingci, Lingyin, and finally Jingshan in Hangzhou. During his tenure at Jingshan, unpaid debts had accumulated like a mountain.

The Sanghārāma was old and dilapidated, but before long, its multi-storied pavilions rose high toward the heavens. Monks in cloud-like robes arrived one after another, such that the assembly did not fall short of the peak prosperity during the time of Master Zhe.
He once composed a verse on Bodhidharma crossing the river: "He trampled over the earth’s axis and the celestial gate;

The people of the entire nation followed, yet he would not return. Gone, gone—his single body as light as a leaf; For a thousand ages, the waves of the Long River remain like mountains. The tenth day of the sixth month.
He wrote this verse and passed away.
Chan Master Píng of Jiéshí at Shuanglín in Wǔzhōu once saw a portrait of the Mountain Master Yù; a monk nearby requested a eulogy for it, and the Master wrote with his hand:
"Having picked up the pearl of the black dragon, his smiling eyes open; To say that the dust has vanished only to give rise to more ash. If... [text continues]
To those who do not directly take up [this truth], you have failed the Master with this single blow.

He once composed a verse regarding Mingzhao Qian, who on a day when the weather was cold, said while ascending the hall: "The wind is somewhat stiff; it is not a place for you to settle your body or establish your life.
[The Master] said: "The stiff windhead has long since gone astray; yet you further bury yourself in warmth. This causes a thousand ages to become mere traces—what a waste!"
He brought white rice from Mount Kirā.
Zen Master Dongshan Yuan composed a verse on Master Xiandao He, saying: "Pitiful creature amidst piles of paper money; As soon as that foul mouth opens, it is a tangle of vines.
Having swept away the poor livelihoods of the ghostly household, To this day, no one travels to the ancient temple. Furthermore:
At Yexian, the Master abridged the story of the "Pine Tree" for the monks, saying: "Drops dripping from the eaves, clear and distinct;
the blue-eyed one and the yellow-headed one—neither recognizes them. Whether recognized or not, the whole world is in utter disorder."
Chan Master Bianshan Qian’s verse on the occasion of Li Ao’s visit to Yaoshan says: "Valuing the ear while despising the eye, he draws a golden arrow behind his back;
Looking up at the azure sky, the arrow has already passed beyond the kingdom of Silla."
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Rui of Yuyang (the master’s succession from Yuyang Guang has no recorded lineage; he is now included here to supplement the Lamp Records).
Chan Master Wuliang Chongshou of Ruiyan in Qingyuan Prefecture was asked by a monk: "When the World-Honored One beheld the morning star and attained enlightenment, what was the meaning of this?
The Master replied with a verse: "The moment the morning star was seen, his eyelids were pierced through. Han speech and Hu speech..."
"Ten thousand, ten thousand, ten thousand! You beggar who became rich overnight, stop talking in your sleep. In whose hearth is there fire without smoke?
Chan Master Gudang Zu Jian of Gushan, a successor of Chan Master Qianyinying, was the son of the Xu family from Huian. He paid his respects to Chan Master Zhen of Zhongshan in Jiankang.
The Master underwent tonsure and ordination, then went to rely upon Chan Master Xiatang Yuan, serving him diligently for five years.

Upon returning to Min, he visited Chan Master Qianyuan Ying at Gandhola Monastery, where he finally brought his great matter to completion. He emerged from seclusion at Langya in Chuzhou; not long after, he moved to Beishan in Zhenzhou, and subsequently presided over Zifusi.
The Provincial Governor of Quan, Lord Cheng, invited him to serve at Chengtian Monastery, and he later transferred to Guangxiaosi. In the Jihai year of the Qingyuan era...

He had previously served under Lord Ye of the Shuai-fu for seven years at Gushan. In the year of Kāixī (1205), he retired from his duties. In the fifth month of the following year, he manifested illness.
When his attendant requested a verse for the occasion of his passing, the Master spoke this verse: "Throughout my life I have suffered from too much talk;

what more need I say at the moment of death? To show it fully to others: a single flake of snow upon a red furnace. Thereupon he passed away. His stupa was erected on the western side of the mountain.
[Enter/Rice/Field]. (The Master’s name was Zu Jian; the *Xu chuan deng lu* erroneously records it as Zong Jian.
Chan Master Po’an Zu’an of Wolong Mountain in Kuizhou, a successor of Chan Master Tiantong Jie, was the son of the Wang family from Guang’an Prefecture. Initially, he studied under Mi...
Upon hearing the words of the discourse from the high seat, Tiantong An attained realization. Later, when An resided at Lingyin, he appointed the Master to share the seat.

A practitioner seeking further instruction asked, "What should one do when a monkey cannot be caught? The Master said, "Why bother to catch it? It is like wind blowing across water; ripples form naturally.
After taking up residence there, he ascended the hall and declared: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing."
Unable to restrain his laughter, he provides a way of liberation for everyone. He takes up his staff and strikes once, saying:
"The flowing water silently erodes the rocks by the stream; it is difficult to persuade people to eliminate their right and wrong."
Chan Master Songyuan Chongyue of Lingyin in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of the Wu family of Longquan in Chuzhou.
In his youth, he aspired to the supramundane Dharma and met Dahui at Mount Jing. When Dahui ascended the high seat, he praised Ying’an for being direct and swift in characterizing people.
Upon hearing this, the Master set out before dawn. Once he arrived, he consulted with him morning and evening.

When Ying’an cited the words, "The World-Honored One had secret words, which Kāśyapa did not conceal," the Master replied, "This leaves the Master at a loss. Ying’an let out a thunderous shout, and the Master attained realization.
Ying’an was greatly pleased and regarded him as a vessel for the Dharma. At the beginning of the Longxing era, the Master finally received full ordination; he then traveled to Min to see Muguan.

Dongshan Shouchu said, "The phrase 'having a word' and 'not having a word' is like a vine leaning against a tree. The Master said, "Torn asunder! Dongshan said, "Langya says, 'What a pile of rotten firewood!
What do you say? The Master said, "Adding a point to an arrowhead. They exchanged such responses several times.
Dongshan said, "My brother’s words cannot be surpassed by this old monk; yet, it is still not enough. In the future, when the fly-whisk handle is in your hands, you must act for others."

"No. "Testing people is not possible," [the student] said. The Master said, "To act as a teacher and enable an ordinary person of common ground to leap directly into the realm of the sages is indeed difficult.
But to test a person—striking them right before their face so that one knows their very marrow even before they have opened their mouths—what difficulty is there in that?
The Hermit raised his hand and said, "Clearly I told you: 'Opening the mouth is not a matter of the tongue.'"
[The Master] said, "Later you shall know for yourself. A year later, he met Mian at Xishan; whatever was asked, Mian would simply answer with a smile.
The Master was so intent on reaching ultimate realization that he forgot both sleep and food.

Eventually, while Mian was in his room questioning a monk about the phrase, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing," the Master stood by his side and attained a sudden, great awakening. He then said, "Today..."
At that time, he realized that Master Mudan’s Way lay not upon the tongue. From then on, his skillful discernment became free and unrestrained.
He subsequently appeared in the world at Chengzhao in Pingjiang, and later moved to Guangxiao, Yeyu, Jianfu, Xiangshan, and Huqiu.

In the third year of the Qingyuan era, by imperial decree, he was appointed to Lingyin. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "In general, to uphold and establish the lineage of the school, one must possess the true eye atop the head."
Suspended from his elbow was the numinous talisman. It was just like when Baoshou opened the hall and Sansheng pushed forward a monk;
Baoshou struck him immediately. Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher in this manner is to blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters. These two venerable masters, through their casual jostling and pressing one another, suddenly gave rise to [the realization].
To clarify the heart-essence of Linji is simply to realize that life and nature are both entirely in the hands of this monk. Is there anyone here who can discern this?
In years past, seeking fire, I obtained it with the smoke; today, carrying water, I return with the moon. To the assembly:
An ancient said, "When he picks it up, heaven turns and earth revolves; when he lets it go, the grass bows and the wind blows. —Yezhu.
It is not so. When you pick it up, heaven and earth turn pitch black; when you let it go, even shards and rubble emit light.

Suddenly, if there is one or half of a person who, in an instant, blinds their own crown-center, then the Dharma-lineage of Bodhidharma will not yet have fallen into desolation. [To the assembly: *Note: The character [翟*支] (zhì) is a variant for "blind" (mù).*
Citing the public case of Linji’s “weed-whisk” simile, Xuedou said, "Linji’s letting go was too precarious;
his gathering back was too swift. The Master took up his staff and said, "Linji acted according to the command, yet he did not realize he was betraying Huangbo.
Even though Xuedou carried this burden with all his might, he saw only one side. Now tell me, where does the crux of Jianfu lie?"
At one point, he threw down his staff and addressed the assembly. Citing Fenyang, he said: "Fenyang said, 'If you recognize this staff, your journey as a wandering monk is finished.
Although Fenyang was like opening one's mouth to show one's very guts, he could not avoid falling into the 'second head' [the secondary level].
Suddenly picking up the staff, he said: 'This one must not be called a staff; it is a lacquer bucket! This is the phrase he suspended in the meditation hall."
He said, "Is it the wind that moves? Is it the banner that moves? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. He said again, "It is not the wind that moves; it is not the banner that moves.
As the monk hesitated, the Master likewise struck him. He said again, "Why does a man of power fail to lift his foot?
He said again, "The opening of the mouth is not upon the tongue. He said again, "For what reason do clear-eyed monks [fail to see]?"
"Beating the nose out of him—there is a thief, but no stolen goods. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'one and the same substance'? The Master said, "Torn asunder.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'two and the same great matter'? The Master said, "To settle heaven and earth upon the tip of a single hair.

The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'three and all equally participating'? The Master said, "Frogs, earthworms, lame turtles, and blind tortoises. The monk asked, "What about... [the question was cut off].
[Question: "What are the four 'identical true wisdoms'? [Master: "One does not become two; two are not one. [Question:
"What are the five 'identical pervasive universals'? [Master: "To gather up the great earth, there is not a single inch of soil. [Question: "What are the six 'identical endowments'?
[Master: "It still lacks one move. [Question: "What are the seven 'identical gains and losses'? [Master: "Entering the mud, entering the water. [Question: "What about..."
“What is the eighth, ‘simultaneous birth and killing’? The Master said, “One cannot even save oneself. “What is the ninth, ‘simultaneous roaring with the same sound’?
The Master said, “An octagonal millstone rolling in the void. “What is the tenth, ‘simultaneous entry’?
The Master said, “Hanshan meets Shide. “With whom do they enter together? The Master said, “The Huhu Zhangsan and the Hei Li-si.”
[The student] asked: "With whom do they share the same sound in their roar? The Master said: "The black cat and the white ox. [The student] asked: "How do they share the same life and death?

The Master said: "Deishan’s staff and Linji’s shout. [The student] asked: "What thing shares the same gain and loss? The Master said: "Rolling about in the grass. [The student] asked: "Which one is fully endowed with it?
The Master said: "Picking up whatever comes to hand; every stroke is direct. [The student] asked: "What is it that is the same?"
[The student] said, "Pervasive and universal. The Master said, "Riding a great garuḍa within the shadow of a needle-point, one casually knocks down the moon from the edge of the sky.
[The student] asked, "Who shares in true wisdom? The Master said, "The ghost cave of Black Mountain. [The student] asked, "Who is it that studies together with you as a whole?

The Master said, "A lantern entering a dew-pillar. [The student] asked, "Which one shares in the Great Matter? The Master said, "The great elephant of Jiazhou and the iron ox of Shanfu. [The student] asked, "..."

"What thing has a single substance? The Master replied, "A bowl turned upside down on a mound. The Master retired to the Eastern Hermitage. Shortly thereafter, he was afflicted with a slight illness and wrote this verse:
"Coming, there is nowhere from which one comes; departing, there is nowhere to which one goes. With a sudden turn at the profound pivot, even Buddhas and Patriarchs are at a loss.
He sat in the full lotus posture and passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on the slopes of North Peak.
Chan Master Zuteng Zijing of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of the Gao family of Changxi.

He received his monastic training at Fashi Temple in Quanzhou and later traveled extensively to visit various masters of the Chan schools. He attained the essential meaning of the Dharma under Mian Shanbao.

He emerged from seclusion at Fengshan in Ningde and, in the Guiwei year of the Jiading era, moved to Gushan. While casting a great bell, he composed a verse regarding its hanging, which says: "Once cast from the mold, it turns with elegant grace."
Standing on level ground, he teaches others yet they refuse to desist; wishing to produce a great resonance that fills the universe, one must simply ascend another floor.

In praise of the occasion at Geohu, when Emperor Xianzong of the Tang dynasty issued an edict asking, "What is Buddha-nature? [Nanquan] said: "Because of the ground one falls, because of the ground one rises.
To seek rising apart from the ground is impossible. Not departing from the words of the question is indeed intimate, yet to fixate upon them is to rely [on them]."
Previously, he had not yet returned. In the Jichou year of the Shaoding era (1249), he moved to Beishan in Zhenzhou. Later, he moved to Tiantong;

Chan Master Caoyuan Sheng of Jianfu Temple in Ruzhou was a native of Nanjian. He once composed a verse on Lingyun’s Rock: "The clouds depart and then return, yet they have no intention;
The clouds come and then depart, likewise without mind. When existence and non-existence are cut off, where is the numinous?
A solitary peak stands abruptly, its greenness reaching to this day. He also offered a verse on Changsha and Yangshan enjoying the moon: "The floating clouds disperse completely, and the moon..."
When it is empty, a rabbit conceives and gives birth to a great beast. Leaping forth before the wind, it brandishes its fangs and claws;

The year ends, yet no paper money is burned; the rat’s burrow is pierced by a snake. Even if you attain profound realization, you remain face-to-face with the Western Heaven.
Chan Master Wanyan Zirou of Yinjing in Taiping Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of Chaozhou.

The tip of the willow threads. Furthermore, he offered this verse on *Qian-nü lí-hún* (The Parting Soul of the Maid): "Recalling the past, we strolled through the imperial gardens in the spring breeze;

He offered this verse on Nanquan, Guizong, and Magu going together to pay respects to National Teacher Nanyang: "A golden needle embroiders out jade..."
Mandarin Ducks: A stone woman brings them forth without concealment; they are rudely spied upon by a wooden man. To this day, they remain paired, yet never form a true couple.

Cooked in one place; the water dries up and the mud is spent, and snow-flower blossoms appear. Seizing the moment, he pulls it out and demands a celestial price.
With the evidence so clear, who would dare to dispute? In a verse on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, the Buddha said to Ānanda:

"When you see that which sees, this seeing is not seeing. The rain washes the pale red peach buds tender; The wind shakes the withered green willow filaments light. Within the shadows of white clouds, how strange!
*Shilu*. Amidst the luster of green waters, ancient trees stand clear.
Layman Zhang Yi, Minister of the Board of Rites, styled Yuezhai and named Gongfu, was a descendant of the Prince of Zhonglie.

Holding the rank of Academician of the Hall of the Secretariat, he visited the Meditation Chamber of Miman. Upon receiving the instruction from Monk Meng’an, he brought up the "dog" koan; suddenly, he heard the sound of a bell.
"Awakening through Sound. The verse says: "A single strike of the bell, the faculty of hearing is blocked; from the side of the lump of flesh, a thief is driven away.
When someone asks me what school I understand, I say: 'The face of the Śūnyatā-deva is black. He wrote this to inform them of the source of his awakening. The Hermitage Master (An) approved of it.

Thereafter, he withdrew from worldly tracks and ceased all distractions, strolling leisurely in the small garden by South Lake. Sometimes, wearing a simple headcloth and trailing a staff, he would whistle and sing.

He traveled back and forth with a serene composure, forgetting to return home. He once said, "An ancient sage once remarked that only one who is untainted by worldly sentiments can preach the Dharma to deliver others.
For within the *Glorious Treasury* (*Ābhāsvara-garbha*), what is not a manifestation of playful liberation?
If the mind is ever pure and free from all grasping and attachment, one can constantly enter the samādhi of non-differentiation amidst differentiated objects. Thus, even in brothels or wine shops..."
They traverse the ritual sites, where the sounds of drums and music all discourse upon Prajñā.

Yet, if they do not realize that these things create barriers for the mind and that following emotions leads to shifting attachments—just as a bird stuck in birdlime suffers injury to its life—they will never know what it means to preach the Dharma and deliver sentient beings.
Later, he donated his residence to establish Huiyun Monastery and invited Mian to be its founding abbot.
[Mian was] a Dharma heir of Chan Master Guanzhi of Tiantong (this master was a successor of Jingci Yihui; no record of his lineage exists, but he is now included in the supplementary lamp records).
Chan Master Shanjie of Rentang at Huqiu in Pingjiang Prefecture offered this praise for the Fish Basket Guanyin: *Cloud-like tresses...*
With heavy makeup and forced smiles, she enters the dusty world for the sake of trivial matters. Though she brings with her that which is truly alive, no one buys it;
they view her merely as an ordinary dead commodity.
The Dharma Heirs of Chan Master Tiantong Ying (Master Ying was a successor of Jiaoshan Ti; his records were not included in the *Jianyuan* [Jingde Chuandeng Lu].
They are now incorporated here to supplement the Lamp Records). Chan Master Lingyin Jingrou Rujué of Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Wuzhou.

Initially, he studied under Chidun at Mount Zhong. He once presented a verse, saying: "Under the white blades of Mount Zhong, I pressed forward bare-bodied; Several times I have nearly been buried alive. One..."
Since the man was lost and the house destroyed, I have realized there is no position left to arrange. Being dull-witted, I accept this. Later, after his stay, he ascended the hall and said:
"In the new year, we beat the new drum; universally bestowing the new rain of Dharma, all things are renewed, each and every one coming into accord with the rules."
The Great Being Samantabhadra rejoices; seizing the opportune moment, he opens the door and releases the White Elephant King, who vanishes across the earth with no trace left behind.
Holding up his staff, he says: "Only this one thing does not belong to the old or the new. At the slightest opening of the mouth, it swallows the Dharmakāya.
He throws it down and asks: "What is this? Within the peach pit of a thousand years, there is still that very same kernel of the past."—End of the Tiansheng Period.

In the spring, [the Master] ascended Mount Jing from Yuyewa Temple and gave a small-scale discourse (xiaochan). "This school of ours upholds the full authority of the True Command. It is like a sudden storm or torrential rain, sweeping all before it;
like a spark struck from stone or a flash of lightning, which cannot be overtaken. To raise a thought is to lose the source; to lift one's head is already to have missed the mark.
This is not a dharma of the present moment; do not give rise to various kinds of thoughts. Even if you practice the three types of cultivation simultaneously," [he continued].
To seek realization within a fixed period—this is the first head and third point. Ten thousand props and a thousand supports only serve to increase one’s sense of urgency;
yet they fail to realize that before the skull is even formed, the original eye is already clear. With a single cry of "Gua," everything is resolved once and for all.
Nevertheless, though this is so, among ten thousand who claim personal realization, not one or two are true; those who misunderstand are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. A monk asked Ru...
"What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "A rotting winter melon. He further composed a verse, saying: What is the Buddha? A rotting winter melon.
Biting into it, the frost pierces through the teeth. Though its roots have no storage pit, It blooms once every year.
A Verse on the Day the Buddha Attained Enlightenment: Six years on the Snowy Peaks, he finally attained the Way; He struck out the eyes of his former ghost-self.
His face was filled with shame, with nowhere to hide; To this day, he still fears that bright star.

The Dharma Successor of Chan Master Wanshou Guan (This master was a successor of Dahong Zheng; no *huiyuan* [record of his assembly] has appeared. He is now included here to supplement the Lamp Records).
Chan Master Wumen Huikai of Huanglong, Hangzhou, was the son of the Liang family of Hangzhou. He studied under Yue-lin, practicing the "Mu" (No) koan.
For six years he attained no realization, whereupon he resolved with fierce determination to hold himself accountable, vowing: "If I do not cast away sleep and destroy this self..."
One day, while standing beside the Dharma seat, Linji suddenly heard the sound of the meal drum and attained realization. He spoke a verse:
"A clear blue sky and a bright sun, with a clap of thunder— The eyes of all living beings on the great earth are opened wide.

The myriad phenomena and the entire cosmos bow their heads together; Mount Sumeru leaps and dances through the three stages. The next day, he entered the room intending to communicate what he had realized. Linji suddenly asked, "Where did you see the deity?"
"I have seen a ghost! The Master then shouted; Lin also shouted. The Master shouted again. From this point on, their spiritual resonance and dialogue became perfectly harmonious.

In the sixth year of the Chunyou era, by imperial decree, he was appointed to open the mountain at Huguo Renwang Temple. Ascending the hall, he said: "Right and wrong, long and short—these are but winds passing by the ear.
Do not seek out differences or similarities therein. If you wish to remain unmoved by the eight winds, let the ground of your mind be equal."
"Empty space. Old Man Ciyun only knew how to set sail with the current; he could not steer against the wind. Huanglong was not so.
Having cast aside both right and wrong, realize it within right and wrong. Why is this so? "How many times have black winds tossed great waves?
Yet I have never heard of a fishing boat capsizing. During a great drought that year, Emperor Lizong of the Song dynasty summoned the Master.
He prayed for rain. Upon returning, he sat in silence. The Emperor sent an inner attendant to inquire about him; the Master replied, "It is tranquil and unmoving, yet it responds and penetrates.
Shortly thereafter, a great rain fell. The Emperor conferred upon him the title Chan Master Fuyan.
Chan Master Miaoyin of Zhushan in Tanzhou, while reading the sutras by moonlight, spoke this verse: "Before the tongue moves, the literary brilliance is revealed;
The five thousand scrolls are fully encompassed at once. If you say you must wait for the moon to open the volume again, I dare guarantee that even in a donkey’s lifetime you will not reach the end."
Chan Master Xuefeng Zhen, the nineteenth-generation descendant of Nanyue and successor to Chan Master Hangzhou Jingshan Yuansou Xingduan,
was a native of the He family of Linhai in Taizhou. Initially, he went to study under Master Cang.
At Jingshan, the Old Man asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Taizhou. The Old Man gave a shout.
The Master spread his sitting cloth. The Old Man shouted again. The Master withdrew his sitting cloth. The Old Man said, "I grant you thirty blows; go to the meditation hall.
At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. One day, while attending him, the Old Man said, "There are no monks in Southern Fujian. The Master said:
"Monk? the Old Master asked. The monk immediately struck him with his staff. The Master caught it and said, "Do not say there is no good in being a monk.
The Old Master nodded in approval and immediately invited him to serve in the office of the Attendant. When the Old Master passed away, he went to Jingci Temple to rely upon Chan Master Shilin Gong.
Shilin appointed him as the Secretary (Jishi). He later visited Xueyan, who asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the Two Zhe regions. Xueyan asked, "Why do you speak..."
The sounds were different. The Master said, "Close that foul mouth! Yan replied, "The Tadpole Path Bridge is high; the Jiyun Peak is steep.
I do not yet know where the Secretary resides. The Master clapped his hands and said, "The duck swallows the snail; its eyes protrude!
Yan laughed and, looking back at his attendant, said, "Serve some fine tea. The Master said, "That is unnecessary," and subsequently sent him to reside in the Mengtang Hall. Great!
In the fourth year of the Dade era (the *gengzi* year), he emerged into the world at Zifu Monastery in Lake County; his disciples flocked to him and his fame reached the capital.

By special imperial decree, he was granted the title Chan Master Huiben Zhengbian. Subsequently, he presided over Zhongtianzhu Monastery. In the *renzi* year of the Huangqing era, he moved to Lingyin Monastery.
An imperial decree was issued to establish a Great Assembly for Water and Land at Mount Jinshan, commanding the Master to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma;
he was additionally bestowed the title "Buddha-Sun Shining Universally" (Furi Puzhao). In the *Renxu* year of the Zhizhi era, he was appointed to Mount Jing;

in the *Jiazi* year of the Taiding era, the Emperor sent down an imperial edict to provide him with great protection, and further bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *kāṣāya*. This was the third time the Master had received the gift of a golden-embroidered robe. A monk asked: "The three..."
The Venerable Master Sheng said, "When I meet people, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others.
The Venerable Master Xinghua said, "When I meet people, I do not come forth; when I come forth, I immediately act for the sake of others. What is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"A rooster bites a lamp-stand as it runs; a turtle gnaws a fishing rod. The monk said: "Let us set aside for now whether one acts for the sake of others or not. What is 'meeting'?"
The monk presented a phrase for others. The Master said, "I know. The monk said, "If you do not present it to people when you encounter them, then let it rest for now.
What is the phrase for benefiting others? The Master said, "Urgent. He asked, "What is the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye?
The Master said, "The Stone Brave-at-Heart at the crossroads. The monk said, "Is this not just that very thing? The Master said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain and much [sun]."
Feng. A monk came for an audience. The Master asked, "From which direction do you holy ones come? Where do your numinous spirits dwell? The monk replied, "Linzhen.
The Master said, "Fabricated Chan practitioners are as numerous as hemp and millet. Go to the hall. He then examined another monk, saying, "The Go-board Stone will split your forehead;
the Basin Pond will soak rotten your soles. As the monk was about to answer, the Master gave a shout. He examined him again.
A monk said, "Splitting open the Huaru and Huayue mountains, their beauty reaches the heavens; releasing the Yellow River, it flows clear to the very bottom.
[The Master] said, "Set that aside for a moment. On the ground of reality, speak a single phrase! As the monk prepared to open his mouth, the Master struck him. He ascended the hall and said:
"‘This very mind is Buddha’—this is like exchanging a sweet fruit for a bitter gourd. ‘Neither mind nor Buddha’—this is like a precious vessel filled with impurities. It is not..."
"The mind is not the Buddha, nor is it an object. Zhengzhou produced Cao, yet fortunately there is no connection. Holding up his staff, he said:
"This staff has drilled through Northern Uttarakuru and run toward Western Aparagoyānī; now it goes forth from Mount Xiangfeng to raise clouds and spit mist.
He struck the ground once and said: "A fire breaks out at the bottom of the great ocean, burning everything away."
He struck the ground once more beneath the eyebrows of the Great Image at Jiazhou and descended from the seat. He then ascended the hall and said: "Set aside the Buddhas of the three periods;
set them away on the wall of the six patriarchs. Within the twelve hours of the day, you must first recognize your own master.
Taking charge wherever you are, every place where you stand is true; even when shaken by the five desires and the eight winds, it remains unshakable."
It moves. It cannot be confined within the four modes of birth or the nine realms of existence; only then does it correspond even slightly [to reality]. Let me ask you this:
while you are wearing clothes, eating food, defecating, urinating, walking, standing, sitting, lying down, seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing—who among these is your true master?
There are some people who recklessly speculate within the eighth consciousness and say: "Call..."
It has sound, yet its form is not seen. Right now, as you speak and respond with vivid clarity, is this not your own true master? To say otherwise would be a mistake.
This is the very root of birth and death throughout immeasurable kalpas; it is the mass of ignorance and karmic consciousness from beginningless time.
It causes you to fall into the sevenfold and eightfold delusions and subjects you to myriad sufferings and a thousand afflictions.
Xin! How could you recognize this as being real? Aside from this, after all, who is your true master?
Again, he called out in a loud voice, "Master! Be alert! Ascending the hall, he said: At the ancient watchtower, the horn sounds at dawn;

The bath master and the *karmadāna* oversee the collection: "A thousand grains and ten thousand grains arise from a single grain;
from where does this single grain arise? A thousand lamps and ten thousand lamps arise from a single lamp; from where does this single lamp arise?"

If you recognize one lamp, then a thousand lamps and ten thousand lamps—lamp after lamp—are beyond doubt. If you recognize one grain, then a thousand grains and ten thousand grains—grain after grain—are without obstruction.
A three-legged donkey trots along, treading through the boundless seas of fragrant water. Holding up his staff and striking it once, he said:
"Even at the crown of the head, this one blow must not be lacking. The eighth month of the Xinsi year of the Zhizheng era.
On the fourth day of the month, he wrote a verse and instructed the assembly, saying: "Fundamentally there is no birth or extinction; how could there be coming or going?

Flames burst forth from the icy river; flowers bloom upon the iron tree. He set down his brush, extended one leg, and passed away. His entire body was enshrined and interred in the Jizhao Pagoda Courtyard.

Chan Master Yishan Liaowan of Jiangxin Temple in Wenzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Jingci Ying. He was the son of the Jin family from Linchuan in Fuzhou. At the age of fifteen, he achieved renown for his mastery of the imperial examination essays;
nevertheless, his long-standing aspiration to leave the household life could not be thwarted. He departed to join the community at Changle Monastery in Jinxī.

Upon his tonsure, Dongsou led him to Nanping to serve as the *shangzuo* (chief seat) and *shuji* (record keeper). One day, while passing by a shrine, the Master saw paper ashes swirling upward with the wind;
he was suddenly liberated, forgetting all that he had previously realized. He hurriedly reported this to Dongsou, who questioned him until there was no longer any doubt or obstruction.

Consequently, he received Dongsou’s seal of approval (*inka*). Later, while traveling to Tiantai, the assembly requested him to open the Dharma at Han’an. He subsequently moved to Zituo, Shushan, and Kaixian.

He ascended to reside at Jiangxin; whenever he felt slightly displeased, he would immediately abandon his stay and depart. It happened that Chan Master Yuejian Ming of Mount Lu sent a boat to welcome him back to Dongxi.
After Master Ming passed away, the community of Kaixian again invited him, whereupon he returned to Kaixian. In the winter of the first year of the Huangqing era, he fell ill.
He wrote a parting message and passed away while sitting in meditation.

At Zhangsheng, I likewise have no dharma to give to people, nor do I settle the case according to the facts. He held up his staff and said: "What is the Buddha?
