This is the matter that transcends the Buddha. He cast down his staff amidst the carved beams and painted rafters, then returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.
On the fifteenth day of the second month, he ascended the hall, struck his whisk once, and said:
"Today, Zhangsheng shall take a black bean bursting forth from cold ashes thirty years ago and replace the eyes of the Old Barbarian. He gave a shout and said: "Even if there were a single dharma..."
"Transcending Nirvana. This one shout of mine does not function as a mere shout.
Chan Master Yuanxi Huiji of Yangshan in Hongzhou was a successor of Chan Master Yuwang Guan; he was the son of the Tang family of Nanchang and was born together with his elder brother, Yuanling.

He studied for the civil service examinations. Once Yuan-ling had passed the imperial exams, the Master then shaved his head. Hearing that Wuchu was propagating the teachings at Yují, he went there to rely upon him.
When Wuchu spoke with him, he was greatly amazed and marveled at him; he remained in his service, attending him morning and evening, inquiring after and exhausting the secrets of the Dharma.
Later, he visited Master Dong-sou Ying at Nanping, where Ying appointed him to serve as the recorder (*jìshǒu*). In the second year of the Yuánzhēn era, he departed.
Baizhang of the world moved to Jingci. He ascended the hall and said: "Yunmen spoke the word 'Universal,' and no one in the entire world could do anything about it.
Yet they failed to realize that Yunmen was flat on his face, cornered by all sides.

At that time, had I let out a thunderous shout to rouse him, and waited for this old fellow to lose his temper, I would have slowly performed a bow and said, 'Do not take offense. This would not only have saved him," but...
Lao [Zhang] was also able to revitalize the fundamental principles of Yunmen. Nevertheless, the mouth is the gateway to calamity. He ascended the hall and said:

"In the Three Realms there is no dharma; where can one seek the mind? White clouds serve as a canopy, and flowing springs act as a zither. From antiquity to the present there has been no gap— who is the one who knows this music?
He struck his whisk and said: "One tune, two tunes—no one understands them. After the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep. Up.
In the Hall: Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak, the cold embers flicker but do not glow red. A single spark of fire emerges; a solitary crane flies past Liaodong.
Having spent three months at Mount Qianjing, the Master took up his staff and returned to the foot of the Southern Mountains. When they tried to urge him to rise again, he would not go.
Hearing that the Master had retired to leisure, scholars from Jiangxi all turned their sincere hearts toward the flavor of the Dharma, [seeking it] as far as Baizhang and Dayang.
His followers vied with one another to request him as their teacher. The Master declined, but being unable to refuse, he eventually returned to Mount Yang.
After residing there for three years, he prepared to pass away; he composed a verse for the assembly, cast aside his brush, and entered nirvana. Below Mount Dàyǎng is the Golden Cock Rock;
because it corresponded to the prophetic omen of Great Master Mǎ, he was buried there.

Chan Master Yunfeng Miaogao of Jingshan in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wen of Jingci. A native of Fuling Prefecture, after receiving full ordination, he went to study under Chijue and later met Wuzhun;
both held him in high esteem. Subsequently, he studied under Yancxi. One day, Yancxi raised an analogy, saying, "It is like a cow passing through..."
"The head, the horns, and all four hooves have already passed through the window lattice; why is it that the tail cannot pass?
The Master had a sudden realization and said, "The whale swallows the ocean water entirely, revealing the coral branches. Xixi said, "You have only spoken half of it.
Later, he emerged into the world at Dalu, was transferred to Quanzhong and Heshan, and subsequently received an imperial edict to reside at Jiangshan. (Zhiyuan)

On the *gengchen* day, he moved to Jingshan. He ascended the hall and said: "Before the world had taken form, heaven and earth were in profound stillness; before sentient beings and Buddhas were manifested, the body was fully manifest as the True.

Without cause, the Great Being (Avalokiteśvara) leaped forth from the eagle's nest, tearing off his own face-skin—already having been subjected to the brushstrokes of others' descriptions, how much more so this old bearded barbarian with missing teeth, who, failing to rely on his own fundamental nature, gazes afar toward the Great [Land] of Eastern Zhendan..."
Riding upon his spiritual capacity, he has traveled ten thousand miles from afar. His intent was to cut across the ranks and seize the market;

yet, now that the drums resound in the Phoenix Hall and the bells toll in the Azure Pavilion, every turn of the throat strikes a taboo, and every step taken finds no door. The entire nation cannot catch up, and he has been doubly exposed.
Thus, the Way of Mount Jinshan had no choice but to board another’s vessel and enter another’s domain—where the new official does not take charge.
Regarding past events: how is it ultimately? [The Master] struck the meditation seat and said: "The watchtower is silent, storing the moon over a thousand peaks;
the wild grasses lie idle, spreading the autumn across ten thousand miles. Entering the hall, he said: "The five peaks stand steep and lofty; only those who are truly such people can reach them.

A single mirror hangs in the sky, and there is nothing that does not receive its illumination. The ancestral patriarchs' foundation remains as it was; how has the livelihood of the patch-robed monks ever changed?"
In the midst of change, where there is no place to grasp, one must precisely rouse oneself; when there is no door for the feet to enter, only then can one truly tread the path.

Wait until the mountain clouds are serene and the stream waters flow gently; when the single melody is impartial and the myriad realms enjoy peace and prosperity—at such a time as this, where does the merit reside?
From of old, the chariots and books shared a common script and track; today, the four seas are one family.
Addressing the assembly: "Before words, the meaning is discerned; beneath the phrase, the essence is clarified. On Mount Dongji, the Dharma is preached with blazing intensity;

in the deep waters of the Zhu, it flows on as a continuous stream. If you can grasp this here, you cannot avoid mutually obstructing one another. If you still harbor views and listening, you will be caught in a state of restless agitation.
From the morning cock to the evening bell, there are those who praise and those who slander the Chan school. The Master sighed and said, "This is the School Gate..."

"This is a matter of great importance; I must struggle for it even at the cost of my life. He then hurried to the capital. An imperial decree was issued to assemble the followers of all schools for a debate in the court.
The Emperor asked, "What do you take as the fundamental principle of Chan? The Master replied, "Pure wisdom is wondrously perfect; its essence is inherently empty and still.
It cannot be reached by seeing, hearing, sensing, knowing, thinking, or discriminating. The Emperor questioned him repeatedly, and the Master cited extensively from the West and the East...
He recounted the various patriarchs of the land, including the circumstances of Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shouts.

In general, he stated that Chan is the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye and the Wondrous Mind of Nirvana; it is the vehicle for the Supreme Vehicle—what could surpass Chan? His words were clear and explicit, totaling over two thousand characters.

Furthermore, he was invited before the throne by Imperial Prince Xuanjin, who sat together with the Master of the *Bai fa lun* (Treatise on the Hundred Dharmas), Xianlin, and had each of them hold [the texts].
Lin said, "From the Deer Park until the Bahudhika River, not a single word was ever spoken during that interval.
From where, then, did these five thousand-plus scrolls come? The Master said, "The temporal teachings of a Buddha's lifetime are like a finger pointing at the moon;
one must understand that what the finger points to is ultimately not the moon itself. Lin asked, "What is Chan? The Master struck him with his hand.
Yuanxiang drew a circle. Lin said, "How can you move your hands and feet? The Master replied, "Even this single circle cannot be penetrated;
what need is there to speak of a thousand sutras and ten thousand treatises? Lin was speechless. The Emperor was greatly pleased and granted him food. He took his leave and returned south.
He passed away, and his stupa was erected at the western foot of the mountain behind the temple.
Chan Master Zhihong Jian of Tiantong in Mingzhou composed a verse on the story of Dayang’s “Formless Dharma Hall,” saying:
True emptiness is formless and beyond names or models; That which is established is subtle, while that which is painted is coarse. To speak of it is not difficult—it is written upon this paper:
The bearded man of the Western Heaven has no whiskers at all.

Chan Master Yue Tang Zu-yin of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Peng of Shuanglin. He was the son of Zhou of Nankang. One day, while reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he reached the passage:
"The single, firm, and dense body manifests within all atoms. Suddenly, he had an awakening. He went to see Bieshan, who asked him:
"Where have you recently been? The Master said, "Jiangxi. The Mountain asked, "Is the Great Master Ma well?
The Master joined his palms and said, "I pay my respects to the Abbot. Danqiao asked, "Is it true that Linji was struck three times with a severe staff by Huangbo?
The Master said, "Yes. Danqiao asked, "Why did he then punch Daoyu in the ribs three times? The Master said, "When one receives an ox from another, one must return an ox to that person."
Miaojiao nodded in agreement. After Miaojiao passed away, Jishi filled his position. One day, while in the meditation hall, Jishi brought up the "Pine Tree" koan.
As the Master hesitated, Jishi raised his voice and said, "Why do you not say: 'In front of the Yellow Crane Tower, the Parrot Isle'? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
After some time, he returned to Mount Lu and took charge of Xilin. In the ninth year of the Dade era, he resided at Lingyin.
Once, he interrogated a monk, saying, "The myriad Buddhas of the fine dust are upon your tongue; the holy teachings of the Tripiṭaka are beneath your feet.
Why do you not suddenly awaken? The monk was at a loss. The Master then shouted. Again, he interrogated another monk, saying, "Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his slaves.
Who is he? The monk prepared to respond. The Master then struck him. A newly arrived monk entered. The Master asked him, "What..."
[The monk] replied, "From Minzhong. The Master asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained there? He replied, "When hungry, one eats; when weary, one sleeps. The Master said, "Wrong.
[The monk] asked, "May I ask how you maintain it here, Reverend? The Master shook his sleeves and returned to his quarters.
After staying for four years, he bid farewell to the assembly with a verse, saying: "Coming together through conditions, departing when conditions disperse. *Zhuang* (a sudden strike)..."
He overturned Mount Sumeru, leaving only empty space revealed, and then passed away.
Chan Master Yeweng Bingtong of Xuedou in Qingyuan Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Jie of Lingyin and a native of the Zhang family of Xinchang. Initially, he followed Chijue.

At Tiandong, he next went to the chamber of Dachu. When Dachu raised the story of the fire burning the mountain on the first day of the twelfth lunar month, the Master was about to respond when Dachu suddenly struck him with his bamboo staff.
He attained realization. He then withdrew from public view, traveling with his staff and closing his door to copy the Lotus Sūtra.

There was a couplet that read: "In old age, I do not disdain guests; in stillness, I wish to transcribe the sūtra. At that time, Xuedou’s seat was vacant, and the assembly earnestly requested him to take it.

The Master went to attend. On the fifteenth day of the eighth month in the year of Renyin, he ascended the seat. His words of exhortation to the assembly were exceedingly earnest, as it was clear he was signaling his departure.
When the assembly requested that he leave behind a verse, he smiled but did not respond. At evening, he passed away.

Chan Master Chengjian Yusou of Zhiti Mountain in Funing Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wuwen Can of Jianfu Temple. He was the son of the Zhang family from Ningde in that same prefecture.
He received the tonsure at Longshan in Zhenghe and subsequently entered the inner quarters of Chan Master Wuwen Can. Initially, he resided at Baiyun.
In the twentieth year of the Zhizhi era, Emperor Shizu issued an imperial decree granting him the abbacy of Zhiti and bestowing upon him the title of Great Master Tongwu Mingyin.
Later, when he manifested his passing, he wrote a verse: "For eighty-two years, I have been deceived by worldly conditions; now, with a somersault, I turn to trace my steps toward the Western Heaven.
Having bathed and changed his robes, he sat cross-legged and passed away.
Chan Master Wuzhun Shifan of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Wolong Xian. He was the son of the Yong family of Zitrong in Jianzhou.
At the age of nine, he left the household life and requested instruction from an elder master on the method of sitting meditation. The elder asked, "What is Chan? And who is it that sits?"
The Master investigated this day and night. One day, while on the toilet, he attained a realization regarding the previous dialogue.

He went to visit Fozhao of Yuwang Monastery. Fozhao asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Jianzhou. Fozhao asked, "Have you brought your sword with you? As soon as these words were spoken, the Master let out a shout.
Zhaoxiao said, "This is Wutouzi; he acts in a chaotic manner. When [Zhaoxiao] arrived at Lingyin, Po’an was the First Seat.
While traveling together to Shisun An, a practitioner requested instruction on the "Monkey Child" kōan. The Master attained great enlightenment while standing by his side.
He first resided at Qingliang in Mingzhou, then moved to Jiaoshan, Xuedou, and Yuyang. Later, he received an imperial decree to preside over Mount Jing.

Entering the hall, he said: "At Vulture Peak they pointed to the moon; at Caoxi they spoke of the moon. Passed down from generation to generation, they have taken a tortoise and certified it as a soft-shelled turtle.
Elder Fan usually has a mouth hanging on his wall that he has never once opened. Today, for no reason, he has entered here..."
Traveling from door to door, having reached this point, I have no choice but to sift through here and there.
I cannot help but take up my many-year almanac and point out a few instances where I was misled or deceived, telling them to you all.
This is merely so that Guo Da, Li Er, Deng Si, and Zhang San may know that it is cold in spring and hot in autumn in Jiangnan and the Two Zhe regions. Even so, the Yellow River has three bends...
Once every thousand years, a purification. Entering the hall: This matter is truly simple and easy to understand;

it is mostly because you yourselves create difficulties and create obstacles for yourselves. Therefore, sometimes when I see people on the eastern or western corridors bowing and offering greetings, I simply lower my head to receive them. In truth, there is nothing else to it; I only wish for you all to...
If you recognize this old man, he is a native of Longqing Prefecture in Xichuan.
If you could recognize him, I would speak some local dialect with you and share some regional talk. For now, let us not speak of whether you recognize the old man;
first, each of you should know your own native place. Do you know it? Mingzhou has six counties; Fenghua has eight districts.
Ascending the hall, he said: "It cannot be named; it cannot be described; it cannot be grasped; it cannot be relinquished. If one attains it just like this, tell me, what is it that is attained?
Three people would testify that a tortoise has become a turtle. Emperor Lizong summoned him into the Xuzheng Hall.

His responses were detailed and clear, and the Emperor bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *saṃghāṭī* robe. Furthermore, an imperial decree was issued for Ciming to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma. The Emperor drew back his curtain and watched.
[The Emperor] granted him the title Fojian. On the first day of the third month of the Jiyou year of the Chunyou era (1249), he fell ill.
He then ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying: "This mountain monk is both old and ill; I lack the strength to engage in idle chatter with you all.
Now, exerting myself, I shall thoroughly shake out everything that I have not yet spoken of before and deliver it to you. Thereupon, he rose from his seat.
Shaking out his robes, he said, "How much is this? and then returned to the abbot’s quarters. On the fifteenth day, he assembled the congregation to give his final instructions.
At dawn on the eighteenth day, he wrote a verse: "When I came, empty and bare; When I go, naked and stripped.
If you wish to ask for the ultimate truth, There is the Stone Bridge at Tiantai. A short while later, he passed away. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Yuanzhao Monastery.

Chan Master Shitian Faxun of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an was the son of the Peng family of Meishan. Initially, while traveling to visit Shichuang, he paid his respects to Lei Qian and presented this verse:
"A single thought of compassionate countenance is fundamentally never separated; why must you suddenly act so outlandishly?
Your heart of compassion is so earnest as you level the high and accommodate the low, that it vexes Master Lei into a night of busy toil. Because of this, the Master’s name became widely known.

Chao heard of the renown of Dao-wang of Qiong-long Po-an and went there to rely upon him. Inside the hermitage, as [Dao-wang] raised the story of the World-Honored One holding up a flower and Kāśyapa smiling, the Master said:
"A scorched brick strikes and freezes through to the bottom; red-eyed, one bumps into a firebrand."
Master An-yin marveled at this. He first resided at Gao-feng in Su-chou, and subsequently moved to Feng-qiao, Zhong-shan, Jing-ci, and Ling-yin.

Addressing the assembly, he said: "If you obtain the root, do not worry about the branches. What do you call the root? What do you call the branches? A pine or cypress remains green for a thousand years, yet it does not suit the tastes of the people of the age.
A peony blooms red for but a single day, yet the young gentlemen of the entire city fall into a drunken stupor. I, this mountain monk, am like this..."
"What do you say? If there is one who does not consent, he is my fellow student. Disciple Shi Jun painted a portrait of his master and requested a eulogy, which included the line:
"The final word was entrusted to Chushan. The assembly was quite surprised by this. The following day, the Master suddenly manifested illness; he retired to Baoshou Temple to prepare for his end.
Once the preparations were complete, he immediately entered nirvana. His entire body was interred behind the monastery.
Shan. Yunju Jizan Cijue Chan Master of Nankang Prefecture was a native of Shu. He cited a monk’s question to Yexian:
"What is the place where the student applies his mind in secret? Yexian said, "Rolling a ball through a bustling marketplace. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? Yexian—
He said, "I invite everyone to look. The Master composed a verse: "A ball is rolled through the bustling market; all the people gaze upon it. A gust of pure wind blows, chilling the face.
To settle turmoil, no need for a double-edged sword; To bring life back, what necessity for the Nine-Return Elixir?
When the Master first ascended to Yunju, he stayed one night at the Yaotian Village. There, he dreamed that the local deity Anle Gong said to him, "You and..."

This mountain has only one occasion for serving gruel. Tomorrow afternoon, when you arrive at the temple, after the evening assembly has concluded, two fellow monks will be found quarreling and being unruly, bringing it to the attention of the temple authorities.
Consequently, as is the custom for new arrivals, they will be expelled. You, Master, will then be deeply moved by suspicion and astonishment.
Several years later, a scholar from Shu who had attained high office at court and was a close friend of the Master requested that he take up the vacant seat at Yunju.
The Master filled his position. Joyfully accepting the command, he was about to return when the details of his previous dream were finally realized. Upon reaching Yaotian Village, he passed away.
He was a dharma successor of Chan Master Yue of Lingyin.
Chan Master Wenli, known as Meiweng, of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture, was the son of the Ruan family in Lin’an, Hangzhou. His family resided at the foot of Mount Tianmu.

When the master was six years old, he accompanied his mother to gather mulberry leaves, carrying a basket. Suddenly, he became aware of his thoughts and wondered, "Who is it that is carrying this basket?

Thereupon, he conceived the aspiration for renunciation. At sixteen, he received full ordination and went to study under Huixuan. Huixuan cited the verse on "the already accomplished reality" (xiancheng gong).
According to the records, when his story about "letting you off thirty blows" did not accord with the teaching, he went to see Fozhao. Fozhao asked, "As you come in this manner, who is your master?
The Master suddenly attained realization of the meaning. On another day, Fozhao asked about the monk who said, "It is the wind moving, it is the banner moving.
The Master said, "The object sees its master; the eyes stand bolt upright. Fozhao further asked, "It is not the wind moving, it is not..."
"When the banner moves, where is the Patriarch to be seen? The Master said, "Lift off the skull-cap. Zhaoxi was delighted by his brilliance and dispatched him to serve as a secretary.
After some time, he heard that Songyuan was propagating the Way at Jianfu Temple in Raozhou. When Songyuan asked a monk in his room, "Is it not the wind moving?
Is it not the banner moving? the monk hesitated, and Songyuan struck him out with his staff. Upon hearing this, Zhaoxi suddenly forgot all his intellectual understanding and went to study under him.
Having received formal certification (*kanna*), in the fifth year of the Jiading era, he opened a Dharma hall at Huiyun in Lin’an. He subsequently moved to Nengren and Jingci.

In his teaching quarters, he would frequently raise the kōan regarding the southern bamboo shoots and the eastern sea cuttlefish; whenever a student attempted to deliberate upon it, the Master would invariably strike him thrice with his toothpick.
None were able to find a point of entry. Later, he moved to Fiquan and was elevated to the abbacy of Tiantong, where he ascended the Dharma hall to deliver his inaugural address.
A Japanese monk asked, "When the Master sees Buddha-illumination, how is it? The Master said, "There is jade within the stone.
The monk asked, "After seeing Songyuan, how is it? The Master said, "There is no oil in the sand. A monk asked, "The meaning of 'By observing the directions one knows where the traveler has gone;
yet the traveler does not arrive at any direction'—what is its intent? The Master said, "The road ahead meets no village; behind, one does not reach an inn. There was an *upāsaka* who came forward.
He went straight into the abbot’s quarters and said, “I have come to submit a formal petition to the Master. The Master asked, “Where is the defendant? He replied, “The Master is he himself.
The Master said, “What grievance do I have against you? The man was left speechless. The Master seized him and said, “Worthy adversary!
Worthy adversary! Then Venerable Hu came for an audience. The Master asked, “What is your name? He replied, “Zhihu (Wisdom Tiger). The Master—
The Master withdrew and made a gesture of fear. The tiger hesitated, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters. He ascended the hall and said: "Sentient beings have never been deluded;
at the end of night, the rooster cries out toward the fifth watch. The Buddhas have never been enlightened; in the clear autumn, the wild geese fly across the vast sky.
[He struck his knee once and said: Last night the moonlight was bright by the western window; the cool breeze has already reached the wutong trees."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it arises only by relying on conditions. Since the conditions do not exist, from where could the Dharma be established?
The dragon pool pouring a thousand-foot waterfall is not the condition; the wild goose peak soaring ten-thousand-fathom high and cold is not the Dharma.
When an eye-opening monk arrives here, what should he do? Even if he were bold and discerning, this old monk would break his staff."
It has not yet been set down. Why? It is the sword that kills, the blade that gives life. Entering the hall: In every matter there is no obstruction;
green mountains are reflected beyond the slanting sun. In every dharma there is no discrepancy; ancient trees before the eaves bustle with flocks of crows.

Do you not see how the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan traveled to the ends of the earth? In Yangzhou, at the fifth watch, he heard the painted horn; it blew the plum blossoms down and broke them apart. Directly—
Even now, one has not yet reached home. On the occasion of the Imperial Birthday, he ascends the hall; seated within the crystal palace, he lowers the curtains of luminous night.

He is a single, undifferentiated whole, beyond all categorization; he responds to manifold conditions in profound stillness without error. From the time of the ancient patriarchs until now, this station has been revered as supreme.
Furthermore, how can one raise and chant a single phrase that embodies the whole body? "The wondrous leaves respond to all capacities, entering together into the tribute;
let the various paths be distinguished as they are by their own provisional means. On the anniversary of Master Hongzhi’s passing, he ascended the hall:

"Beyond the night-bright curtain, before the precious mirror stand, there is fundamentally no 'both-and' nor any 'exclusive-or. At such a time as this, who ultimately occupies the position of the absolute? Ancient...
Crossing the desolate pass, the frosty moon is cold; amidst the wind-still reeds, the herons sleep. Entering the hall: Ten thousand pines guard the distant pass, nine ridges shrouded in mist.

Across the valley, the wind carries echoes; in the mountain stream, the water flows with sound. If you observe with the eyes and listen with the ears, your tongue will be pulled out and you will be ploughed under.
If you do not observe with the eyes and listen with the ears, your tongue will still be pulled out and you will be ploughed under. But where does the point of benefit and harm lie? If not...
"Sleeping on the same bed, how could one know the lining of the quilt was torn? The Master retired from his monastery and lived in leisure upon the banks of Liangzhu.

When groups of monks gathered to visit him, it was no different than when he was presiding over the monastery. As he was about to enter nirvana, he said to his attendant, "Who will build a seamless stupa for me?
The attendant replied, "Please provide us with a model for the stupa, Master. The Master said, "Even with all one's might, one cannot paint it. He then passed away with a serene expression.
Chan Master Wude Jue Tong of Huazang in Changzhou ascends the hall on the occasion of the Green Sprout Festival: "Shatter a single mote of dust and the Great Sutra emerges;
The soaring hawks and leaping fish are even more distinct. To not look with the eyes but to look with the mind— This is already like repeatedly striking ice within fire.
Soaking black beans, obscuring one’s whole life; Only when reaching the end does one speak of abundance outside the gate. Spinning white snow."
The mulberry trees are deep green; the yellow clouds of ripened rice have been harvested, and the grain is now turning verdant.
Chan Master Zhongqian Daxie of Xuedou in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Ying family of Yiwu, Jinhua.

In his youth, upon seeing the *Mind-King Inscription* by the Great Master Fu (Dashi), he vowed to leave the household life. He first met Xian’an, who regarded him with high esteem yet suppressed his [ambitions].
Rui said, "Your Confucian habits have not been eliminated; how can you reach the state of great rest and ultimate repose?
You should become like a person made of wood or earth. The Master studied this morning and evening until he had an awakening, whereupon he named himself "Daxie" (Great Rest).
Later, upon meeting Songyuan, one day while hearing the story of Bimozhi holding up his staff, he suddenly cried out, "What can be done? There is someone who cannot bear it!"

Yuan held up his bamboo whisk and said, "I am going to strike you, and you will not find it agreeable. As the Master was about to offer a word in response, the whisk suddenly came down upon him; he was at a complete loss for what to do.
Yuan let out a thunderous shout, and the Master immediately attained sudden enlightenment.
Chan Master Yun’an Puyan of Daochang Mountain in Anji Prefecture praised Zhaozhou, saying: "Without cause, he lifted up the seven-pound robe;
how many practitioners of Chan have applied their minds to it? They all make their nests in Qingzhou, unaware that the spring colors lie in Jiangnan."
Chan Master Shan Kai of the Yan-shi Hall at Jinshan in Zhenjiang Prefecture composed a verse on a monk’s question to Yunmen regarding the Dharma-body:
“Six are not gathered; one is not established. Where can the pure Dharma-body be sought? Last night, a gust of wind blew through the leaves;
it swept away all floating clouds, and the moon shone upon the wall. He also composed a verse on Jingci Ken-tang’s public address: “By observing the directions, one knows where they have gone.”
Who says that observing the directions does not depend on the directions? As soon as one opens their foul mouth, they fall into error.
The traveler who seeks the road to Chang’an does not realize that his entire body is already in the Imperial Capital.
Chan Master Hilian of Shiyuan in Fengxiang, Wenzhou, was the son of the Ma family from Chaoyang. A monk asked:

"In the past, when Emperor Xiaozong summoned Chan Master Fozhao Guang and questioned him about what Śākyamuni Buddha accomplished during his six years in the mountains, Fozhao replied, 'I thought Your Majesty had forgotten. What is the meaning of this? The Master answered with a verse: The Great Root...
A great vessel, a great cultivation; in a flash, the pivot of the mechanism turns toward the ultimate source. For ten thousand billion years there has been but one Buddha;
the Snowy Mountains have never truly separated him from the imperial palace.
Chan Master Shaoshi Guangmu of Ruiyan in Taizhou praised the Fourth Patriarch, saying: "At the summit of Pòtóu Peak, purple clouds fly;
Three times he declined the imperial summons, aging in the emerald mists. Though this 'stale merchandise' has no further use, It should not be handed over to a small child.
He composed a verse on Lingyun seeing peach blossoms: "As soon as he saw the peach blossoms, his heels were stuck; The Iron Ring Mountains have swallowed him whole."
There is no gate through which to exit. How many times have you leaned against the wall and pressed against the fence? With every spring breeze, one’s soul is severed.
Zen Master Xinxin of Beihai once composed a verse on the occasion of Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty and the clam:
"Mixing water with mud—how busy he was! He was caught out by that [clam], which was far too audacious. Though he silently grasped the King’s intent, He had already lost his entire body."
Entering the boiling cauldron. Regarding the verse on Xuefeng opening the door and letting his body fall through: "Born of the same lineage, yet we do not die together;
the younger brother is deaf and the elder brother is blind. The family estate is utterly ruined and reduced to bare-bones poverty;
he takes gold and treats it like dung. This is the final word: do not be crude or careless. The sweet is sweet, and the bitter is bitter.
Chan Master Zhuonan Zhao once composed a verse on the occasion of Nanquan carving a Buddha, saying: "Bringing it forth with both hands is difficult to conceal;
As before, he returns it with both hands. Sleeping soundly under a pillow of pure breeze, A bird carries a falling flower onto the path before the cliff.
He also composed a verse on Songyuan’s public address regarding why "an eye-opening monk loses his nostrils," saying: "Kill!"

Ten thousand people lose three thousand; playing alone with the single-pointed staff, the pivot is incomplete. Under ten thousand acres of blue waves on a bright moonlit night, a short flute sounds from a fishing boat.
Chan Master Guyuan Dao of Jingci Monastery in Lin’an once composed a verse on the story of Shitou clearing weeds, which says:
Shitou cleared the weeds to test the heroes; Dana was muddled, his eyes not yet high. Had he known how to turn back and walk the living path, To this day he would not have entangled his descendants.
Chan Master Yugou Yuanzhi of Gushan in Fuzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Tian Tongjing. He was a native of the Xue family of Changxi.

At the age of eighteen, he received his monastic training under Chan Master Zhanranben of his home county. At that time, Kuchan was presiding over Fengshan; the Master went there to follow him and seek instruction.
He was extremely diligent. Chan already marveled at him. He left the mountain range to pay his respects to Master Yan of Xi at Shuangjing.
Subsequently, he studied under Master Song of Shaolin at Beishan and remained there as the recorder (*jishi*).

He gained renown at Shaolin, and when Kuchan moved to Jingshan to succeed to that seat, the Master said with joy, "The unfinished business before Mount Qingfeng is now complete. When Chan arrived, he again served as the recorder; shortly thereafter, their spiritual resonance was realized.
He subsequently received formal certification (*kanna*). In the Jiashì year of the Jihài cycle, he went forth to reside at Jianfu in Pingjiang.
He was later transferred to Cuifeng on Mount Dongting and then to Fuyong in Yixing. He retired to Lingyin, but was later summoned to serve as abbot at Fashi in Quanzhou.

Before long, he was moved to Yishan in Fuzhou, where he restored its ruins. In the autumn of the Guihai year, he moved to Gushan; after only one summer, he requested leave due to illness and retired to the East Hermitage to spend his final years.

On the seventeenth day of the first month of the Bingyin year of the Xianchun era, he sat in the lotus posture, wrote a verse, and passed away. He was seventy-one years old by secular age and fifty-eight years by monastic seniority.
His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at Nanyuan on Mount Gu.
Chan Master Qingxi Yuan of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: “When Bodhidharma came from the West, he occupied the entire ground with a single sitting mat.
Yet, after Shen Guang paid him three prostrations, it was all claimed at once. This has caused the descendants of later generations to each divide up the territory and establish their own boundaries.
Monks of our tradition pluck through the weeds and gaze upon the wind; morning in Wu, evening in Yue; south to Mount Tiantai, north to Mount Wutai.”
"Have you ever trodden upon the grass at the tip of the staff or the soles of the sandals? After a long silence, he said, "By all means, do not tread upon them.
Chan Master Jianfu Sheng was a dharma successor of Chan Master Chijue Daochong of Mount Jing in Lin’an; he was the son of Xun of Wuxin and possessed a nature that far surpassed others.
Chang failed to pass the jinshi examinations and studied under [Master] Zizhou at Miaoyin Monastery. In the third year of the Shaoxi era, he crossed the Gorges;
at that time, Cao Yuan had been installed as the abbot of Miaoguo. The Master went to pay his respects, and upon hearing the master’s words regarding the lineage, he attained realization.

He was asked to attend upon him for three years, after which he took leave to travel to Zhejiang with a verse stating: "There remains but one pair of destitute hands, now turning toward all quarters."

Regarding the phrase "scratching where it itches": [Zhaozhou] studied under Songyuan at Lingyin. Songyuan’s gate was steep and forbidding; for eight months, Zhaozhou lived there like a straw hat, yet he did not gain entry into the inner chamber.
When someone reported that the Master had lost a fine disciple, Songyuan said, "I have already opened the gates wide with my eight characters to accommodate him."
"From this point on, he has simply missed the mark face-to-face. When the Master heard these words, his oral and auditory faculties were simultaneously lost;
he saw through the source of Cao Creek. While at Miaoguo Guifeng, his laughter, scolding, and abuse were all skillful means for the sake of others.
From then on, he no longer doubted the tongues of the old monks throughout the land. He first resided at Tianning in Jiaxing, and moved to Xuefeng after only half a year.

By imperial decree, he was transferred to Tiantong Monastery. As the seat at Yuyang was vacant, he concurrently assumed the position of abbot there. He ascended the hall and said: "The tools used at Tiantong are not needed here at Yuyang;
the tools used here at Yuyang were not needed at Tiantong. Although this is so, though they are not needed, in that place where they are not needed, their utility is inexhaustible.
With a single arrow, two vultures fall from one’s hand. He ascended the hall again and said: "The monastery of Perfect Enlightenment."

In every atom there is a path; sitting and cutting off coming and going, one suddenly empties past and present. "Thirteen over there, fifteen on this side"—the sequence does not differ by a hair's breadth.
It is laughable that the Yellow-faced Gautama, even to this day, does not know where he has fallen. [He] ascended the hall and said:

There is one person who, in a single thought-moment, attains sudden realization and enters the ranks of the Buddhas. There is another person who, for kalpas on end, remains an icchantika and has no wish to become a Buddha.
Tell me, which of these two is worthy of receiving the offerings of devas and humans? After a long silence, he said: "The butterfly pierces the fragrant path, its two brows damp;
the bee plunders the withered flower, its two thighs stout. Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three..."
[The student asked: "There is no differentiation. What is the past mind? The Master said: "Set it down and wait for it to cool before you look at it. [The student asked: "What is the present mind?
The Master said: "You ask and I answer. [The student asked: "What is the future mind? The Master said: "I will tell you when I ascend the hall next time.
[The student asked: "What is the past Buddha? The Master said: "Last year’s plum blossoms. [The student asked: "What is..."
[The student asked,] "What is the Buddha of the present? The Master said, "This year’s willow. [The student asked,] "What is the Buddha of the future?

The Master said, "His countenance and fragrance remain as they were. [The student asked,] "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the past? The Master struck the left side of the meditation seat with his whisk.
[The student asked,] "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the present? The Master struck the right side of the meditation seat with his whisk.
[The monk] asked, "What is the wisdom of future differentiation? The Master pointed a single dot in the middle with his whisk.
The monk said, "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings have no front or back; the oceans of lands in the ten directions are contained within a single hair. He then prostrated. The Master then said:
The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended.
Since these three minds cannot be apprehended, what is called "discriminating wisdom"?

If one sees through this thoroughly, the Buddhas of the three periods of time have never for a single moment not been turning the Great Dharma Wheel upon the crowns of everyone’s heads. Come here and test it further!

"Shoulders side by side and feet together—what is there to seek in a bowl? With these words, he drove them all away at once with his staff. Not long after, he was summoned by imperial decree to move to Mount Jing.
As he approached the time of his passing, he said to the assembly: "The anniversary of Wuzu’s death falls on the eighteenth of the third month;

I shall depart on the fifteenth, so I will not be able to prepare incense or offer ritual provisions. On the fourteenth, he ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly and cited the occasion when the World-Honored One was about to pass away.
Upon entering *nirvāṇa*, he addressed the assembly, saying: "You should all carefully observe my body, which is the color of purple-polished gold.

Look up at it with reverence and take full measure; do not let yourselves regret it later. Today there is, but tomorrow there will be none. The Master said: "Throughout his life, the World-Honored One exhausted every skillful means;
yet at the moment of death, he could not find birth when seeking birth, nor could he find death when seeking death. As for this mountain monk—"
"Not so. When he wished to walk, he walked; when he wished to go, he went. Even the eight-armed Nala could not restrain him. He descended from his seat.
At the hour of midnight, he sat up and passed away within a short while. He was eighty-two years old, having lived for sixty-one [years since his ordination].
During the cremation, there were countless five-colored śarīra relics. Half of the sacred bones were enshrined in a stupa at Wangshan Hermitage in Jinling; the other half was enshrined...
At the Yuzhi Hermitage in the Chongpu fields of Tachang,
Master Yuan of Shuangshan— successor to Master Yinjing Rouchan—
once composed a verse on the story of Emperor Taizong’s exhortation to arouse the bodhicitta, which begins: "Ten thousand miles of songs of praise."
The Sage’s transformation is complete; with gentle breezes and timely rains, woodsmen and farmers rejoice. Were it not for the three cries at Mount Song, who would know that this is true peace?
Furthermore, he offered a verse on Ying’an’s question regarding Migan’s "True Eye of the Dharma":
When the young sons of the Five Tombs were in their prime, They galloped through the spring breeze, hearts full of joy. They spared no yellow gold for their pellets, [Only] the *hai-tang* flower...
"Striking down the yellow oriole.

Master Xijiang Mou of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huazang Jing; he was one of the four elderly masters of Jiangnan who did not receive imperial edicts from the Yellow Court.
In his tenth year, at the end of his life, he received three imperial edicts from the Son of Heaven. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The spring day is bright;
the oriole sings. How most intimate! Who understands to listen? One day, as he was about to enter nirvana, he looked toward his attendant monk, requested a brush, and wrote this verse:
"A single laugh turns the body over; the face of the sun, the face of the moon. He set down the brush and passed away. A stupa was erected for him at Tiantong.
Chan Master Kongyan You of Zhongtianzhu in Hangzhou, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Lingyin Jue, gave this instructional phrase (*chuyu*) in his quarters: "A true man forged of gold.
Donghai Yong composed a verse on it: "The young lord in brocade robes is drunk at a farmer’s house; He sleeps soundly upon a wooden bed while the sun has not yet risen."
Slanting. Parched with thirst and crying out for drink, he found nothing; he then traded his jade belt for a bowl of tea.
Master Chan Zong, surnamed Chou-an, of Huguosi in Hangzhou, a successor of Master Huanglong Kewen, ascended the hall and said, citing Master Linzhen of Yue-lin who addressed the assembly:
"The opening of the bag's mouth—do you still have anything to buy? The monk said, "I do. Lin said, "If it is neither expensive nor cheap, how will you buy it?
The monk was speechless. Lin said, "The old monk has lost out. The Master said, "Yuelin’s presentation of the question is truly extraordinary;
yet when confronted by another person saying the word 'yes,' he was immediately left with nothing but to cover this way and that, his treasury empty."
The treasury is not handed over in turn. Today, Huguo opens the mouth of his cloth bag; is there anyone who would buy it? After a long silence, he said:
"Though we lean upon the same balustrade, we do not view the mountain colors alike."
Chan Master Wenzhou Xialu Wujian once composed a verse on Xinghua’s beating of Kebin: Xinghua beats Kebin;
The words are intimate, yet the speech is not. From the tip of the staff, raindrops fall; He strikes forth the Jade Qilin.
The layman Fàngniúyú was a native of Gǔháng. During the Chūnyù era, he visited Wúmén, who would invariably intercept him with a face-to-face rebuke, saying, "Not so!
Not so! Later, when he met Chòuān, he asked, "What kind of realization do you have, Master, that you dare to distort right and wrong before this assembly of gods and men?
Chòuān replied, "Under Wúmén’s seat, I have no dharma to be attained, nor..."
"The Way can be transmitted, yet it consists of only two characters. The scholar asked, "How can these two characters be explained? The Hermit said, "Not so, not so.

At these words, the scholar finally realized that there was no gateway through which to help others. He once recounted the Barrier of Right and Wrong, saying: "Directly pointing to the human mind, seeing one's nature and attaining Buddhahood;
turning the light back upon itself, utterly transcending all obstructions. As soon as one attempts to deliberate... (The text breaks off here).
Clouds stretch ten thousand miles. When encountering people, one evaluates their character; when meeting things, one uses the "yellow and black" (i.e., praise and blame) of critics.

Valuing the ancient while disparaging the present, honoring what is heard while devaluing what is seen—one may indulge in conjecture and hesitation, yet remain a dreamer who has not yet glimpsed the "passage of right and wrong.

While staying in Anji Prefecture, the nun Shen Dao asked, "How many phrases are there in the 'passage of right and wrong'? The Master said, "There are four phrases. The nun asked, "How do you illustrate these four phrases? The Master said, "First..."
The first phrase: to have "is" and "is not" is unacceptable. The second phrase: to have neither "is" nor "is not" is also unacceptable. The third phrase:

to have both "is" and "is not," and "neither is" nor "neither is not," is also unacceptable. The fourth phrase: to have neither "is" nor "is not," and neither "is not" nor "neither is" nor "neither is not," is also unacceptable.

Only when one is able to transcend these four phrases does one finally see the natural radiance of the original ground. [The Master] asked, "Am I able to transcend them? The Master said, "You have transcended them."
[The Master] said, "It cannot be. [The Layman] said, "Every person has their lot; why should I not be able to leave? The Layman said, "When a hen is married, she flies after the cock;

when a dog is married, it runs after the dog. [The Master] asked, "What is the scenery of the original ground? The Layman said, "The crescent moon shines upon how many prefectures? How many rejoice, and how many grieve?
[The Master] said, "I am not asking about these words; I ask about the scenery itself. The Layman said, "Then you are asking about that [moon]."
The local scenery is such that it is said there is no appearance of male or female. The Master asked, "Since there is no appearance of male or female, what is the matter of right and wrong?
He replied, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is. He asked, "What is this matter further beyond?"
The scholar said: "The horse-leech has pinned the heron's feet; when you ascend to heaven, I shall ascend to heaven.
Chan Master Gufeng Xiushou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Zhengning Wanshan of Gushan in Fuzhou. He was a native of the Li family of Taihu in Shuzhou and received his monastic training there.
Regarding the Two Springs of Huangzhou: In the first year of the Jiāxī era, he entered Fújiān to pay his respects to Chan Master Gūfēng Xiù at Nángshān in Pǔtí.
He attended him for five years, fully mastering his profound teachings. He served as the Librarian at Gǔshān and occupied the seat of honor at Xuěfēng.

During the Bǎoyù era, he took up residence at Jiàolóngtái in his native prefecture, later moving to Wànshuài. In the tenth month of the Jǐsī year, he transferred to Gǔshān. He once composed a verse on the World...

When the Venerable One was about to enter parinirvāṇa, he rubbed his chest with his hand and said: "This decrepit Gautama knows no shame; even as he departs, he still displays his affectation of elegance.
Rubbing his chest to show the assembly where he is returning—when a single cry of a bird sounds, the mountains grow all the more secluded.

He also offered a verse on the story of Jingu Peak’s Pillow: "The calamities wrought by Heaven may still be avoided; The calamities one brings upon oneself cannot be evaded. He further offered a verse on [the same].
Deshan visited Longtan and said: "The dragon is not seen; the pond is not revealed. My whole body is already within the Hall of the Empty King.

Returning from my dream, I suddenly hear the dawn oriole singing; the spring breeze blows down petals of peach blossoms. On the eighth day of the twelfth month in the Jiaxu year of the Xianchun era, he passed away.
During his cremation, his rosary remained unburnt, and śarīra were recovered from within his teeth; consequently, a separate stupa was erected for him. Thus it is of the Master.
He entered Min more than thirty years ago; both monastics and laypeople revered and admired him as if beholding a living Buddha.
Whatever offerings he received, he entirely applied toward meritorious works, never accumulating any for himself. He lived to the age of eighty-four, with forty-five years of ordination.
Chan Master Jie of Shuanglin in Wuzhou once composed a verse on the occasion of Fu Dashi donning his cassock and wearing his crown, saying:
Neither Confucian, nor Daoist, nor yet Chan; His fabricated practice is truly pitiable.
He has delayed himself for three lifetimes without completion, Until now, more than eight hundred years have passed.
The Dharma Heirs of Chan Master Rongyang Hai (Master Hai succeeded Zhulin An; An succeeded Zhulin Bao; Bao succeeded Lanniuo He; He succeeded Tianmu Qi).
Qi succeeded Wuzu Faian (from Qi onwards, no one has emerged who has compiled the *Huìyuán*).
One night, Chan Master Zhonghe Zhang of Qingshou Monastery in Yanjing dreamed of a strange monk who, leaning on a staff, walked straight to the abbot’s quarters and sat upon the lion throne.
At dawn, he said to the guest prefect: "Today, whenever there is someone from the guest quarters, have them come to see me."
When it grew late, Haiyun arrived. The Master smiled and said, "This patch-robed monk is the one I dreamed of last night.
Yun said, "I have come without coming; how shall we meet? The Master said, "Study must be studied truly, and realization must be realized truly.
Do not go wandering through the wilds. Yun said, "Because the sparks flew out when I struck the fire, I finally knew that my eyebrows are horizontal and my nose is straight."
The Master said, "In my place, it is different. Yun asked, "How do you manifest this conviction? The Master said, "The teeth are a set of bones; the ears are two pieces of skin.
Yun said, "I thought there was something else. The Master said, "Wrong. Yun shouted, "The grass-robbers are utterly defeated!"
The Master retired for the day. On the following day, the Master cited the case where Linji’s two head monks of the two halls both let out a shout simultaneously.

A monk asked, "Is there still a distinction between guest and host? Linji replied, "Guest and host are perfectly distinct. How do you understand this? Yunmen said, "Shatter the mirror of the Qin dynasty;
