Chan Master Zheng Kui of the First Gate at Zhong Tianzhi in Hangzhou was the son of the Fang family from Poyang in Rao.
He went to visit Huiji, who asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "From Poyang. Huiji asked, "How deep is the water in Lake Poyang?"
The Master said, "Staring with wide-open eyes, one does not see the bottom. Ji said, "If that is so, then the nostrils of the patch-robed monk will be soaked and rotted away.
The Master said, "I certainly do not borrow the Venerable’s nostrils to breathe out. Ji said, "In the end, whose nostrils do you borrow to breathe out?"

The Master said, "I respectfully wish the Abbot ten thousand blessings. Ji approved of this and appointed him to serve in the *shisong* (attendant's office). He subsequently went to visit Yuansou, who appointed him to oversee the records (*zhangji*).
Later, he took up residence at Chongyin Monastery in Jinling. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way.
A single thought involving deliberation causes the entire body to enter the weeds. Therefore it is said: 'Before one's eyes there is no dharma,' for the intent lies in..."
It is not the present; it is not a phenomenon of the present. It is beyond the reach of the ears and eyes.

The heavens and earth of past and present, the sun and moon of past and present, the mountains and rivers of past and present, and the human relations of past and present—all are manifest in every instance, fully revealed in every thing.

It is not borrowed from the thousand sages, nor sought through the myriad functions. Within and without, there is nothing to take up; throughout past and present, there is no fixed location. To understand it thus—this is how it is.
This is still like mistaking the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for one’s father’s chin.
Nevertheless, since he is the Great Sage of Sizhou, why did he appear in Yangzhou? After a long silence, he said: "Investigate! (Chán).
Chan Master Zu Ying of the Stone Chamber at Yuwang in Mingzhou was the son of the Chen family of Wujiang in Suzhou.

Having left home at the age of seven, he immediately took up his staff to travel abroad. He first visited Xugu Ling; hearing of the spiritual transformation brought about by Huiji, he went to join him with great urgency.

Upon seeing him once, they were in perfect accord; he was subsequently retained as a record-keeper (*pangji*). He went forth to reside at Longjiao, moved to Wanshou, and was later transferred to Xuedou and Yuyang.

The Master composed a verse in thanks to Chan Master Pingshi Di for visiting him during his illness, which says: "This body is without self, yet the roots of illness are deep; I am ashamed that Mañjuśrī has come so far to visit me.
There are naturally mountain flowers to discourse on non-duality; Facing each other by the blue lamp, we laugh and chant."
Later, he constructed a wooden shrine and sat within it daily, no longer engaging with worldly affairs. As his death approached, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"For fifty-three years I have played with cleverness until I became clumsy; I have trodden through empty space and walk barefoot. The myriad phenomena and all living beings cannot help but laugh."
He then sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.
Chan Master Niangchang of Meiwu at Xiangfu Temple in Jiaxing Prefecture was originally from Huating; his secular surname was Huang.
At the age of twelve, he received the tonsure at Yuanming Monastery in Pingjiang. In the year Dushen (the fifth year of the Zhida era), Huiji moved from Baiyang to Jing... [text continues]
Cishi went to visit Master Ji. He happened upon the occasion when Ji was ascending the hall to address the assembly, citing the kōan concerning the elder Fushō of Taiyuan hearing the sound of a horn.

Ji’s verse said: "The lute-player enters the vast sea; The Grand Historian travels to famous mountains. From now on, along the road outside the city of Yangzhou, The strict order forbids the gates from opening early.

Upon hearing this, Cishi attained realization. He entered the master’s quarters to present his understanding. Master Ji nodded in approval and appointed him to serve as the head of the record office (the *jishitsu*).

He served diligently for seven years. In the *Bingchen* year of the *Yanyou* era, he presided over Xiangfu Temple and composed the twenty-two fascicles of the *Fozu Tongzai*, which was circulated throughout the monastic communities.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Yinglin Yun.
Chan Master Zongkuo Wuwai of Donglin in Jiangzhou was the son of the Wei family of Nanchang.

He first visited Yuetang, who questioned him regarding the kōan concerning the saying, "The sound of the stream is entirely the broad and long tongue. Their words and insights accorded with one another, and he subsequently received the master’s seal of certification.
He initially resided at Yunju and later moved to Donglin. His verse on his deathbed reads: "At the age of seventy-one, my worldly ties have now come to an end."
Overturning the five Sumeru mountains, the sun rises at midnight; suddenly he passed away.
Zen Master Xueyan Zuqin of Yangshan in Yuanzhou was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Fanzhen of Jing Mountain. Initially, while under Iron Stake Yuan, he took up the koan of the "Buddha-Dog."

Regarding the saying, "The son has no Buddha-nature," he remained sitting in a state of clear, stagnant water. Later, while visiting Tianmu Li at Jingci, he applied himself with fierce and courageous mindfulness within the hall;
suddenly, he attained something, yet he saw that his realization was not yet liberated from the ground, which obstructed his correct insight.
Later, while serving for many years under Wuzhun at Mount Jing, this ailment did not subside.

One day, while walking in the Buddha Hall at Mount Tianmu, he looked up and saw a single ancient cypress tree; the "obstructing object" (the mental blockage) suddenly dispersed, and for the first time he beheld the place where the Elder of Mount Jing stood.
He initially resided at Longxing Temple in Tanzhou and later presided over Mount Yangshan. Throughout...

Sixth Case. Entering the Hall: "The white ox on the open ground is pitch black; though you search for it here, you cannot find it. The mountains are green and the waters are blue—seeming to exist yet not existing.
What is seen by the eyes and heard by the ears is but a vague semblance. He pays no heed at all to the time, yet his hooves and horns remain."
As soon as one stirs, the traces have already vanished. Under the moon, leisurely blowing the short flute; before the wind, there is no need to pull at the long tether.
Hehehe! How extraordinary! Now, even if you try to pursue it, it will not go; free and easy, moving east, west, south, and north.
Small Assembly Sermon. The Way of Jibei emerges from the ordinary; whether speaking or remaining silent, moving or still, it is revealed in its entirety.
The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials are like straight pines and crooked thorns; the Four Guests and Four Hosts are like the short web-footed duck and the long-necked crane.

Thus, when Yuanwu spoke of the place where all Buddhas emerge, he said: "A fragrant breeze blows from the south, bringing a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions. This has brought unfortunate consequences for Miaoxi’s striking [the meditation seat].

The nostrils are lost; they pervade the world and are difficult to conceal. The mountains are verdant and vast; the waters are boundless and wide. There is no trace of a path; there is nothing to be taken up.
Beyond the bamboo fences and thatched huts of the river village, a returning sail hangs over the distant bay as the sun sets.
Entering the hall: "Good beans for making sauce; good salt for cooking soup. Rice can cure hunger; tea can quench thirst. This has been the direct transmission from the time of the ancients."
Reaching the ultimate point where principle is realized and emotion forgotten, nothing surpasses this. Why, then, did the old master Yangqi say, "A kicking donkey has three legs;
it is right when the eyes are open, and it is right when the eyes are closed"? Entering the hall: sound and form have already been exhausted.
There are those who have not yet reached the end; there are those whose seeing and hearing are already liberated, yet there are still those among them who are not yet liberated.
It is simply like a block of wood looking into a mirror or a hard stone listening to a bell—there is still that "block of wood" and "hard stone" present. Do you people ever reach such a state?
Has there ever been such a moment? If you think that by practicing Chan today you will accomplish the Way tomorrow, [you are mistaken].
"Good Wealth holds a single blade of grass in his hand.
Chan Master Duanqiao Miaolun of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou was the son of the Xu family of Huangyan in Taizhou.
At the age of eighteen, he received the tonsure at Guangci Monastery in Yongjia. There he met Guyuan at Ruiyan, where he heard the "three pounds of flax" koan and came to harbor doubts about it.
Suddenly, while reading the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*, he reached the passage stating that even mosquitoes, insects, and ants can accomplish tasks without speech; he attained a sudden realization.
He then went to visit Wuzhun at Xuedou. Wuzhun asked him to provide a response to the question: "Why does a dog have karmic consciousness? (Wuwei gowu yeyi).
After thirty turns, he still did not attain realization. The Master asked, "Is there no expedient means? Zhun answered with a verse by Zhenjing.
At that moment, Zhun stood transfixed for a long while; suddenly, hearing the sound of the wooden board, sweat poured down his entire body. Thereupon, he was finally liberated.
He traveled from Chushi Jiyuan to Qian Ruiyan and Guoqing, and finally arrived at Jingci. Ascending the hall, he said: "In the mountains of Jing there is jade;
those who obtain it do not find it within the mountains themselves. In the waters of Chi there is a pearl; those who pick it up do not find it within the waters themselves.

A monk possesses the 'True Person of No Rank'; those who realize him do not find his entry or exit within the face-gate. He suddenly took up his staff, held it crosswise, and said: "Do you understand?"
"Ma! A stone man crouches at the mouth of the Yangtze River in Youzhou. He ascends the hall and says: "Deshan bows his head; Jia Shan nods his head;
Jueyi raises a finger; Xuansha strikes the toe and breaks it. Taking up his staff, he says: 'All of these do not go beyond the tip of this mountain monk's staff.
How can this be seen? He plants the staff on the ground and says: 'A single leaf falls, and autumn comes to all under heaven.'"
The Master raised up the case of Chan Master Daguan Ying, who addressed the assembly, saying: "The seven Buddhas are the subjects of nature; the myriad dharmas are the slaves of mind.
Now tell me, where is the master of the house? He then gave a shout himself, saying, "From the seven Buddhas downward, they all show their heads!

Then he himself responded, "Each attends to his own duties. The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "To call the seven Buddhas 'subjects of nature' and to point to the myriad dharmas as 'slaves of mind'—[this is the master]."
Daguan claimed he possessed a path for leaving the world; yet when it came to shouting "Self! or responding with "Yes!", these were merely matters of a slave.
When has the true Master ever been seen even in a dream? Does the assembly wish to see him? With a single sweep of his whisk, he said:
"A spring breeze stirs at dawn, causing every kind of flower to bloom throughout the gardens. He then gathered the assembly at the time of his death, entered his room, and composed a letter.

He took his leave of the various mountains and the Duke of Wei. The Duke sent someone to inquire of him, saying, "The Master was born at Tiantai; because of [the influence of] Kumārajīva, he died at Jingci.
The Master replied, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. Having written this verse, he passed away.
Chan Master Xiyuan Hui of Tiantong in Mingzhou once composed a verse on the story of the Sixth Patriarch’s transmission of the robe, saying:

"He did not become a woodcutter, but became a miller; He used only his own strength to test the quality of the grain. Whether he knew he had trodden upon it or not, The rice and the husks alike reached the alms bowl.
He also composed a verse on the story of Lestam Changxing seeing Nanquan arrive and immediately turning his back to face the wall, saying:
Facing the wall amidst a perilous heap, he leads the guest past. When asked who it is, he asks further, "How is it? To say that the ordinary is already a matter of much concern;
when scrutinizing my own household affairs, they are even more so.
Zen Master Bieshan Zuji of Tiantong in Mingzhou was the son of the Yang family from Shunqing in Sichuan. At fourteen, he received full ordination.
Hearing a monk recite the words of Sixyan, he was filled with joy; at that time, Sixyan was residing at Qionglung in Suzhou, so he went there immediately to follow him.
While reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, he came across the passage concerning Maitreya’s tower closing after he had entered it; he was suddenly awakened as if from a dream.
He then composed a verse on Lingyun’s seeing peach blossoms: "A single red dot amidst ten thousand greens—how many rejoice, and how many resent?
Yan nodded in approval. Over the next two years, he visited various venerable masters, finally meeting Wuzhun at Xuedou.
From this it may be known that he was a vessel for the Dharma, treated with ever-increasing severity. At times, blows and shouts were delivered together, and not a single word was spared.

Whenever the Master attempted to respond, he would immediately be silenced and unable to utter a sound. Through this, his intellectual understanding was completely lost. After a long time, he spoke up and said:
"All the skills I have possessed throughout my life are but dead methods. Only now, upon meeting this elder, do I begin to tread the path of life.

Subsequently, he was appointed to the abbotship of Mount Jing (Jingshan). The Emperor then commanded that the Master share the seat [with the abbot]. He later took charge at Tiantong Temple on Mount Dongting. In the *Bao Yu* era, the year *Bingchen*, Tiantong was destroyed by fire;

by imperial decree, the Master was appointed to restore it. Upon his arrival, he lived in a hut made of bound reeds, carrying only a single bag and a single bowl. After three years, he successfully restored the temple.

The Old View. On the first day of the ninth month in the year of Gengchen, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The clouds are thin and the moonlight fresh; the trees have fallen away, and the mountain’s bones are exposed.
Since heaven and earth first came into being, how many have had eyes that truly see? When someone asked for an awakening, the Master said: "We shall not meet again; each of you must exert yourselves.

Ten days later, at the hour of night-watch, he called his attendant and entrusted him with his final affairs, saying: "Hold the great assembly in high esteem. He then crossed his arms and passed away.
[The Master] remained silent with his hand [raised].
Zen Master Yuepo Ming once composed a verse on a monk’s question to Zihu: "Do the sages of antiquity still penetrate the ultimate truth?
He said: "The fishing line in his hand is rolled up and then unfurled; His small boat ripples across Lake Dongting. Suddenly, a violent wave overturns the void."
He stood up; having packed up his things and returned, he possessed not a single skill.
The Chan Master Huanxi once composed a verse on the saying "This very mind is Buddha," which says: "This very mind is Buddha—arsenic and wolfsbane.
To raise the dead and restore life, it takes no more than a single dose."
Master Xishi Tan cited a monk’s question to Nanquan: "When the Master returns to his chamber, what will he point to as the guide?
Nanquan replied, "Last night at the third watch, I lost my ox; when I rose at dawn, I had lost my fire. The verse says: With servile faces and cringing knees, one runs through the world;
Ashamed to see those in sheepskins on the Qili River shoals. Though Emperor Wen-shu holds the nobility of a Son of Heaven, Zi-ling remains a man of the commoner class.
Viewed as an old acquaintance.
Master Ning Changuan of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "After the rain, the mountain colors before one's eyes are verdant;

amidst the seats, the wind is warm and the birds' songs are clamorous. He struck the meditation seat once and said: "It is laughable that the Old Barbarian [Bodhidharma] lacked the wisdom of transformation. Shaoshi..."
He sat before the peak for nine years. Entering the hall, he said: "The thousand peaks stretch before the eyes, their verdant hues filling the void. Willow catkins drift like cotton;
pitiful, the True Man of No Rank has been sleeping on grass and under the dew all along. *Ayya!* This spring is passing once more—when will it be the year of our return?"
Chan Master Jue’an Keyang of Xuefeng in Fuzhou was the son of the Ge family of Ninghai in Taizhou. Having studied under Wuzhun Shifan, he attained the essential meaning [of the teaching].
In the eighth year of the Xiachun era, he presided over Xuefeng for ten years. Upon resigning from his duties at the monastery, he retired to Baoshou Temple in Hangzhou.
He once composed a verse on the question posed by a monk to Guizong: "What is the profound principle? to which he replied: "The three sounds cover the cauldron lid everywhere."
The gate opens; those weary souls in the sea of suffering cannot be called back. Half of the spring’s ninety days has passed once more; empty petals fly, dotting the moss.
He further composed a verse on the "Eightfold Return" from the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* regarding the discernment of seeing: Return, return, and after returning, there is nothing left to return to.
A single idle man dwells between heaven and earth. Last night a tiger was bitten by a leopard; its fur and skin have fallen away, yet its body remains striped.
In the twenty-seventh year of the Zhizheng era, he manifested parinirvāṇa at the age of eighty-five. His remains were returned to Xuefeng, where a stupa was erected at the Western Hermitage.
He was a dharma successor of Chan Master Xun of Lingyin.
Chan Master Yujie Hui of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou went to study under Shitian. Shitian brought up the "Seven" koan of Yunmen, but no one could offer a word in response.
Suddenly, as a monk was just stepping across the threshold, Shitian said, "Xuefeng rolls the ball.

Hearing this, the Master suddenly attained realization while standing by his side and spontaneously uttered a verse: "Yunmen’s 'Seven,' Xuefeng rolls the ball. White artemisia and red smartweed— How clear!"
"A solitary boat under the moon. Tian nodded in understanding.
Chan Master Xue’u Ke of Zhongtianzhi Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "The withered mulberry tree knows the wind of heaven; the sea water knows the cold of heaven.
But tell me, what does the patch-robed monk know? He knows that rice is made from grain. Even if you were to understand it thus..."
"The Old Man Yama will have a day when he demands his meal money. The Master then resigned from his duties at the temple as the Song imperial throne had already been moved elsewhere.
Chan Master Moan Jue of Jinshan was well-acquainted with the Master and held his spiritual conduct in high esteem.
At that time, the Yuan army was descending upon Jiangnan; Moan was coerced by the Generalissimo Bayan into joining his staff and accompanied him to Wulin. Moan said:
When Buyan invited the Master to ascend and reside at Lingyin Monastery, he personally carried the letter of invitation and knocked at the Master’s gate.

The Master pulled back the bolt of the door to reveal half his face and asked, "Who are you? Mowan replied, "I am an old acquaintance of the Abbot. The Master dropped the bolt and said, "I do not know you.
This was because although the Master lived beyond the world, he maintained his integrity through loyalty and principle; thus, he felt no inclination to accept the invitation.
Regarding the legacy of Lingyin, Master Jiang En of Houduan later praised it, saying: "Forty years have passed since the Snow Hut was lost;
its lofty wind remains as chilling as ever. Although Prime Minister Buyan bowed at his bedside, he refused to come to Cold Spring for him."

The Night Assembly of Chan Master Heixuan Ruogong of Yuyang, Mingzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Lianzhai Litong: "The Shaoshi [Patriarch’s] room has no doors or gates; how can one immediately gain passage?
Standing patiently through the deep night, listen as I speak of the east and west. [He once composed a verse on Tan Yuan’s question to the National Teacher regarding the hundred...]
Later, when someone asked about the matter of the ultimate limit, he said: "The Way flows directly;
there is no need to carry a talisman for protection. The National Teacher truly acted out of concern for Danyuan; it was not a mere exchange of words at a parting.
Chan Master Xing Gong of Shilin at Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: A monk once asked an ancient worthy, "What is the eye for reading the sutras?
The ancient worthy held up his fist. The Master said: "If you call it the eye for reading the sutras, it is still a fist;
if you call it a fist, it is still the eye for reading the sutras. At this point, how do you distinguish between them? [He] called out, 'Great [assembly]!'"

The assembly said: "When the points of 'contrary' and 'touching' are difficult to distinguish, and when one fails to perceive before the opportune moment, even empty space is pierced through—how could it stop at rotten ox-hide?

Ascending the hall, he said: "In the stillness of the mountains, the bees’ thighs grow heavy with pollen; in the emptiness of the woods, the bamboo shoots reveal their bright flesh beneath the sheaths.
Leaning on the railing, I unconsciously become dazed and motionless, until a yellow oriole calls out once more. Sikong, speaking thus, deserves a blow from my staff.
[Offense] thirty *zhàng*. Why? Because it is improper for others to follow after sounds or pursue forms.

Chan Master Xuzhou Pudu of Jingshan in Hangzhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Huazang Tong; he was a native of Jiangdu in Wei-yang, surnamed Shi. He left the household life and traveled extensively...
When Yuanzhe (Wude) went to pay his respects, he asked, "Who is it that does not act as a companion to the myriad dharmas?
The Master said, "An iron Kunlun under a golden incense burner. Yuanzhe said, "I thought this short man had some merit; it turns out his understanding is only like this.
The Master bowed deeply and said, "Thank you, Preceptor, for your testimony. He later appeared in the world at Banzhan in Jinling, and subsequently traveled through various regions.
Having traveled through various lands, he arrived at Mount Jing and ascended the hall. He said, "When a person of heterodoxy speaks the True Dharma, the True Dharma is entirely heterodox;
when a person of orthodoxy speaks heterodox dharma, the heterodox dharma is entirely orthodox. He struck his staff once and said, "Heterodox?
Orthodox? He struck it again and said, "Speaking? Not speaking? "If you can discern and distinguish within this point, even a house made of gold will be yours."
This is not yet considered noble. What glory is there in fine food and brocade robes? [He] ascends the hall and says: "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind;

all conditions are but the awakening of nature. Originally, there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it is simply a matter of being enlightened today. Since there is no person who is deluded or awakened, what is it that is enlightened?
He strikes his staff once and says: "A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them. Again, they follow the warbling orioles past the short hedge."
[The Master] ascends the hall. He cites Master Linji, who said: "There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home;
there is another person who leaves home yet is not on the road. Which of these two deserves to receive the offerings of devas and humans?
The Master says: "Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have none. An inch of hair and a centimeter of silk—the heavens and earth are vast and empty. Pan Lang fell backward.

Riding a donkey, he fell and killed Huang Fancho. Shortly thereafter, showing signs of slight illness, he asked for a brush and wrote in large characters: "For eighty-two years I have steered the bottomless boat;
now I have capsized it and return home, under a single sky of bright moon. He threw down the brush and passed away.

Chan Master Jue’an Zhen of Chengtian Monastery in Ping’an Prefecture was a successor of Chan Master Xuedou Qian. A Huayan lecturer, acting under imperial decree, intended to convert the monastery into a lecture hall for doctrinal studies.
The Master said, "If you can expound on Chan, I will follow your request to change it; if I cannot expound on the teachings, you may change it."
"I shall follow you. Thereupon, he beat the drum and ascended the hall. With a single shout, he entered the five teachings to manifest our school—the one stroke upon the crown of a thousand sages.
The lecturer wept; he bowed twice and withdrew, requesting absolution for his transgressions.

Chan Master Xutang Zhiyu of Jing Mountain in Lin’an Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Daochangyan of Yanchuan. He was a native of Siming. He first appeared in the world at Xingsheng Monastery in Jiashhe, and later presided over ten monasteries in succession.
In the tenth year of the Xiachun era, he received an imperial decree to reside at Jing Mountain. Upon ascending the hall for the formal discourse, he said: "Words are sufficient."
Speaking all day long, one exhausts the Way; yet speaking, it remains insufficient. Speaking all day long, one exhausts all phenomena (*dharmas*).
Now, as for the Way and phenomena—*dharma* and *vastu*—are they one or two? If the Way were one, why is the guest mountain high and the host mountain low?

If the Way were two, why does [Zhuangzi] say that "heaven and earth are but a single finger" and "the myriad things are but a single horse"? If you can distinguish the black from the white within this, then...
"Money for your straw sandals. "Otherwise, I only wish that next year the silkworms and wheat will ripen. He gave one coin to Rāhula.
When the Master first resided at Jingci, an imperial messenger delivered an edict asking: "Vzhou was eighty years old when he traveled on pilgrimage;
why did he stay in the empty hall for another eighty years? The Master recounted the story of Vzhou’s pilgrimage to Linji and offered this verse: "Vzhou at eighty..."

He then set out on a pilgrimage. Having resided at Xutang for eighty years, he returned once more to the mountain. Possessing a unique faculty that revitalized the Buddhas and Patriarchs, he moved the imperial countenance within the nine-layered capital.

When the Emperor requested a verse to be presented in response, the Master submitted one, which greatly pleased His Majesty. He was specially granted five hundred *shí* of rice and one hundred rolls of silk.
During his tenure at Yuyang and Jingshan, he likewise received abundant imperial gifts and favors. Within his quarters, the Master offered this instructional phrase: "The Self..."
Why is it that those whose eyes are not yet clear take empty space for trousers to wear? Why is it that those who draw lines on the ground to make a prison fail to pass through this very point?
Why is it that those who enter the sea to count its sands stand on tiptoe upon the point of a needle?
After he passed into nirvana, he was interred at the foot of Zhiling on Mount Jing.
Chan Master Shi-fan Yan of Jingci Temple in Hangzhou cited the karmic occasion of Dayuan Da-dian expelling the Head Seat, and offered this verse:
"A single string of mani-jewels, confronting the situation directly before one's face; It deceived the Head Seat to death and left Han Yu in doubt.
Having exhausted all these wretched stratagems, Spring and autumn have never been known from the start."

The Master replied, "A short man watching a play. "A single point of compassionate heart cannot be split open; amidst the boiling cauldron, his smile fills his cheeks. Such a marvelous thing as this is difficult for me, the Emperor, to believe."
I have seen [him] come to preach the Dharma for the Sovereign.
Chan Master Jing of Jingshan, a successor of Chan Master Chong, while at Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou, raised the case where Guishan asked Yangshan: "Throughout the day, I am with you..."
"What kind of matter have you settled by deliberating? He drew a line in the air. Mian said, "Had it not been for me, he would surely have been deluded by that.
The Master offered this verse: "Though father and son are close, they deliberate together; How could one believe there are swords and spears within the breast?
If at that moment a single stroke had severed [the doubt], The entanglements throughout the world would never again arise. He also offered a verse on Mañjuśrī:
Questioning Ātreyī: What is the meaning of birth, and what is the meaning of death? The question was clear, and the answer was direct;
meeting face-to-face as the occasion required, there was no deception. Birth and death, life and death, have originally no boundaries;
the moon rises over the green mountains like a single sphere of jade.
Chan Master Beishan Long’s verse on Niaokuo Blowing on the Cloth Hair: An eighty-year-old elder must practice with vigor;
The cloth hair was blown up, and calamity arose anew. A stream of blood flows for three thousand miles; An old monk atop the branch of a withered tree.
Master Mengshan Yi, a dharma successor of Master Ningshan of Gushan, went to Gushan to visit Master Wanshan. Wanshan instructed him to contemplate the word "Mu," yet he did not achieve awakening.
He subsequently traveled to Chengtian Temple to pay his respects to Master Guchan Ying. One day, while sitting in meditation, the head seat entered the hall to burn incense.
While striking the incense box, he made a sound and attained realization. He composed a verse, saying: "The road ends where there is no further way; Treading upon the waves, they are but water.

The peerless old Zhaozhou— His countenance is just like this. Next, he stayed with Xutang. Xutang pointed to a vase of plum blossoms and said, "Whoever can compose a verse on this may return to the hall.
The Master said: "Having fought back the host of dark yin, I return with joy; Atop the hundred flowers, I am the champion of spring."
Observe how he employs skillful means for the sake of others, releasing the harmonious breath of spring. [Dongshan] said, "Go back to the hall.
He then went to study under Huanshan. Huanshan asked, "The radiant, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges—is this not the speech of the scholar Zhang Zhuo?"

As the Master was about to open his mouth, Shishuang struck him and shouted, driving him out. On a certain day the following year, as the Master was ascending the stone ladder, he attained great enlightenment.
He returned to the abbot’s quarters, where Shishuang again asked, "The light of luminous stillness pervades the sands of the Ganges—is this not the words of the scholar Zhang Zhuo?
The Master then overturned the meditation seat. Shishuang seized him and said, "Where is the point where you fell into verbal error?"
The Master covered the mouth of the mountain with his hand. Shanshan asked, "Where is the error? The Master said, "A second offense will not be tolerated.
Shanshan said, "Recite another verse. The Master immediately recited: "Yunmen acts strangely; he cannot even defeat himself. A lion bites a man;
a low hound chases after clods of earth. Shanshan said, "The staff is not here; I shall give you a beating on another day. The Master said, "Even so..."
"I still need to borrow something from you. Shanshan picked up his bamboo staff and struck him three times.
The master then prostrated three times and withdrew. Later, while instructing the assembly, he said: "There is one in Suzhou; there is one in Changzhou. An octagonal millstone rolls through the void.

Chan Master Haiyun Yinjian of Qingshou Monastery in Yanjing was a dharma heir of Chan Master Qingshou Zhang. He was the son of the Song family from Ningyuan in Shanxi. From birth, he possessed divine insight.
At the age of seven, his father taught him the "Opening the Sect and Clarifying the Meaning" chapter of the *Xiaojing* (Classic of Filial Piety). The Master asked, "What is the 'opening' sect?"
"What does 'clarity' (ming) mean? the father asked in astonishment. Thereupon, he took Zhongguan Zhao as his teacher.
One day, while supporting Zhao during a walking meditation, Zhao said, "Master Faldeng says, 'Look at how busy the affairs of others are! Now tell me, by whose power do they proceed?
How do you understand this, my son? " The Master gave Zhao’s hand a sudden tug. Zhao said, "You wild fox spirit! The Master replied, "Yes, yes. Zhao said:

One must further investigate this separately. Later, during a gathering while leaning on his staff, he passed through Songpu. Encountering rain, he stayed overnight beneath a cliff; there, while striking a fire, he attained great enlightenment.
He rubbed his face and said, "Only today do I truly believe that my eyebrows are horizontal and my nose is straight.

Only today do I believe the words of the old monks throughout the world who never sleep. He went to visit Chan Master Zhonghe Zhang and subsequently received the seal of transmission (as recorded in the *Zhonghe Zhang*). The year was Xinmao.
The Master was celebrating his birthday. One day, he encountered several monks in the corridor. He asked the first monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to view the flowers.
The Master struck him. He asked the second monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to prostrate before the Buddha.
The Master struck him as well. He asked the third monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "Where are you going? The Master struck him as well. Then he asked the fourth monk.
"Where are you going? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him as well. He asked the fifth monk, "Where are you going?
He replied, "I am going to look for the Master. The Master said, "Why do you look for him? He said, "To give him a beating. The Master said, "With what will you beat him?"
He said, "Bring me the staff to strike me. The Master struck him four times and said, "You are a fellow who traffics in empty talk. The assembly all fled. The Master called out, "Venerable Elders!
The assembly turned their heads back; the Master asked, "What is this? Later, he received successive imperial honors and greatly propagated the Way of Jibei (Linji).
He passed away, and was posthumously titled Great Master Furi Yuanming.

Chan Master Nanshi Wenxiu of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou was the son of the Li family of Kunshan in Suzhou.
He left the household life at Shaolong Monastery in his home district and once sought the essentials of the Dharma from Chan Master Xingzhong of Huqiu, whereby he attained the meaning beyond words.

In the fifth year of the Hongwu era, he resided at Pumen Monastery in Suzhou. On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked: "When the World-Honored One appeared in the world, the heavens rained down four [flowers]..."
Huā asked, "When you, the Master, appeared in the world, what auspicious signs were there? The Master said, "A single ox drinks water, and five horses do not neigh.

Huā said, "If that is so, then the joyful intent shall be transmitted for a thousand ages, and the lineage of Quiescent Illumination shall spread in all directions. The Master said, "Better that good things had never happened.
Later, when he moved to Lingyan, he ascended the hall and said: "The treasury of the true Dharma-eye has endured from antiquity to the present. Prajñā is the true..."

The lamp illuminates heaven and earth; facing the sun, there is no front or back. Directly beneath, there is nothing to take up. It is spiritually manifest alone, penetrating form and penetrating sound.
Vastly it appears before one, beyond hearing and beyond seeing. It is ever-present in all places, yet not constrained by any place.
It is not separate from any time, yet not encompassed by any time. If you can see it here, there is nothing—

Bringing this to this land, one does not know by what power of grace he has attained such extraordinary excellence. After a long silence, he said:

At the beginning of the Yongle era, an imperial decree was issued for Confucians, Buddhists, and Daoists throughout the realm who were profoundly versed in literary meaning to compile and edit [the canon].
The *Yongle Dadian* was commissioned by imperial decree; the Master responded to this summons and remained in the capital for three years.
In the summer of the seventh year, he resided at Mount Jing. Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad phenomena of the forested universe are all sealed by a single dharma.
What do you call 'the single dharma' here? The peak before us is Bowu Peak; in the center is the Buddha Hall. After a long silence, he said: "The Patriarch Guoyi was originally from Kunshan."
Four years later, the Master retired to the Pines Monastery on North Mountain in Suzhou due to old age and illness. One day, he passed away without illness.
He was a Dharma successor of Chan Master Ming of Jingshan.
Chan Master Tianning Xibai Lijin of Jiaxing Prefecture was the son of the Yao family of Wudu.
In his youth, he took refuge under the Baoji Monastery and received the tonsure. He first visited Guding, who showed him the koan of Deshan meeting Longtan; through this, he attained realization.

He was appointed to serve as the Head of the Secretariat (Chamberlain). Before long, he was commanded to lead the assembly and take his seat to preach the Dharma. In the *dingyou* year of the Zhizheng era, he went to reside at Rui Guang Temple.

When Tian Ning Temple was destroyed by fire, the Master undertook its restoration. The Imperial Preceptor conferred upon him the title "Universal Salvation through Perfect Penetration" (*Yuantong Pujie*).
The Master lost his father in childhood; only his mother remained. He therefore went one *shè* east of the city to build Gūyún Ān (Solitary Cloud Hermitage) to provide for her care.
Some criticized him, to which the Master rebuked them, saying, "Do you not see the venerable master Biān Pú?

Why do you speak so easily? At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he moved to Jìngcí Monastery. In the spring of the fourth year, by imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Tiānjié Monastery. Upon seeing the Emperor...

The Emperor received him at the outer court, where he offered words of comfort and praise more than twice, his gracious intentions being most profound and generous. He immediately ordered an inner official to escort him into the monastery.
Subsequently, the Emperor summoned him again to the inner palace; his responses to the Emperor’s inquiries were to the latter’s satisfaction, and the Emperor was greatly pleased.

That spring, an imperial decree was issued to establish a Great Memorial Dharma Assembly on Mount Zhong, and the Master was commanded to preside over the fasting rites. In the fifth year, another great assembly was established. The Great...

there was none who was not delighted and won over. One day, he suddenly said to his disciples: "I have a karmic debt from a previous life that remains unsettled; I must surely repay it. Do not constrain me with worldly appearances.
Not long after, he manifested a slight illness and passed away in accordance with the natural course of things. His body was then cremated.
There are countless śarīra relics. His stūpa is located at the Huancui Aranya (Monastery) to the west of the city of Jiaxing.

Chan Master Jueyuan Huitan of Tianjie Monastery in Nanjing was a dharma successor of Chan Master Longxiang Yin; he was the son of Yang of Tiantai. His mother dreamed that she had swallowed a bright pearl.
She became pregnant, and when he was born, his appearance was remarkably dignified. In his youth, he did not associate with other children;

as he grew up, he followed the Yue Faguo Monastery to renounce the householder’s life and soon received full ordination. Initially, he studied the teachings of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* and the practice of *śamatha-vipaśyanā*, mastering them all without exception.

He then left those studies to enter into meditative cultivation. At that time, Xiaoyin was propagating the Way in Central India, so the Master went to visit him. Xiaoyin asked him from where he had come.

[The Master] said, "You have come. Yunmen said, "I have come to tour the mountains. [The Master] asked, "As for 'under the bamboo hat, how is it that you have smashed through what Luopu studied while traveling everywhere?'—how is this?
Yunmen said, "Before you even entered the gate, you had already presented it. [The Master] asked, "Why then do you not bring it forth right now?"
The Master was about to deliberate when Yinyuan gave a shout. At that moment, the Master experienced a sudden, liberating realization.

On another day, Yinyuan opened both hands and showed them to the Master, saying, "I have spread this out for you like eight characters; why do you refuse to accept it? The Master replied, "Stop trying to be so obtuse."
Fenyi said, "Come closer and I shall speak for you. The Master immediately covered his ears and departed. Fenyi nodded in approval and ordered him to serve as the attendant for incense.
He subsequently served as the Librarian at Longxiang Monastery. In the second year of the Zhishun era, he first took up residence at the Patriarchs’ Hall of Niushou.

He was later transferred to Shicheng, Qingliang, Baoning, and Jiangshan. By imperial decree, Longxiang was renamed Tianjie, and the Emperor issued an edict appointing the Master as its abbot, specifically bestowing upon him the title of Yan...
The Great Chan Master Chongjiao of Fanzhenshi Li Country ascended the hall. "A single phrase," he said, "is pitch black;

it has no handle, yet it possesses a standard. After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand? The pestle pounds in the southeast; the millstone grinds in the northwest. He ascended the hall again:
"Before the Peak of Shaoshi and beneath the gate of Caoxi, the lamps have been passed down one after another, transmitted with absolute clarity from antiquity to the present day."
It is not at all difficult. Furthermore, what serves as the proof? Above and below the pavilions, fire illuminates fire;
carriages and horses pass to and fro, and people look upon people. Entering the hall, he said: "The tall have the long Dharma-body; the short have the short Dharma-body.

Right now, this entire assembly is sitting and standing with solemn dignity—some are tall, some are short. Everyone knows it and everyone sees it. But ultimately, which one among you is [the Dharma-body]?"
The Dharmakāya. If you can realize this, you will hold up your alms bowl and go to the world of Gandhavyūha to eat rice.

If you cannot realize it, you shall simply eat gruel and rice upon your long, continuous couch. Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "The Sūtras have masters of the Sūtras; the Śāstras have masters of the Śāstras.
Today, I, the Dragon River, let loose a single thread to divide the sections and arrange the chapters. He took up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said: "Tell me, is this..."
What sutra passage? [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "This very present case is one that many among the assembly have understood, yet not a few have misunderstood.
Consequently, gold and brass are not distinguished, and jade and stone are not differentiated.
Here at Longhe, I must distinguish them clearly: Elder Zhang and Elder Li—one has long arms, the other has large eyes. Altogether..."
"Like the single school of Bodhidharma today, what person can be entrusted with this burden? He let out a long sigh and descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja and after Maitreya Buddha, there is a ready-made public case that I dare not break open for you.
Why? Because the heart bears no grudge against others, and the face shows no shame. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The spring wind sweeps vast; the spring days..."
Slowly, slowly. The oriole sings upon the branches of a hundred flowers. Within this, there is boundless meaning; who knows its message?

Before he had finished speaking, a monk stepped forward and asked, "When the mind, intellect, and consciousness cannot be suppressed, what then? The Master said in a stern voice, "Who is it that suppresses them?
He then said to the monk within the room, "During the twelve periods of the day, there is no time for you to peck and snatch; there is no place for you..."

"Regarding the section on 'Tending Toward': do you understand? The monks were at a loss for a response. The Master said, "If one has not yet clarified three eights and nine, it is difficult to avoid self-murmuring.
In the third year of the Hongwu era, he was commissioned as an envoy to the Western Regions and arrived at the kingdom of Siṃhala (Sri Lanka). Its king served him at the Fo-shan Vihāra.
In the ninth month of the following year, he passed away and was interred alongside the Pratyekabuddha Stūpa. Previously, that Buddha had made a prophetic prediction.

The current opening of the grave for the enshrinement coincides exactly with his words. The Minister of Personnel submitted a memorial, and the Emperor issued an edict granting him a set of funeral robes and permitting burial to the left of Huayuantai.

at twenty, he received full ordination (*upasampadā*). One day, Xiaoyin asked: "The National Teacher called out three times, and the attendant responded three times."
"What do you think? the Master asked. "How can you cut flesh and create sores? Yun said, "I thought you were extraordinary; now it turns out there is nothing to be gained. The Master gave a shout.
As Yun prepared to raise his staff, the Master swept his sleeves and departed. Later, at the end of the Yuan dynasty, Yun resided at Mount Jing;
in the first year of the Hongwu era, he took up residence at Zhongzhu and ascended the hall to preach: "The Diamond King’s sword is brandished horizontally; a thousand demons..."

He withdraws his traces. Śakrāloka’s eyes penetrate and illuminate; though the myriad things hide their forms, when one reaches this state, rolling up and unfolding are within oneself, and killing or giving life are applied according to the occasion.

He resided at Zhizhu Temple during the Phoenix’s Nest era. In the fourth year of the Hongwu reign, he moved to Mount Jing. By imperial decree, all eminent monks of learning and conduct from throughout the realm were summoned;
the Master was the first to respond to the summons and arrived. His responses to the Emperor’s inquiries met with the Sovereign’s approval, and he was ordered to reside at Tianjie Temple.

In the fifth year, the Emperor established a Great Memorial Service at Mount Jiangshan and personally performed the three-fold offering ritual. He commanded the Master to compose the musical lyrics for the ceremony and summoned him to attend.

He gathered the spirits of the deceased and commanded the Master to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma. In the winter of the tenth year, an imperial edict was issued for the Master to provide annotated commentaries on the *Heart Sūtra*, the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, and the *Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra*.
In the year Ding-si, he was appointed as an envoy to the Western Regions. In the fifteenth year, upon his return to court, he was granted the title of Right Street Overseer of the Sangha (*Shanshi*).
He was further commanded to grow out his hair and be invested with a Confucian office; the Master respectfully obeyed the command, and when his hair had grown long, the Emperor—
The Emperor summoned him to appoint him as an official, but Master Shi declined twice. The Emperor then followed his request. Later, Master Shi was censured for being associated with the Hu faction;
he resided at Chaya Peak in Fengyang for nineteen years before returning to Yue. Five years later, he was granted leave to retire due to old age.
Upon crossing the river at Shifo Temple in Jiangpu, he manifested illness and called to his attendant, saying: "What about this?"
The other was bewildered. The Master said, "Suffering," and then passed away. He was enshrined in a stupa behind that of Master Xun at Tianjie.
Chan Master Chongyu of Yuan Tong in Jiuyang Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of Pilin.
At the age of sixteen, he followed Master Xiao of Donglin at Shouchang Temple as a śrāmaṇera. After receiving full ordination, he first studied under Yuansou Duan, and subsequently visited...

The Master replied, "The one who prostrates is not another. Xiaoyin said, "One who enters through the gate is not [the true person]."
Jia Zhen said, "Master, please do not deceive people. Yinsou consented by nodding his head. He remained with Xiaoyin for over ten years.
Initially, he resided at Nanchan, and subsequently at Yuan Tong, where he renovated it;

it was completed in no time, just as it coincided with the prophecy of the Ancient Buddha Min that the Dharma would flourish greatly three hundred years later. He further moved to Yuyang, restoring its ruins as well.
In the autumn of the fifth year of Hongwu, the Emperor established a Dharma assembly at Mount Zhong.

The Master was summoned to the Private Audience Hall (*biandian*), where the Emperor questioned him on the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma. The Master offered a verse in response, which greatly pleased the Emperor; he was granted a meal.

During the audience, the Master occasionally dozed off, and the sound of his breathing could be faintly heard. A fellow monk sitting nearby pulled his robe to wake him. The Emperor laughed and said, "This old man..."
He was free from worldly attachments; he was truly a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). Later, he passed away and was interred in a stupa on Shier Peak.
Xiaoyin once remarked that, in terms of the strict purity of his precepts and the consistency between his words and deeds, Chongyu alone was his equal.
Chan Master Yongzhen Fuliang of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Wuxian County in Suzhou. He was a tenth-generation descendant of Lord Wen Zhengfan.
At the age of fifteen, he received the tonsure and full ordination at Ying Chan Monastery, whereupon he declared: "I study the Buddha-dharma in order to clarify the mind."

The mind cannot be shown its essential subtleties without a teacher. He went to study the Tiantai teachings under Dharma Master Ze of Beichen, whereupon he felt a profound sense of resonance as if he had attained some realization.
Later, when the scholar Zhan met with Master Baoshu, he was encouraged to change his robes and enter the practice of Chan. Baoshu directed him to visit Xiaoyin;
upon seeing him, Xiaoyin recognized his potential. During their dialogue, Xiaoyin employed both the staff and shouts, and in an instant, all ordinary delusions were suddenly cast away.
On another day, Yinyou asked further questions, but the Master’s words became increasingly severe. Yinyou laughed and said, "You have attained it, indeed;
yet you remain at the level of the second meaning. After some time, he finally realized the essence of the Mind School (*cittadharmatā*).

He then went to Yuyang (Sima) at Mount Siming to study under Shishi Ying, where he engaged in vigorous and penetrating exchanges. Shishi highly praised him, and he subsequently took up residence at Zisheng Monastery in Jiaxing before moving to Yue.
This celestial chapter was moved from Zhongzhu in Hangzhou to Lingyin, where he addressed the assembly: "The single school of Bodhidharma has declined until it is nearly extinct.
You must exert yourselves as if your heads were on fire. Nevertheless, there are hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable subtle meanings."
One can come to know [all things] completely upon the tip of a single hair. If you know this, you may transform the great earth into gold and accept it without hesitation;
otherwise, you will incur the shame of being a "white-feeder" (one who consumes the fruits of others' labor without contributing). Time flows like a flash of lightning;

you must urgently cultivate yourselves toward the higher goal. On the fifteenth day of the first month in the fourth year of Hongwu, I personally wrote this letter and donated my clothing and possessions.
He distributed the public funds to his friends and for the funeral arrangements. Looking at those around him, he said, "I expect my passing will occur at the hour of Si (10–11 a.m.).
When the time arrived, he requested a bath, sat upright, and entered into stillness.
Chan Master Qingyuan Huaweï of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Wei family of Nanchang and the nephew of Xiaoyin.
At his birth, a miraculous *lingzhi* fungus grew from a courtyard catalpa tree. He soon displayed exceptional brilliance; he could recite the classics without waiting for instruction from a teacher.
At that time, Xiaoyin was residing at Longxiang Temple. Upon hearing of this, he said with joy, "This is a 'thousand-li colt' of our school. He invited him to join the assembly at his seat. Long...
Xiang was a metropolitan center of the southeast, where eminent scholars from all quarters frequented with the recluses.

Some revealed the secrets of human nature and destiny, while others expounded the methods of literary composition and the opening of the gates of eloquence; the Master was able to hear these teachings, whereby his learning advanced greatly.
Everyone vied to admire him, saying, "This is a tiger among writers. The Master said, "Do you gentlemen think that I am one who specializes solely in this craft? As for the Buddha-dharma..."
He does not contradict worldly dharmas; therefore, he employs his remaining strength to assist them, merely to bring luster and refinement to their religious teachings.

The Master stepped forward and spoke bluntly. Yunzhin shook his staff and let out a single shout; the Master’s spirit was not the least bit dampened.
After they had exchanged challenges and refutations back and forth, Yunzhin said with a smile, "You may enter my chamber. He appointed him as the Record Keeper (Jishi).

As Yunzhin approached death, he summoned the Master and said, "I have occupied this master's seat for over forty years. The people I have encountered have been numerous indeed, yet it is you who can propagate the Way of Dahui so that it does not fall into decline."
"None but you and Zongle [are worthy]. You must be diligent! Later, he presided over Baoxiang in Kuaiji, Baoguo in Hangzhou, and Daochang on Lake (West Lake).
At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he presided over Jingci Monastery. Responding to an imperial decree, he entered the capital; upon his return, he retired to Liangzhu in Qiantang.
In the twelfth month of the eighth year, he summoned his disciples to entrust them with his final affairs, remaining serene."
He entered nirvana on the sixteenth day of this month. There were three items that remained indestructible during the cremation:
his teeth and jawbone, his *pāṣāṇa* (stone) bowl, and his *śrīphala* (mango) bowl. These were enshrined in a stupa at Liangzhu.
Chan Master Gudong Mingde of Daochang Monastery in Anji Prefecture was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zhutan Lin. His surname was Zhu, and his family lineage hailed from Changguo in Mingzhou.
His father was a friend of Puto Jiao; having heard the sound of a rooster, Jiao entered the Way, and whenever he preached the Dharma, he would invariably flap his wings.
When the cock crowed, Jie had already been dead for some time. His mother dreamed that he came to stay with her as a guest; upon waking, she became pregnant. After fourteen months, a child was born.

While still a young child, he delighted in sitting in the lotus posture (*paryaṅka*). When asked what he sought to achieve, he replied, "I wish to study seated meditation (*zuo chan*) and seek to become a Buddha.
At the age of twelve, he entered Jing’e Monastery to become a monk. Five years later, he received full ordination (*upasampadā*). He then felt a profound sense of resolve and sought [the Way].
As for Daozhi’s intent: he first went to visit Zhixi. Zhixi asked, "From where have you come? The Master replied, "I come from Mount Jing'e.
Zhixi asked, "How high is Mount Jing'e? The Master replied, "Its summit cannot be seen. Zhixi rebuked him. One day, Zhixi raised the story of the World-Honored One holding up a flower.
Suddenly, the Master felt he had attained an understanding; he composed a verse and presented it to him. Zhixi approved of it, and he was further purified.
Ciji saw Huizhi. Huizhi asked, "Who is it that comes like this? The Master replied, "Hū Zhangsan and Hē Lisi.
Huizhi said, "From morning until evening, while you are putting on clothes and eating food, do you still recognize yourself?
The Master replied, "Hū Zhangsan and Hē Lisi. Huizhi raised his staff. The Master shook out his sleeves and departed, going to see Mingji Jun. Huizhi—

His words were in perfect accord with the Dharma, and he was summoned to serve in the administrative office. Shortly thereafter, he presided over the Zanghui Hall. Later, Mingji traveled to Japan, while the Master arrived at Xuedou.
There, he encountered Zhutian ascending the hall to cite the story of Yishan’s “clay ox entering the sea. At that moment, the Master’s many doubts were suddenly resolved.
He presented his realization to Tian, who said, "The eyes of humanity and heaven are clearly present here. Subsequently, the Master resided at Songjiang.
He moved again to Baoning, where he resided for fifteen years. After three further moves between monasteries, he was appointed to Jingci Temple.

At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he declined the appointment and returned to his Zhalin Hermitage at Daochang. On the second day of the second month of the fifth year, he manifested a slight ailment;
on the twenty-seventh day, he entered nirvana.
Chan Master Gaofeng Yuanmiao of West Tianmu Mountain in Hangzhou was a successor of Chan Master Yangshan Qin. He was the son of the Xu family from Wujiang in Suzhou.
At the age of fifteen, he left home to become a monk at Miyin Temple in Xiushui. He first studied under Duangqiao and subsequently visited Xueyan at Beijian. In Huai... [text fragment ends]

Jiawu could not answer. Yanguan asked, "Why can you not hit it? The Master shook his sleeves and left. One day, Yanguan asked, "In the midst of the vast bustle of the day, can you maintain mastery?
The Master replied, "I maintain mastery. He asked, "In the midst of sleep and dreams, can you maintain mastery?
The Master replied, "I maintain mastery. He asked, "When one is fast asleep—without dreams, without thoughts, without seeing, and without hearing—who is the master?"

As soon as he awoke from sleep, he shook off his drowsiness and looked within: "In this single awakening, where exactly does the master reside to establish his life?
Thereupon, the Master resolved to enter Longxu. Five years later, because a monk pushed a pillow off the ground and it made a sound, he attained great enlightenment.
He subsequently moved to Shuangji. In the spring of the Jimao year of the Deyou era, he entered Xitian.
He looked toward Lion Rock (Sijwa Seonyeom) and immediately constructed a small chamber about one *jang* square within a stone cave, naming it the "Gate of Death" (Sigwan).

As the cave could not be ascended without a ladder, he removed the ladder and severed all means of access; thus, even his disciples rarely had the opportunity to behold him. He then set forth the discourse on the Three Barriers (Samgwan) to test his students, saying:

"A person of ultimate penetration is fundamentally liberated from birth and death. For what reason, then, is their life-root (*myeonggun*) not yet severed? This is the public matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs."
In truth, it is simply one principle. Why, then, is there clarity and lack of clarity? A great practitioner of the Way ought to follow the Buddha’s conduct;
why, then, do you not observe the *vinaya*? When your words did not accord with the truth, I closed my door and would not receive you.

When meaning and phrasing both reach [the truth], and the essence and the teaching both penetrate, one is like a blind turtle or a lame tortoise. Xifeng makes this announcement: is there anything else that arises apart from this?"

An iron snake drills into the Diamond Eye; Kunlun rides an elephant led by a heron. Within these four lines, there is one line that can kill and can give life.
Alive! He can bestow and he can take away. If you can discern this, I grant that your lifelong study of Zen is complete.
Taking his leave of the assembly, [Xifeng] said: "For thirty years I have spoken falsely of Prajñā; my offenses fill the heavens.
In the end, there is one phrase that I dare not burden others with—I shall carry it off myself. "Does the assembly know where it lands? After a long silence, he said: "A single hair..."

There was a slight difference [in his demeanor]. Heaven and earth were as far apart as could be. He composed a verse which said: "Coming, he did not enter the Death Barrier; going, he did not exit the Death Barrier.
An iron snake drills into the sea, knocking down Mount Sumeru. He passed away peacefully. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the Death Barrier.
He lived to the age of fifty-eight, having received the full precepts at forty-three.
Chan Master Chiding of Lingyun Iron Ox in Hengzhou was the son of Wang of Taihe in Jixian.
At the age of thirty-one, he visited Chan Master Ken’an Qin and shaved his head; he subsequently followed Xueyan at the fodder shed to practice the dhūta ascetic virtues.

Xingyan addressed the assembly, saying, "Brothers, if you practice with such diligence that for seven days and nights your single thought is uninterrupted and your eyes do not blink, yet you find no point of entry, then take this old monk’s head and make it into a latrine scoop! The Master [Xuedou] silently grasped the meaning.
Not long after, he contracted dysentery; he took a washbasin and sat upright upon it in a secluded spot, focusing his mind solely on the *Nian* (Recitation).
Maintaining right mindfulness, he did not close his eyes for seven days and nights until they were nearly half over.

Suddenly, he perceived that the mountains, rivers, great earth, grasses, trees, and forests throughout the entire world were like the bright moon shining under a clear sky; his own person stood majestic and imposing, such that heaven and earth could not contain it.

After a long while, as if hearing the sound of wood being struck, he was startled into realization. Sweat poured from his entire body and his illness was cured. He leaped for joy, celebrating his own good fortune.
He did not stop there. Early on, he went to the Abbot’s quarters and presented the case to Yan. Yan questioned him by citing the *gong'an*, and his responses were unhindered.
He further composed a verse, saying: "What is this brilliant and numinous awareness? In the blink of an eye, it has already been missed. The tally-stick by the latrine emits radiance;
Directly beneath, it has always been none other than myself. In the Wuyin year of the Zhiyuan era, he was ordained as a monk. Furthermore, [he] rested his side...
For six years, he did not even touch his mat. One day, while on the mountain peak, the Master ascended the hall and raised the question:

"When a deceased monk has died and been cremated, where does he go? He offered this in his own place of response: "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth—these fully reveal the body of the Dharma King.
The Master then went to the abbot’s quarters and said, "Just now the Abbot expounded upon Prajñā; it has startled the stone lion in front of the Dharma Hall so much that it is laughing and dancing!"

[Zhao] Yan did not stop. Yan said, "Try to say something. The Master said: "The spring wind beyond the kalpas withers all things; mountains, rivers, and the great earth are not a single speck of dust.
How can one express the Dharma-body that transcends all? It makes the blue-eyed barbarian of the Western Heaven laugh to his heart's content.
Yan struck the table in front of him and asked, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are not a single speck of dust—what is this? The Master gave a shove and knocked it over.
Shiyan laughed and said, "One throw, two bets. When the Master entered the room, Shiyan asked, "Bring me a single phrase regarding the point of intimacy.
The Master said, "I will not speak. Shiyan asked, "Why do you not speak? The Master picked up the incense box in his hand and said, "This thing is not worth half a coin.
Shiyan said, "A talkative fellow. Later, while the Master was making a circuit of the hall, Shiyan...
The Master was sleeping with a paper quilt wrapped around his body. When Yunyan summoned him to the abbot’s quarters, he said in a stern voice, "While I was inspecting the hall, you were fast asleep.

If you can speak a word of Dharma, I shall let you go; if you cannot, I will drive you down the mountain. The Master replied spontaneously: "Last night I dreamed I was a king; today I am a commoner. (昨夜夢為帝王 今日却作田舍翁)
The iron ox has no strength and is too lazy to plow the fields; wearing its rope, it sleeps amidst the mud and snow.
The great earth and white clouds completely cover all, leaving no place for Deshan to lower his golden whip. Yan remarked, "What a fine iron ox! and thus he took that as his title.
Later, while residing at Lingyun, he propagated the Way of Xueyan. In the winter of the Great Virtue (Dade) year of Renyin, he wrote this long verse for the assembly; its conclusion was as follows:

He said, "The mundane world is not permanent; it is worn away day by day and month by month. After thirty years, a single branch from the Peach Blossom Spring will flow forth—a flute with no holes—to play the song of Great Peace. Next spring, I shall pass into extinction. When his attendant monk requested words of parting for the assembly, he replied: The original text is: 曰。塵世非久。日消月磨。桃源一脉。三十年後。流出一枝無孔笛。吹起太平歌。明春將示寂。侍僧求別眾語。 Translation: He said, "The dusty world is not enduring; it is eroded day by day and month by month.

From a single stream of the Peach Blossom Spring, after thirty years, there shall emerge a branch—a flute without holes—to blow forth the song of Great Peace. Next spring, I shall manifest my passing into extinction. His attendant monk then requested words of farewell for the assembly.
The Master said, "It has been a long time since we parted. He then sat peacefully and passed away.
Chan Master Xugu Hiling of Jingshan, whose courtesy name was Xibai, was the son of the He family of Yiwu.

His family was poor, yet he applied himself to his studies with great diligence, remaining the same in both winter and summer. In his youth, he dreamed that he entered the Hall of Arhats at Jingci Temple; when he reached the southeast corner, suddenly—
The Venerable One pointed to a poem between the rafters and showed it to the Master, saying: "A single chamber, vast and silent, opens at the mountain peak;
several peaks like paintings, their blue surpassing that of moss. Having casually finished turning the *pātra* leaves, one cuts and sews the hundred-patch *kāṣāya* oneself.
From this, he developed the resolve to leave secular life. At the age of nineteen, he shaved his head at Zishou Monastery in Dongyang and relied upon Dong-sou Ying at Jingci Monastery.
He served as the inner recorder (*neiji*) for Shilin Gong; concurrently served as the outer recorder (*waiji*). He attended Xueyan Qin at Yangshan, where he managed the library keys.
Later, while relying on Yunfeng Gao at Mount Jing, he again managed the library keys. Subsequently, he was appointed to share the seat (*fenzuo*) and preach the Dharma.

Throughout his career, he successively moved through various positions until reaching Yangshan. Emperor Yuan Shizu summoned him for an audience; his preaching met with imperial approval, and he was granted the title "Fujian" (Buddha-Mirror). Emperor Chengzong further [honored him].
He was titled Dayuan (Great Circle). By imperial decree, he was appointed to reside at Mount Jing. Emperor Renzong further bestowed upon him the title Huizhao (Wisdom Illumination).

On the twelfth day of the fourth month of the *wuxu* year of the Zhizheng era, he wrote a final testament by hand, delivered his parting instructions, and recited a verse before passing away. He was posthumously honored with the title Dabian (Great Eloquence), and his stupa was named Baohua (Precious Flower).
His *Puyuan ji* (Collected Works from the Waterfall Cliff) and his recorded sayings (*yulu*) were circulated in the world.

Chan Master Juexiang Jian, a successor of Chan Master Lun of Jingci, once composed a verse on the karmic conditions concerning Dongshan’s illness, which says: "The path of Dongshan leads through Yunyan;

At the point where it is severed, it is difficult for those who arrive to pass through. Only when one opens a living path at the tip of the staff Does one know that there is not even a single barrier."
At the tip of a hair. Furthermore, a verse on National Teacher Yan’s visit at the Great King’s invitation, with Xuefeng seeing him off at the gate, says:
"The celestial cave has no walls, the moon has no obstruction; the Master of the Morning Star knocks his teeth together. The wind shakes the ancient altar and pine seeds fall;
it knocks over the paper crown on his head, tilting it askew. Furthermore, a verse on the assembly at Letan asking Mazu about the meaning of the Westward Journey says: "The sound of roosters..."
The moonlight shines bright upon the thatched inn; the traveler’s dream is so deep he has not yet awakened. When his eyes open, the sky is already wide dawn;
with disheveled hair and a grime-stained face, he sets off on his journey.
Chan Master Zhuyu Jian composed a verse on Drum Mountain’s “Holy Arrow,” saying: “The young lad double-reins his jade-steed as it neighs; A pale white spring robe is encircled by a green sash.
Returning at midnight beneath the flowers and the moon, The golden whip strikes down a flight of scattered red petals.
He also said: “The Ninefold City is not distant at all; Shooting through layer after layer, the arrows are more than enough. Suddenly encountering the siege of two armies...”
At the place of circumambulation, there is a clearly defined path leading straight to the heavens. A verse on Touzi pointing to the rain and showing it to the monks:
"The sky and sun bring fine rain; amidst the fragrance of a hundred flowers, the partridge cries. The fair-faced young man is drunk as mud. Under the blazing sunlight, he opens his eyes;
at the eastern edge of Fucheng, the grass grows lush and green."

Chan Master Yuetting Chung, a successor of Chan Master Wuxue Yuan, once composed a verse on Kāśyapa’s expulsion of Mañjuśrī, which says: "The silk-clad young lord is accustomed to wandering through spring;
The white-haired beauty harbors much regret. Though wealthy, he still laments his household is too small; Being poor himself, he can do nothing for his single person."
What? Furthermore, when a monk asked Baizhang, "The old year has already passed and the new year has arrived;
what is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? He replied: "Falling leaves have followed the flowing water away; The spring breeze has not yet caused the hundred flowers to bloom.
The face of the green mountain remains as it was; All day long it lies across, facing the setting sun."

Chan Master Duanya Miaoen of Kaiyuan Monastery in Quanzhou was a dharma heir of Chan Master Xuefeng Xiang. He was the son of the Ni family from Quanzhou. Having initially traveled extensively to study under renowned masters, he subsequently entered the quarters of Master Xuefeng Xiang.
