That evening, while conversing and laughing with his Zen students until the late hours of the night, he said, "The old monk is going to Tiantai tomorrow.
A student said, "I will follow my teacher. The Master replied, "Even if you were to gallop like a horse, you could not catch up with me. At noon the following day—
He passed away while sitting in the full lotus posture. His lifespan was seventy-two years and forty-nine *lǎ* (years).

During the initial funeral feast held at Zhongfeng after his passing, the Master smiled and said to the assembly, "Twelve years from now, there shall be another gathering for this old monk. This present moment marks exactly twelve years since that statement.
He was posthumously granted the title Great Master Fohui Yuanming Zhengjue Pudu. His disciples then followed the Master’s [final instructions].
A stupa was erected at the spot where he pointed.
Chan Master Zuyong of Budana Temple on Mount Tianmu in Hangzhou was a native of Ninghai in Mingzhou.

Having received the essential instruction from Gaofeng, he personally attended to the tasks of gathering firewood and cooking; his appearance was very dark and emaciated, and he was blunt with little literary refinement. He once composed verses in response to Yongming...

A Verse on Dwelling in the Mountains: I wish to extinguish my mind; I shall simply let it turn to ash. Why need I seek out a skilled matchmaker? At the crossroads of a thousand differences, I shut every gate;
at the pivot of ten thousand diversities, I sever every mechanism. I build a dwelling by binding reeds to trees;
I open a cottage by weaving thorn branches beside the stream. This is the lazy Zan, who lacks spiritual efficacy, yet he has provoked the Celestial Writings to come three times.
It is further said: "In ordinary times, cold understanding knows itself to be wrong; Retreating, one leaves no trace, dwelling amidst the green mists.

Sweeping away the hundred-year dream of honor and shame, One turns back to the original faculty of many kalpas. Ants crawl up the steps seeking their burrows; Butterflies fly through the gardens seeking flowers.
One must believe that from the heavens above to the earth below, Every single thing has a true home. The First Crane.
Shagong Gongting built a temple for Gaofeng at the foot of Lotus Peak and requested that it be named Dajue Peak (Great Enlightenment Peak), entrusting the Master with its administration.
When Gaofeng passed away, he assumed the position of abbot. Later, he moved to Zhongzhu. Once, a rosary was carried off by a crow;
the following day, the crow returned it, carrying it back. No one among the assembly failed to marvel at this. One day, while free from illness, he wrote:
He composed a verse, sat peacefully among the assembly, and passed away.

At White Clouds (Baiyun) in Chuzhou, Jia Chan Master received the Dharma from Gao Feng; he later resided at White Cloud Mountain, where Zen practitioners from all directions heard of his reputation and came to visit until the doors were filled with those waiting outside.
On one day in the summer of the *wuchen* year of the Zhizhi era (*1276*), he took up his brush.
He wrote a verse, saying: "Earth, water, fire, and wind were predicted by the former Buddhas; dig deep into the earth and bury [the remains] according to the primary truth (*paramārtha*).

First, this will spare the donor from needing more firewood; second, it will spare one from the talk of others that there are no *śarīra*. Having spoken thus, he sat cross-legged and passed into stillness.
Chan Master Jue Xue Shicheng of Bore Monastery in Hongzhou, a successor of Chan Master Lingyun Ding, addressed the assembly:

"Brothers, if you have been practicing for three or five years without finding an entry point, do not cast aside the previous *hwadu*. You must realize that you may have traveled halfway along the path and [abandoned it]."

Futile! It is a pity that so much mental effort has been expended thus far. A person of true resolve, seeing that firewood is dry, water is available, and the monks’ hall is warm within the assembly, should make a vow not to leave their door for three years; they will certainly find a way to experience realization.

There are those who, as soon as they apply themselves to practice and their minds become pure, immediately encounter objects appearing before them and construct four conceptual propositions, taking these to be [the truth].
A person of great potential has been brought to ruin by a quick mouth and a glib tongue for an entire lifetime. When the three inches of breath have faded, what will you rely upon?
If a son of the Buddha wishes to transcend, his investigation must be a genuine investigation; his awakening must be a genuine awakening.
Chan Master Jin Shao Da of Yun Huangshan Baolin and Tongjiang was a dharma successor of Chan Master Ling of Jingshan. He was originally from Tongjiang in Yan.
His surname was Wu. In his youth, he entered Fengshan Temple as a śrāmaṇera. After receiving full ordination, he first traveled to the Double Peak (Shuangjing) to pay his respects.
Xugu attained the essence of the single transmission. After a long time, he took his leave and traveled to consult various renowned masters.
He then remarked, "From this day forward, I know that the Dharma has no differing flavors. He returned once more to Mount Jing. At that time, Dongyu Hai was propagating the Way at Jingci Monastery;

he invited the Master to preside over the Tripitaka Library. Every night, he would spread mats upon the ground and, by the light of the lamp before the Buddha, read through the Great Canon. This continued until the third...
He eventually mastered the full intent of the teachings. In the *Renshen* year of the *Zhishun* era (1252), he appeared in the world at Wolong Temple in Yan.
Later, he moved to Baolin Temple in Zhiyi’s tradition. On the seventh day of the eighth month of the *Jihai* year (1279), he gathered the assembly to bid them farewell.

When the congregation requested that he write a verse, the Master took up his brush, threw it to the ground, and said, "Even if I were to write until Maitreya descends to be born in this world, would I ever leave this place? Thereupon, he passed away with serene composure.
The *śarīra* relics from the cremation were the color of deep blue pearls; his teeth and rosary remained unbroken.
Chan Master Zhuyuan Zhengyuan of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was the son of the Ouyang clan of Nankang.

At the age of twenty-seven, he first received full ordination. He initially went to visit Xugou, who questioned him with the "Longtan Extinguishing the Paper Candle" koan. The Master replied, "It is burnt."
Stone may be shattered, and layered ice may be broken. Gu said, "After it is broken, what is there to do? The Master replied, "One knows through exploration.
Gu asked, "What is it that is known? As the Master was about to answer, Gu struck him. The Master was startled and understood in silence. Later, he presided over five great monasteries.
While he was residing at Lingyin, it was ravaged by fire; yet the place where the Master lived alone remained intact, as if protected by divine intervention.
During his tenure at Mount Jing, he was granted the title Chan Master Fohui Cizhao Puying.

In the sixth month of the twelfth year of the Zhizheng era, as he was about to pass away, he announced the date in advance, wrote a verse, and entered nirvana. His entire body was enshrined in a stupa on Mount Jing. His disciples...
When his fingernails and hair were cut and buried in various places, śarīras sprang up in clusters everywhere. Such are the accounts of his numinous wonders.

As for Chan Master Shiwu Qinggong of Fuyuan Temple in Jiaxing Prefecture, he was a successor of Chan Master Xinxin of the Daochang Monastery and was born to the Wen family of Wenshu in Suzhou. He relied upon...
He entered the monastic order at Kōkyō Shōfuku-ji Temple on Honshū. At the age of twenty, he shaved his head and received full ordination.
Later, he first visited Kōkō, who gave him the koan "The myriad dharmas return to one. He served him diligently for three years. Subsequently, while residing at Saikyō-ji in Jōyō, he visited Jakuan.
Zhao’an asked, “Where have you come from? The Master replied, “From Tianmu. Zhao’an asked, “What instruction did you receive there?
The Master replied, “All dharmas return to the One. Zhao’an asked, “How do you understand this? The Master was speechless. Zhao’an said, “This is a dead word.
What kind of feverish delusion has possessed you to make you speak like that? The Master bowed and requested further guidance. Zhao’an said, “Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell.”
"When there is no Buddha, run past quickly. "What is the meaning of this? The Master replied, but it did not accord with the Abbot's intent. The Abbot said, "This too is a dead word.
The Master was suddenly overcome with perspiration and sought to become his attendant. Later, when he entered the room for instruction, the Abbot again questioned him using the previous dialogue.
The Master said, "One sees the road while on horseback. The Abbot rebuked him, saying, "After six years here, you still hold such a view!"
The Master, filled with indignation, abandoned his studies and departed. On the road, he suddenly raised his head and saw Fengting (Maple Pavilion);
at that moment, he attained a sudden realization. Returning, he said to Guoan, "To not dwell where there is a Buddha is a dead word;
to hurry past where there is no Buddha is also a dead word. Today I have understood the living word. Guoan asked, "How do you understand it? The Master replied:
On the Qingming festival, the rain had just cleared. A yellow oriole sang clearly upon a branch. Chan’an nodded his head.
After a long while, the master took his leave. As Chan’an saw him off at the gate, he said, "In the future, we shall share the same shrine.

Not long after, when Chan’an arrived at Daochang on Lake Hu, the Master visited him again and was appointed to the position of Librarian. Later, he established a hermitage at Tianhu and, in the Xunwei year of the Yuantong era, resided at Danghu.
Fuyuan ascended the hall. When he restrains [the mind], not even a trace of its sharp edge is revealed; when he lets it go, the ten directions are traversed in all their breadth.
Meeting in the depths of water and clouds, one is instead atop a thousand peaks; meeting atop a thousand peaks, one is instead in the depths of water and clouds.
Today, within Fuyuan Temple, the hall is opened and the Dharma is expounded; yesterday, by the side of Tianhu Hermitage, the earth was tilled.

The smoke of the plow. This is why the Dharma has no fixed location; when conditions meet, one takes that as the source. Thus, the wind of true stillness can be transmitted, and one may look up to assist in the transformation of non-action.
At such a time, how is it? [He] struck the meditation staff and said: "A nine-myriad-li peng-bird has just spread its wings;
a thousand-year-old crane soars even higher. On New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said: "Jingqing says, 'At the head of the new year, there is a Buddha.'"
The Dharma exists. The clear teaching says that at the beginning of the new year, the Buddha-Dharma does not exist. To say it exists does not necessarily mean it exists;
to say it does not exist does not necessarily mean it does not exist. "When Mr. Zhang drinks wine, Mr. Li gets drunk. "Zhaozhou hangs a gourd on the eastern wall.
Entering the hall: eating is for ending hunger; drinking water is for ending thirst; wearing clothes is for avoiding cold; returning home is for arriving.

"Householder, if you would study the Way, you must reach the point where the Buddhas of the three periods cannot open their mouths; if you would practice Zen, you must reach the point where the patriarchs of the world have no foothold.

If it is not like this, you are merely leaning on others' gateways and huddling against others' walls, listening to the commands of others and swallowing the spittle of others—you are in no way a true man of spirit. When Fuyuan speaks thus, it is like bitter medicine."

Mouth. Loyal words are harsh to the ear. Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; the moonlight on the towers vanishes as the clouds withdraw.
Where there is no Buddha, pass by with haste; the lotus leaves in the pond are blown apart by the wind. Even when meeting people three thousand miles away, do not speak of this mistakenly.
The mountains of Langzhou and the waters of Lizhou—the four seas and five lakes are all within the Imperial Transformation. Pack the bag.
Wearing a thousand-ribbed bamboo hat on his head, whenever questioned, he would speak only of mountains and waters. Suddenly, one who was dissatisfied came forth and said:
"If the mountains simply speak of mountains and the waters simply speak of waters, what fault is there? After a long silence, [the Master] said: "One must not yet cast away one's whole heart;
when meeting people, speak only three parts of the truth. He resided there for seven years, then retired to Tianhu on Xawu Mountain. Upon arriving—

During his lifetime, the Imperial Court heard of the Master’s fame and sent down incense and silk offerings to honor his extraordinary character. The Empress bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered robe.
On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month in the autumn of the *renchen* year, he manifested his passing. As he bid farewell to the assembly, an attendant monk asked about his final affairs.
He then wrote a verse, saying: "The green mountains do not harbor stinking corpses; Once dead, why need one dig the earth to bury them? I, too, have no fire of samādhi;
A single pile of firewood, cutting off the past and ending the future. Having cast aside his brush, he passed away. His cremation produced relics of five colors, brilliant and beyond counting.
He was interred at the site of Tianhu, adjacent to the tomb of Pairyuan, to demonstrate that [the two were of one essence].
I have forgotten the record of our shared dwelling in the same niche. There was a disciple named Yu Taigu, a native of Goryeo, who personally received the Master’s instructions.
He once received the Master’s seal of approval through the teaching of a verse, which contained the line: "The golden scales ascend the straight hook. His king honored him as National Preceptor;

upon hearing that the Master had passed away, he submitted a memorial to the imperial court, by which decree the Master was posthumously titled Chan Master Foci Huizhao, and the king subsequently entered the mountains [to pay his respects].
The relics were divided and distributed, and stupas were erected in his home country.
Chan Master Tianzhen Weize of Haimen, Jiaxing Prefecture, was a dharma successor of Chan Master Kuangshan Yuan; he was the son of the Fei family of Huzhou. His mother dreamed of a strange monk...
While begging for alms, she became aware that she was pregnant. At dawn, a wondrous fragrance permeated the air.
Having left home as a child, she traveled extensively to consult eighteen venerable masters, including Chushi and Qianyan, yet in all cases her karmic conditions were not met.

Later, hearing of Chan Master Wujie Yuan of Mount Lu, she went directly to seek him out; however, Yuan likewise gave her no further inspiration. Subsequently, encountering Yuan in the latrine, she hurried toward him and questioned him.
[The Master] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Huairang seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment;
he simply shook his hand. Huairang asked, "Have you gained something? The Master replied, "How could there be anything to gain?

[Huairang] asked, "Do you understand it through intellectual reasoning? The Master brushed out his sleeves and departed. He subsequently served Huairang diligently for over a month, and day by day [his realization] increased.

The profound mystery was perfectly resolved when Master Shānlín Gōngzhào invited the Master to serve as the keeper of the treasury. Later, at the request of the assembly, he opened the gate to the ocean of Dharma.
Entering the hall, a monk asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? The Master said, "Seek it by looking downward.
The monk asked, "How does one seek it by looking downward? The Master said, "Do not touch it at all. The monk asked, "What happens after touching it? The Master said:
"I give you thirty blows," he said. "As for matters above and matters below, cut off both ends and cease clinging.
Suddenly let loose a 'tortoise-nosed snake'; only when it has bitten you to death will you know how difficult it is to escape. Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ!
Haimen, unable to restrain my impatience today, I have overstepped the bounds to deliver this message for all of you. Do you understand it thoroughly? Thus he spoke.
With his whisk, he made a single dot and said: "Casually cast down this elixir of life; a vast, pure wind stirs heaven and earth.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Three, three, three. Nine, nine, nine. At the sea gate, the sound of the tide roars like thunder.
Fragrance floats from the chrysanthemum garden as golden coins are offered; at Linggan Bridge, jade dogs appear. You have them too, and I have them too—turn the Southern Dipper around and look!"
The Northern Dipper. At such a time, ascending high to the peak of Haimen, one bursts open the azure void and scatters the white clouds.
How would you express the phrase for manifesting the marks of a Great Being and displaying great spiritual powers? Suddenly, assuming the form of an Asura upholding the sun and moon, he says:
"Swallowing and spitting out the void, upholding the sun and moon; throughout the Dharma-realm of the ten directions, this is the entire body. Flowers.
Ascending the hall in the morning: when the flowers bloom and the moon descends, divine immortals descend from the Palace of Flower Essences.
When the willows embrace the spring breeze, embroidered maidens walk amidst the clusters of silk. In the midst of bustling clamor, they manifest the ocean of nature of Vairocana;

in the midst of profound stillness, they bury the practice-gate of Samantabhadra. At such a time as this, tell me: is the livelihood found in the bustle, or is it the livelihood found in the stillness?
Haimen was not so. After a long while, he snapped his fingers and said: "In the Tuṣita Heaven palace, they strike the precious desk;

in the world of Jambudvīpa, the golden bell resounds. At the beginning of the Hongwu era, he once participated in a grand memorial Dharma assembly, after which he was granted leave to return home due to foot ailments.
In the second month of spring in the year of Guiyou (1393), he manifested slight illness. One morning, he addressed the assembly, saying: "I am departing. His attendant requested a verse.
The Master said in a stern voice, "Is what I have usually taught not correct? He then closed his eyes and passed away. Upon cremation, countless *śarīra* relics were obtained;
his skull bone, teeth, and tongue remained intact. A stupa was erected at Fuyou Chan Monastery.
Chan Master Wujian Xiandu of Huading Peak at Tiantai was a dharma successor of Chan Master Ruiyan Bao. He was a native of the Ye clan of Xianju in Taizhou.

By nature he was exceptionally brilliant and fond of reading; he could recite from memory anything he saw once. He received the tonsure under Goutian Hou and subsequently attended upon Fangshan Bao. One day...
During his period of manual labor, [his doubts] dissolved completely like ice melting. Master Shan sealed this with a verse, saying: "This mind is utterly vast; even space cannot be compared to it.
This Way is just like this; uphold it and cease seeking elsewhere. Having received these instructions, the Master built a hut on Mount Huading.
He sat in meditation for forty years, never once crossing the threshold of his door.

Zen Master Nittō of Fōkō-ji was a successor of the Japanese National Teacher Musō Soseki of Tōsotsu-in; his secular surname was Minamoto, he was a native of Settsu Province, and [his posthumous title was] Uda...
He was the ninth-generation descendant of the Heavenly King (Emperor). His mother prayed to Guanyin and became pregnant after dreaming that she had swallowed golden light.
When he grew up, he painted the nine successive transformations of a corpse and sat alone in contemplation, realizing that the physical body is no different from flowers in the sky.

Moved by this realization, he conceived the aspiration to seek the Way. At eighteen, he became a monk and dreamed of traveling to the two monasteries of Shushan and Shitou in China, where he encountered a man with a bushy beard.
The monk held up an image of Bodhidharma and presented it to him. Upon waking, he said, "That which thoroughly illuminates my original mind is surely Zen meditation.
He first visited Wuyin Fan, and next visited Yishan Ning. Yishan said, "In our school, there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma to give to others.
The Master said, "I pray that the Honored One will compassionately provide the skillful means to instruct me. Yishan replied, "It is originally vast and empty."
However, Qingjing was compassionate and skillful, yet he too had none. The Master felt weary and despondent.
Seeing Dayong of Feng Peak at Mount Fohua, he went to him and made his request as before. Dayong asked, "What about Yishan? The Master recounted their exchange of questions and answers.
Dayong shouted fiercely, "Why do you not say that the Master has let slip no small amount? At these words, the Master attained realization. He took his leave and returned home.
Jiuyin was formerly a hermit at Changmushan. One night, after sitting for a long time, he happened to lean against a wall; suddenly, he collapsed and attained a sudden, great awakening.
He uttered the verse: "Casually shattering the very bones of empty space. Seeking confirmation from Xiqing, Xiqing said, "The secret meaning of the West has now been realized by you.
Guard and uphold it well. He established a hermitage in Nongzhou, where the King of the state commanded him to lead Nanzen-ten.
At the abode of the Dragon King and others, the Queen Mother invited him into the palace, where he received the rites of a disciple and questioned him.

She bestowed upon him the title "Perfectly Enlightened" (Zhengjue) and further conferred the title "Heart-Essence Universal Salvation" (Xinzong Pujì). She also sent him a letter, the gist of which read: "Your Way has vibrated through three reigns, and your fame has flown across the four seas.

You preside over the seat of the Deva-Dragon, turning the Wheel of Dharma once more; you wield the authority of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, crushing the fortresses of the demonic armies. Thus did the Master...
In his advanced years, he retired from public life and soon passed away.

Chan Master Fuguo Ruizhao of Kaiyuan was a successor of Chan Master Kaishan Zu of Kaiyuan; he was the son of the Cai family of Jinjiang and left the household life under Master Daofu at his own monastery.
At Kaiyuan Temple, they were united as one. Miaoen was the first generation master; the Master served him closely, and Miaoen held him in high esteem.

Subsequently, he traveled extensively to consult various masters, whereupon inner wisdom arose within him and he attained profound realization. He returned once more to Kaiyuan, and Miaoen honored him even more.

When Miaoen passed away, Zuzong succeeded to the abbacy and appointed the Master to oversee the Tripitaka library. In the eighth year of Dade, he took charge of the Rear Hall; in the tenth year, he moved...

In the front hall, following the passing of his predecessor, the Xuanzheng Yuan ordered the Master to fill the seat and succeed to the ancestral Dharma. Upon ascending the hall at Fucheng Monastery, [the Master said]:
"Snow fills the mountains; the stars turn in the heavens. To see once is to see; what need is there to wait another six years? Gautama, Gautama!
Without cause, you have led sentient beings to give rise to delusion—looking toward the Western Heaven from this Eastern Land. He further said: "Born in a snow pit..."

How fortunate and pitiable! For six years he never once loosened the seal of his mind. After the third watch, his eyelids burst open; had he revealed even a glimmer of light, it would have been intolerable.
Upon petition to the Emperor, he was granted the posthumous title of Buddha-Fruit Hongjue (Great Enlightenment). In the second year of the Zhishun era, he passed away suddenly and without illness.

Chan Master Shuzhong Wuyun of Ruiyan in Taizhou was a dharma successor of Chan Master Zituo Dao. He was the son of the Chen family of Linhai in Taizhou. At the age of seven, he entered the local school;
when reading, he required no more than a single instruction. Before reaching the age of twenty, he informed his parents that he wished to rely upon Chan Master Jizhao of Mount Jing for guidance.
The Master shaved his head and went to visit Zhuyuan with the koan regarding the dog having no Buddha-nature.

Before he had even broken through his doubts and as soon as he opened his mouth, he was met with a shout from Yuan, whereupon he attained great enlightenment. He presented a verse, saying: "The dog has no Buddha-nature; Spring colors fill the imperial capital."
"In Zhaozhou’s East Courtyard, a gourd hangs on the wall. Yuan [Zhaozhou] laughed aloud and said, "Even if you understand it this way, how can you attain it?
The Master [Fengxue] shook his sleeves and departed. Initially he resided at Lingyan in Mingzhou, then moved to Ruiyan. He ascended the hall;

when there was a question and an answer, it was like lighting a lamp beneath the sun. When there was no question and no answer, it was like cutting off the horns of a rabbit. This is a separate path, ten thousand miles from the precipice.
"State! Accept it directly! For now, proceed slowly. [The Master] picks up his staff, draws a line, and says:
"The heavens lean toward the southeast; the earth leans toward the northwest. Linji’s little servant possesses but a single eye. He plants his staff on the ground and lets out a shout.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The meaning of the Patriarchs is no different from this: when walking downstairs, one’s shoes are worn through; when sleeping upstairs in bed, one’s socks are pulled off.
To act just like this is far too absurd; not to act like this leaves nothing to be reconciled. The water buffalo of Mount Mui; the wild duck of Baizhang."
"Bearing water and dragging mud is not worth looking at; the halo behind the head is most brilliantly radiant. (He lets out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Chan Master Huanglong Xin, who was engaged in a profound discussion with Xia Gongli on the *Zhaolun*.

They were discussing how "the myriad things are one's own self" and that "sentient and insentient beings share a single body. At that time, a dog was lying beneath the incense table. Huanglong picked up his ruler and struck the dog.
The Master again struck the incense table and said, "The dog has sentience and thus departs; the incense table lacks sentience and remains still.
How can sentience and insentience become one body? Gao-li was unable to offer a rebuttal. Longshu said, "As soon as one engages in conceptual thought, it becomes a superfluous dharma.
When have you ever realized that all phenomena are oneself? This old fellow Huanglong lacks compassion."
Too little! Lord Xia stood up as if entering a mountain of treasure and returning empty-handed.

Do you all wish to understand how the myriad things are one's own self, such that the sentient and the insentient share a single body? Beat to death the sentient dog; smash the insentient incense table.
Gather it all up with full intent and bind it into a single bundle; cast it into the great ocean of the Eastern Sea. Yourself—
Yet, it is clear and unobstructed. Nevertheless, you must further know that there is a single aperture at the crown of the head before you can succeed.
[The Master] brandishes his staff and strikes the incense altar, saying: "A-la-la! A-la-la! Climbing the mountain, my knees ache; drinking tea, my tongue slips."
The Stone Daring at the crossroads; facing the moon and the wind, he blows the *chī-bā* flute. On this festival day, there is a small assembly:
the heart of the ancient Buddha is just as it is now. The bright moon shines upon the secluded valley; the cold waves assist the night-time mortar. Thus did the former masters reveal themselves.

It may be said that a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt awaits only a formidable adversary before its trigger is pulled; a ten-thousand-hu vessel does not set sail merely because of a small puddle.
If one is a guest upon the vast ocean or a general beyond the passes, one can turn the prow of the ship and trample the shooting target to pieces.
Within spontaneity, one acts before the occasion arises; how could one wait to observe the wind by means of the five-pronged weather-vane?
Thus it is said: "It is like the lion king’s roar; when the lion cubs hear it, their courage and vigor all increase. This is not unlike Dongshan’s question to Xingping:
"What is the mind of the ancient Buddha? Xingping replied, "Your own mind is it. Dongshan said, "Even though this is so..."
This is still where such-and-such a person has doubts. Píng said, "If that is so, then go ask the wooden man. O Great Assembly:

if you cannot see through or step upon this small matter, then even if your eloquence were like that of Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra and your wisdom like that of Śāriputra, you would still inevitably wander in madness outside the gate.
Tonight, precisely at the time when the mass of yin is exhausted and the single yang returns, I shall briefly [address] it with you.
After the assembly had gathered for a short while in conversation, [the Master] addressed them: "I venture to ask you all:

when Dongshan asked in this manner and Xingping answered in that way, was it a case of 'taking a mistake to correct a mistake' or 'borrowing a path to pass through'? Or was it a case of 'truly acting for one another,' where fists and kicks meet in mutual response?
To engage in such critical discussion is like leaving the city of Zhengzhou and heading straight for the gate of Cao. He continued, "As for Xingping’s final words, 'In this way...'"
He immediately asked the man who had taken the wood to leave. This single turn of phrase is exceedingly compassionate. How many people have misunderstood it here?
If one can clear away the narrowness of their chest and breathe freely at this point, what need is there to mention the nectar of clarified butter being poured over one’s head?
If this were not yet the case, one would not ride a golden horse through the humble lanes; returning, one would instead don a tattered robe.

Later, having retired from affairs to enter the Pine Rock, he sent a letter resigning from the monastery. Although the assembly earnestly entreated him, the Master firmly refused and would not consent.

In the summer of the seventh year of Hongwu, the ruler of Japan dispatched an envoy to present tribute and concurrently petitioned that the Master convert his country. The Emperor summoned the Master.

Upon arriving at the imperial palace, the Master declined on account of his old age and illness. The Emperor took pity on him and did not dismiss him. He subsequently resided at Cui Mountain in Yinzhou.
One day, he suddenly fell slightly ill; he asked for a brush and wrote this verse: "In seventy-eight years, there is no dharma to be spoken.
This final phrase—let the pillar speak! Ha! Having said this, he sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Liao Tang Yi of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture resided at Zhituo in Tai during the second year of the Zhizheng era. He subsequently moved to Tianning and then to Tiantong.
A monk asked, "In the past, when Baoshou opened the hall for the first time, Sansheng threw his body across the path to assist him;
when Linji took up residence at the monastery, Puhua exerted all his strength to support him. Ultimately, what matter did they clarify? The Master said, "Both ends..."

“Severing in a sitting, a single sword leans against the cold heavens. The monk said, “If that is so, then the five ranks of ruler and subject are all torn asunder, and the weapons and armor of the three mysteries are withdrawn at once.
The Master said, “You have wrongly applied names and phrases. The monk gave a shout. The Master said, “Confused Chan followers are as numerous as hemp and millet.
He ascended the hall and said, “Take a blade of grass and make it the sixteen-foot golden body; take the sixteen-foot golden body...”
"Make it into a single blade of grass. Good assembly, those who have not undergone bitter toil do not understand. He then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"If you can grasp directly the first word and the final pivot, then the lanterns and the pillars will shake the earth as they radiate light.
If this is not yet so, today Zhushan has lost ground. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The songs of woodcutters come from the layered peaks; the shadows of sails fall upon the marshes."

On the Continent: A monkey wearing a paper hat climbs straight to the tip of the tree branch. The seven-star sword; the five-cloud pavilion. The ball strikes the person, and the person strikes the ball.
In all matters, nothing can be grasped or toyed with. A fish swallows a bubble on the surface of the water. Residing at Tiantong, I ascend the hall:
The long-beaked bird does not perch in fragrant trees; Mokejia does not enter the vast ocean. Longquan is made of the same iron as the axe and hatchet.
The difference between the sharp and the dull is as vast as the distance between heaven and earth. A fine steed and a common donkey may share the same path, yet they differ in their speed.

[The Master] drew a line with his whisk and said: "The flowers must bloom tonight; do not wait for the morning breeze to blow. Small Assembly: The numinous light is never obscured, its sublime influence enduring through all ages;

the mirror of wisdom is brilliantly clear, responding universally throughout the ten directions. Now that the year draws to a close and the season of the "cloud-writing" (the winter solstice) has arrived, [he] struck the gong.
The Dharma drum sounds and the great assembly gathers like clouds. Each is authentically true; each is luminously wondrous. What more remains to be said?
If one speaks of the existence of dharmas, one is again hindered by existence. If one speaks of the non-existence of dharmas, one is again hindered by non-existence.
If one speaks of neither existence nor non-existence, one is again hindered by neither existence nor non-existence. If one speaks of neither non-existence nor non-non-existence, yet again...
Enveloped by neither existence nor non-existence, and unimpeded by neither being nor non-being. "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. "When the Sage arises, all things behold him.
The sun may grow cold; the moon may grow hot. No demons can destroy the True Teaching. With his whisk, he drew a single line and said:
"On the head of the Huangbo tree hangs a honeyed fruit; the silent youth sings a folk song. He asked: "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra..."
Xian said, "The myriad dharmas all share the same source. What is this dharma that shares the same source? The Master said, "Hu Zhangsan and He Liisi.
Xian said, "A single hair swallows the vast ocean; what more can be said therein? The Master said, "There is no need to hang up the stone mirror; when day breaks, the rooster crows of itself.
Xian said, "In a place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still a phrase? The Master said, "I truly know you."

The assembly was in confusion. [A monk] asked for the names of the provisional dharmas and provisional persons, and for the emptiness of dharmas and the emptiness of persons, requesting the Master to point directly at them.
The Master said, "How many people have you questioned so far? [The monk] said, "Where does one plant the rootless tree? The Master said, "It is still bearable before midnight;
after midday, it brings more sorrow to people. [The monk] said, "It is right here before our eyes; why do we not see it again and again? The Master said, "For a thousand years..."
The Chan Master Nantang Qingyu of Benjue Monastery in Jiaxing Prefecture,
a successor of Chan Master Baoning Moshan, was a native of the Zhu family from Linhai in Taizhou. He lived during the Yuan Dynasty.
In the second year [of his abbacy], he ascended the hall at Kaifu Monastery in Shoujing. Holding up his staff, he said:
"Those who come in this way—are they not like a variegated phoenix dancing in the crimson heavens? Those who come in that way—are they not like an iron snake blocking the ancient road?

Even if one goes or comes neither in this way nor that way, such that the path is cut off, it is still 'a plummet dipped in vinegar. He struck the ground with his staff. Ascending the hall, he said: "The *maṇi* jewel..."

"I do not know it," [he said]. "It was personally obtained within the Tathāgatagarbha; amidst the manifestation of the myriad phenomena in their dense array, there is a single orb of light whose color is neither color nor non-color.
Yongjia was much like a beggar who suddenly becomes wealthy. Kaifu said: "Who does not recognize the maṇi jewel?"
Shattered to pieces, it is not worth a single coin. Thrown into the void, it goes even further beyond. This is to spare people of this age from harboring it in their breasts.

Thus, when the clouds part and the sun rises, one’s own function reaches its full majesty. Upon encountering a practitioner of true substance, it is just like a person from Sizhou meeting the Great Sage.
In the first year of the Yuantong era, while residing at Benjue, he ascended the hall and looked at the assembly, saying: "This..."
"Is there anyone here who is a master warrior? At that time, a monk stepped forward from the assembly and said, "The entire earth is this question;
how would you, Reverend, answer it? The Master said, "All of empty space is this answer; how do you understand it? The monk said, "Ten thousand blessings!
The Master said, "The staff is not here; I will give you thirty blows with the broom handle. The monk said, "In all quarters..."
There was a man of clear vision present. The Master said, "Are you perhaps afflicted by blindness? The monk remained silent.
The Master shouted, "I took you for one with the talent to capture Yan and break Zhao; it turns out you are not even fit to be a minor soldier on the battlefield! Get out!
He then said, "If we speak of battle, everyone has their strength in the turning point. To reach this state, one must be a person of superior capacity who penetrates all quarters."

A true descendant of the noble lineage: not a single inch of blade is deployed, yet he completely overcomes his opponent with his full edge. If this were not so, even before a thought could arise, his skull would be shattered to pieces.

(He strikes the meditation staff and gives a shout, then descends from the seat. Small Lecture on the Winter Solstice while aboard a boat: A single path of empty luminosity is entirely one's own field.
Since the first line has already manifested its omen, the heaven and earth beyond the kalpas are fully revealed. There is no...
There is no distinction between coming and going, motion and stillness; there is no difference between grasping and abandoning, right and wrong.

One may ride upon sound and cover over form; one may follow the current and flow with the stream. One may drift in a single-leaf boat upon the waters of Huating; one may exhaust the splendors of the misty waves of the marshlands.
Without raising the fishing line of Ren Gong, yet not the same as the excursion by the Hao River. Striking the whisk, he said: "Split!"
Once the mouth has been hooked, it is already wounded by the salt and vinegar. At three inches from the hook, stop turning your head back. [He] pats his knee and says:

"The moon shines brightly through the eternal night; the waters reflect the sky. The cry of wild geese flies past the white duckweed isles. He asks: "The bitter cold of mid-winter is an annual occurrence."
"How is it as the movement of the sun's shadow shifts? The Master said, "Last night the sun’s disk drifted with osmanthus blossoms; this morning in the moon’s cavern, *zhicao* fungi have grown.

[The student] asked, "The direct transmission and pointing directly has already involved the realm of 'leaving' and 'subtlety. Having cut off all manifold differences, I request the Master to provide an answer."
The Master said, "A broken mirror does not reflect again; fallen flowers cannot climb back onto the branch. [The monk] asked, "If one departs in this very manner, what then?
The Master said, "A tortoise drilling through a ruined wall. [A monk] asked, "If preaching the Dharma does not accord with the capacity [of the listener], it is all untimely speech.
How can one preach so as to accord with the capacity? The Master said, "Rising at midnight, one loses the ox; rising at dawn, one loses the..."
"Huìhuǒ asked, 'The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. Is there anything else that is truly so?
The Master said, 'Eating food stops hunger; drinking water quenches thirst. Huìhuǒ said, 'Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it.
But what then? The Master said, 'Block your ears and listen clearly. He passed away in the eighth month of the Gui-mao year.

Chan Master Shíān Mào of Rìyún Qīngliáng Monastery in Míngzhōu was the son of the Zhèng family of Fènghuà in the commandery. While still a youth, he would sit in meditation during the middle of the night;
his mother detested this and would push him down, yet he would invariably remain awake until dawn. Later, he left the household life and went to study under Chan Master Nánjiàn Quán.
One night, beneath the moonlight on a pine tree, he attained realization upon hearing the sound of flowing water. He went to inform Quán of his insight, and Quán...
He was sent to Gulin. Gulin asked, "What have you come here for? The Master replied, "Precisely because the matter of birth and death is great, I have come to seek liberation.
Gulin said, "You clearly know that the four elements and five aggregates are the root of birth and death; why then have you entered this leather bag?
As the Master hesitated, Gulin struck him with his monk's staff, and he attained sudden enlightenment. In the *Zheng* year *Renwu*, he took up residence there.
At Mount Ruiyun of Changming, there was a monk who, before his question and answer were finished, struck the ground with his hand and laughed.
The Master said, "Why must you bring out such stale merchandise? The monk let out a single sigh. The Master then gave a shout.

The monk attained realization and withdrew to live in seclusion at Dongtang, never again venturing beyond the mountains. Yuanming, the Master’s own nephew, invited him back to Cixuan at Tiantong. Not long after,
He manifested illness. When the assembly requested that he write a verse, the Master said, "Within this, I am vast and empty; what need is there for a verse?

He then sat upright, leaning against his couch, clenched his right hand into a fist, rested his forehead upon it, and passed away. He was posthumously titled Great Chan Master Foguang Puzhao (Buddha-Light Universal Illumination).
Chan Master Yuet-tang Yen of Mount Jing was a successor of Chan Master Hai of Lingyin.
A native of Mingzhou, he received ordination at Baolin Temple in Wuzhou and studied extensively under various masters, eventually becoming the primary heir of Dongyi Hai.
He first resided at Dongchan Temple in Kunshan and subsequently moved to Wumen.
To celebrate his ten-thousandfold longevity, he ascended Nanping Peak on Mount Hulin and subsequently climbed the Double Path (Shuangjing) to erect the great banner of the Dharma.

His fame spread throughout the capital, and both monastics and laypeople arrived like clouds, flowing toward him as water rushes into a ravine. The imperial court twice issued sealed edicts to protect the teachings and bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered dharma robe.
The Master presided over four major monasteries in succession; his recorded sayings comprise four volumes. Duke Song Lian of Jinhua [wrote] for him...

In the preface, it is stated that he guided and led others according to their capacities, bringing benefit to many. This is what is meant by employing skillful means to unravel the knots of habitual tendencies, using provisional言辞 (words) to exhaustively reach the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
Chan Master Daguizhengzhang of Mount Dou Peak in Jianning Prefecture was a native of Fucheng, Fuzhou. He received the tonsure under Juejing of Hunan.
He studied under Dongyu Hai, who instructed him to investigate the "Vzhou’s Dog" kōan. Although he practiced without interruption, he remained unaware of its ultimate point.
One day, upon hearing Dongyu’s verse on the story of Juzhi raising his finger, he attained sudden enlightenment. Thereupon, he ascended [the seat].
The Abbot presented what he had received. Haikū said, "What is this? The Master said, "It is a matter already perfected throughout past and present;
why must one involve discursive thought? Haikū said, "Since it does not involve discursive thought, why have you come?

The Master said, "I ask the Reverend to bear witness. Haikū said, "Witness to what? The Master then gave a shout. Haikū said, "Where did you see Zhaozhou? The Master said, "Wrong. Haikū [said], "... (The text ends here).
Xuefeng said, "What did you just say? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru leaps. Xuefeng said, "Where is Zhaozhou now? The Master said, "He is not here.
Xuefeng said, "Why is Zhaozhou’s nostril in my hands? The Master said, "Thank you, Preceptor, for your testimony.
Xuefeng said, "I grant you thirty blows; now give me back the verse on the word 'Not' (Wú). The Master offered this verse: Dog.
If you look for the Buddha-nature in your children, your eyes will wither. In a flash, turn yourself around: *Oṃ sili suru*. He then sealed this by stroking [the assembly] with his hand.

Later, he built a thatched hut on Mount Doufeng, where it gradually became a monastic center. Entering the hall, after a long silence, he said: "Though gold is precious, once it enters the eye, it becomes dust.
Then he descended from the seat. Entering the hall again, he said: "The jade palace is clear with frost; the emerald grove sheds its leaves. One.

Toward the total upholding [of the Dharma], the myriad functions have been stilled and pared down. This master loves to seek medicine for those who are not ill. Ascending the hall, he raised the story of the "Chezhou Cloth Robe.
The Master said: "In the third watch of last night, the rain soaked the void. Does the wildcat know? It climbs up and stands upon the treetop branch. Ascending the hall again:
"The beginning of the New Year brings forth blessings; all things flourish. To call this the Buddha of the New Year's head is to name it."
“Dharma! It blinds your eyes. I will not call it the Buddha-dharma of the New Year’s head; it would break my tongue. After all, what is it?
He then descended from his seat. His verse at the time of death said: “Birth is fundamentally not born; extinction likewise has no extinction.
Illusory transformations come and go—what use is there for discrimination? Venerable assembly, take heed: it does not reside in words. He then joined his palms and entered *parinirvāṇa*.
Chan Master Dàqiān Huìzhào, the Great Teacher of Yùwáng in Míngzhōu, was the son of the Má family of Yǒngjiā.

At the age of fifteen, he entered the monastic order and received full ordination at Ruìguāng Monastery. Thereafter, he set out on a pilgrimage to visit various masters; first he called upon Huìméi, and subsequently he visited Dōngyǔ.
Xuyun asked, "Rushing about from east to west, what do you intend to do? The Master replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects.
Xuyun said, "The heavens have no four walls and the earth extends beyond the eight frontiers; upon what ground will you set foot? The Master struck the table with his palms and withdrew.
Xuyun knew that he had attained some realization, so he summoned him back and interrogated him repeatedly. Pleased by his responses, Xuyun then retained him.
He served as an attendant. Subsequently, he attended Master Zang at Wanshou. When Xiyu moved to Jingci, he invited the Master to share the seat.

In the Wuchen year of the Tianli era, he took up residence at Mingqing in Leqing. Addressing the assembly, he said: "If you wish for the Buddha-dharma to manifest before you, do not harbor intellectual understanding.
To be bound by seated meditation or to scrutinize the teachings will inevitably result in obstacles. How much better it is to have nothing established and to move about with ease and freedom!"
Indeed, it was for this reason that Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout were both employed out of sheer necessity. In the year Yiwu of the Zhi Zheng era, he moved to Mount Putuo;
not long after, he was appointed to Yewang Monastery. He once offered three "critical barriers" (*san guan*) to instruct his students, saying:
"The fierce tiger in the mountains takes flesh as its life; why does it not eat its own cubs? Space has no front or back; by what cause does it have..."
Throughout the four directions—east, west, south, and north—he consumed milk and other sustenance equal to the waters of the four great oceans; his accumulated bones were like Mount Vipula.
Who were your original parents? After residing there for nine years, he retired to the bank of the Miaoxi Spring (Spring of Wondrous Joy), where he built a dwelling called Meng’an (Dream Hermitage).
He remained in solitary confinement within his closed quarters; though layers of dust accumulated upon his seat, he paid them no heed.

On the first day of the tenth month in the sixth year of the Hongwu era, he summoned his disciples and said, "I am about to return to the West. You who are outside may return at once. Seven days later, having bathed and changed his robes, he entered nirvana with a serene countenance.
Chan Master Wuguang of Yuyang Xuechuang, whose courtesy name was Gongsu, was a native of Xindu in Chengdu. His surname was Yang.
He first preached the Dharma at Baima Temple, then moved to Kaiyuan, and subsequently ascended to the abbacy of Yuyang.

When Tiantong’s seat became vacant, the Emperor ordered the Master to concurrently hold both positions. He compiled the *Record of the Four Assemblies*, for which Song Gong Lian wrote a preface, stating: "The words of the four assemblies..."
He stood firm and immovable like a true victory banner; he traversed perilous terrain and crossed over dangers like a great Dharma vessel.
As for his practice of employing the "three words" to test those who came to study under him, it was as if standing with hands cast off at the edge of a precipice ten thousand fathoms high.
The Duke of Wenyu, Yu, remarked that he was a "phoenix feather or unicorn horn" from the lineage of Fuguo; these words are indeed not false.
The laywoman Sankong was among the most virtuous of the female disciples of Chan Master Tantan of Tianning. Possessing the resolve of a heroic man, she remained untainted by the worldly dust.
She studied under Zhuyun, single-mindedly upholding the "Mu" (No) koan for thirty-six years. One day, she suddenly asked:
"When birth and death arrive, what then? Yun said, "Who is it that is born? Who is it that dies? The layman bowed his head in greeting.
Yun, suspecting this was unusual, pressed him further, saying, "Who is it that is born? Who is it that dies? The layman again bowed his head in greeting.
Yun said, "Be careful not to die right here. The layman picked up his prayer beads and counted them.
He [held] one hundred and eight prayer beads. Before long, he manifested a slight illness, spoke a verse, and passed away. After the cremation, a great many *śarīra* relics were obtained.
Chan Master Tánfāng Zhōng of Lóngxiáng in Jīnlíng was a successor of Chan Master Yùshān Zhēn; he was a native of Nánkāng and once succeeded Master Duān in presiding over Jìngsōng Monastery.

He moved from Mount Shan to Jiangshan, and later ascended to Longxiang. One night, the temple was destroyed by fire. The next day, the Prince of Liang visited the temple and asked, "How will you restore it?
The Master replied, "We rely on the presence of a great donor. The Prince said, "Since the temple has been burnt down, upon what does the Buddha reside?

The Master replied, "The Buddhas of antiquity have passed away, but the Buddhas of the present have returned. The Prince remarked, "What the monks call 'Jiangbo' (the thinness of Jiang) is indeed so."
